British Columbia has declared a state of emergency as a rapidly spreading wildfire devastates communities, forcing over 20,000 residents to evacuate their homes along Okanagan Lake in western Canada.

Premier David Eby announced the emergency Saturday, with over 100 wildfires currently raging across the province. Nearly half of these blazes are out of control, fueled by hot, windy conditions and a prolonged drought.

The entire community of Summerland, home to approximately 12,000 people, received overnight evacuation orders, alongside 8,000 individuals in and around nearby Peachland. Officials have yet to determine how many homes were destroyed.

Eby confirmed some residents became trapped and required rescue, while search-and-rescue teams continue to comb areas behind fire lines for any others who may have been caught.

Nearly half of these blazes are out of control, fueled by hot, windy conditions and a prolonged drought ( Gary Nylander/The Canadian Press via AP )

“I know many families are facing an unimaginable day today,” Eby said. “People have lost their homes. And many people have been displaced. Others are waiting for news about loved ones.”

Cliff Chapman, director of wildfire operations for the BC Wildfire Service, said firefighting helicopters were diverted to rescue people who could no longer escape by road. He said the outcome would have been significantly worse without cooperation among agencies responding to the fire.

The Bald Range wildfire was first reported on Friday evening but grew to about 50 square kilometers (19 square miles) within hours, overwhelming the smaller community of Faulder and covering the roughly 15 kilometers (9 miles) to Summerland at extraordinary speed.

Chapman described fire conditions across British Columbia as “explosive” and warned that other communities could face fires similar to the one that forced the evacuation of Summerland.

British Columbia Emergency Management Minister Kelly Greene said the state of emergency gives the province additional powers, including the ability to restrict travel and secure accommodations for evacuees that might otherwise be unavailable.

Erick Thompson, an emergency official with the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen, called it one of the “quickest-moving, fastest-growing” wildfires the region had experienced.

Thompson eventually had to abandon the emergency operations center and evacuate his own family.

“I had to leave the EOC to come and get my family to leave this area. We’re heading south,” he said in a video posted early Saturday from his vehicle as traffic backed up around him.

Videos posted on social media appeared to show multiple homes burning as residents fled along roads with flames on both sides.

Homeowner Kerry Gold and her husband, Mike Elsinga, fled around 12:30 a.m. after watching flames spread beyond nearby mountains.

“It’s scary. It’s moving fast,” Gold said.

The couple, who recently moved from the city of Vancouver, had packed bags, prepared a carrier for their cat and planned to help a disabled friend evacuate.

“You want to stay here and protect your home, but you also don’t want to get caught in it,” Elsinga said.

Canada has endured increasingly destructive wildfire seasons in recent years, forcing mass evacuations and repeatedly sending smoke across large parts of Canada and the United States.

He didn’t score many points in his brief stint in the pros — but an ex-NBA player running for Congress appears to be going to great lengths to make one.

Former NBA bust and current Republican Senate candidate Royce White has announced plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft, claiming he now identifies as transgender — for athletic purposes, anyway.

“I’m transgender. I’m a woman. I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball, professional basketball, so I’ll be declaring for the WNBA draft in 2027 as well,” White, 35, told Fox News Saturday.

White’s announcement comes one day after former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom, who is a man, said he also plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. Freedom’s statement followed comments from WNBA player Sophie Cunningham about transgender athletes that renewed a heated debate on the league’s policies for transgender players. It also comes as President Donald Trump has made barring transgender women from from competing in women’s sports.

White, a 6’8” forward who played just three games in the NBA, all in 2014, continued Saturday, “I think I’d be unstoppable. But I’m a team-first guy. I’m a pass-first kind of player. I do the little things. I led my team in all five major stat categories at Iowa State University, so I do a little bit of everything. I’ll do whatever the coach needs me to do. I’ll do whatever the girls need me to do.”

open image in gallery Former NBA player and U.S. Senate candidate Royce White announced Saturday that he plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft amid controversy over the league’s transgender eligibility policies ( AP )

“I think it’s only fair,” he added.

Freedom said he reviewed the WNBA’s eligibility rules before announcing his plans to enter the league and believes he meets the requirements to play.

The WNBA’s 2026 collective bargaining agreement states in Article XIII that “only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA.” However, the 409-page agreement does not define what qualifies as a “woman” for eligibility purposes.

Following Freedom’s announcement, the Women’s National Basketball Players Association said in a statement: “We embrace justice equity, diversity, and inclusion. Those are the values that unite this Union and allow it to protect women’s sports while creating transformational change.”

“Hate, abuse, and demonization of any person or group of people, including transgender people, only fuel fear, division, and harm. We will continue to have hard conversations,” the group added in the Instagram post. “But we will not be used as political pawns.”

White said Saturday that the WNBA could end the controversy by clearly stating its policy on whether males are eligible to compete in women’s sports.

“I think the WNBA could come out and make a definitive statement about guys with a pair of balls playing in the Women’s Association,” he said, adding he will continue moving forward in his draft bid unless the league addresses the controversial issue.

In a memo obtained by the Associated Press, WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert told teams that a discussion about the inclusion of trans athletes “will continue to receive significant attention.”

“I wanted to reach out to share how we are approaching these conversations at the league office and to thank those of you who have responded to questions from the media with thoughtfulness and professionalism,” she wrote Friday.

“We recognize that this is a complex and nuanced topic, and we will continue to have important conversations with all of you and the Players Association in the weeks and months ahead,” Engelbert continued. “We also plan to convene additional discussions and offer listening sessions for any team leaders who would like to participate. Your perspectives and feedback are invaluable, and I appreciate those who have already reached out to share their thoughts.”

open image in gallery Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was the first to declare for the 2027 WNBA Draft on Friday ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery The WNBA’s transgender athlete debate intensified in July after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham criticized trans participation in women’s sports ( Getty )

White further claimed he could take legal action if he is not drafted or signed by a WNBA team.

“I have to file a discrimination lawsuit, right? I mean, that’s, that’s ridiculous,” he told Fox News. “We’re gonna have to have a huge legal battle about discrimination if I can’t play.”

White was selected 16th overall by the Houston Rockets in the 2012 NBA Draft out of Iowa State but never played for the team because of severe anxiety and a fear of flying.

Nowadays, he is running in Minnesota’s August 11 Republican primary for U.S. Senate. White previously ran as the Republican nominee against Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar in 2024 but lost the general election.

The debate over transgender athletes in the WNBA intensified last month after Cunningham, a guard for the Indiana Fever, criticized trans participation in women’s sports.

“I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men,” Cunningham told ESPN, later doubling down on her comments, claiming they were “common sense.”

The Independent has contacted the WNBA and WNBPA for comment.

Fifa has hit out at what it described as attempts to “undermine” its embattled president, Gianni Infantino.

Infantino has faced calls to resign from his role in the aftermath of a saga that saw him abandon a proposed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions.

That proposal brought the threat of a boycott from Uefa, European football’s governing body, with England’s Football Association (FA) among those to officially withdraw their support for the Fifa president.

Infantino is due to seek re-election in March of next year. He has received backing from South American body Conmebol and the Confederation of African Football (Caf).

open image in gallery Fifa president Gianni Infantino is under pressure ( AP )

Infantino succeeded Sepp Blatter as president of Fifa in February 2016 having previously served as Uefa’s general secretary for seven years.

Infantino has strongly denied a claim made by The Telegraph that Uefa paid off his alleged lover with a six-figure sum during his time working at European football’s governing body, and has now been given fresh backing by Fifa.

“Echoing the recent statements of Conmebol and Caf, as well as discussions with Fifa Member Associations and Confederations from around the world, Fifa will not support, facilitate or tolerate any process concerning the election of the Fifa President that is inconsistent with Fifa’s Statutes, democratic procedures and established governance framework,” a Fifa spokesperson said. “The Fifa President was democratically elected by Fifa’s Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate.

open image in gallery Fifa’s management board backed Infantino at a meeting in Morocco on Wednesday (Sam Corum/PA) ( PA Wire )

“It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its President. Those who do not have the support of FIFA’s Member Associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes.

“Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning Fifa and its President. Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.

“The Fifa President has dedicated more than 30 years of his professional life to European and world football, contributing to significant change in the game and, in particular, to broadening access, resources and opportunity across world football. Change inevitably challenges established interests, but disagreement with that change cannot justify efforts to undermine the democratic mandate of Fifa’s President or the institution he was elected to lead.

“Fifa welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, Fifa will challenge it directly and vigorously.

“Fifa’s responsibility is to its 211 Member Associations and to football around the world. We will not be distracted or diverted from strengthening the organisation, delivering for our Member Associations and continuing the work of making football truly global. Through the FIfa President and the Fifa administration, our focus remains firmly on that mission, and we are more determined than ever to fulfil it.”

Uefa has said that its threat to boycott remains in place despite the abandonment of the sell-off plans.

Fifa’s management board backed Infantino at a meeting in Morocco on Wednesday.

Common painkillers including ibuprofen could increase the chance of getting sunburn, Britain’s health watchdog has warned as the country braces for its fifth blistering heatwave of the summer.

The public is urged to take extra precautions if taking the medicine in warmer weather, with temperatures set to soar to 36C next week.

The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) said on Friday that drugs like ibuprofen and naproxen could increase sensitivity to the sun, making burns more likely.

Other treatments that can increase sensitivity include antibiotics like doxycycline and tetracycline, acne treatments like isotretinoin and topical retinoids, and antifungal medicines such as voriconazole.

open image in gallery A person drinks from a bottle while sat on sun-scorched grass at Victoria Tower Gardens ( AFP/Getty )

Dr Alison Cave, chief safety officer at the MHRA, said: “Some commonly used medicines can affect the body’s ability to stay hydrated, regulate temperature, or protect itself from sun exposure.

“Simple precautions can make a significant difference. Staying hydrated, avoiding the strongest sun during the middle of the day, and using protective clothing and sunscreen can all help reduce risk.”

She noted diuretics, often prescribed for blood pressure or heart conditions, can increase fluid loss and make dehydration more likely.

Meanwhile, some antidepressants and antipsychotics can affect the body’s ability to regulate temperature, and medicines like beta blockers may reduce the body’s response to heat stress.

The body uses several mechanisms to regulate temperature: sweating, blood flow to the skin and fluid balance. But some commonly prescribed drugs interfere with these processes, making it harder to stay cool.

Older adults, people with chronic conditions – especially those with heart or lung disease – and those taking multiple prescription drugs are especially vulnerable to heat-related illnesses.

open image in gallery The public is urged to take extra precautions if taking the medicine in warmer weather ( PA )

Last month, doctors warned people on certain mental health medications to take extra precautions ahead of another heatwave.

Dr Nick Broughton, NHS England’s national director for mental health, learning disabilities and autism, said that people taking antipsychotic medication and antidepressants need to be extra cautious during hot weather because some of these medicines can make it harder to keep the body cool.

“Most importantly, they should not stop taking their medication suddenly and can speak to their GP, pharmacist or mental health team for advice if they need to,” he said.

New yellow health heat alerts came into force this week as the UK prepares to face its fifth heatwave of the summer.

The alerts run until 9pm on Tuesday across all of England, except the North East and North West.

They warn that the hot weather is likely to affect the wellbeing of the population, particularly those who are vulnerable or have health conditions.

Luxury car manufacturer Mercedes AMG is facing a class-action lawsuit from two drivers who allege the prominent AMG logo on their vehicle's driver's seat becomes so hot it causes burns and literally brands them.

Gabriel Lahijani and Karendeep "Karina" Bath are the plaintiffs in the suit, filed earlier this week in the U.S. District Court of California’s Western Division.

They claim the front seats of certain Mercedes AMG cars contain a design flaw where the raised metallic AMG logo is "reasonably expected to contact an occupant’s upper back, neck, or shoulder."

The plaintiffs are seeking compensation from Mercedes for medical expenses, as well as for any pain, suffering, and emotional distress they can prove at trial. They also demand that Mercedes cover the cost for other owners to have the problematic logo removed from their vehicles.

open image in gallery The plaintiffs demand that Mercedes cover the cost for other owners to have the problematic logo removed from their vehicles. ( Mercedes-AMG )

Mercedes-Benz couldn’t be reached immediately for comment.

Lahigani, a Los Angeles resident, had leased a new 2026 Mercedes-AMG E-Class vehicle from an authorized Mercedes-Benz dealership in Los Angeles, according to the suit. He reported receiving second-degree burns on his back on May 31, after entering his vehicle wearing a tank top. A board-certified dermatologist subsequently documented first- and second-degree burns, describing the injury as “AMG inscribed."

Roughly six weeks later, Bath, a Chatsworth, California resident, received similar burns allegedly from the logo design while wearing a sleeveless top. After parking her Mercedes-AMG vehicle in Los Angeles, Bath returned to the vehicle and entered the driver’s seat, the suit said. Her shoulder immediately touched the logo, causing a burning sensation. In the following days, a mark in the shape of the AMG logo “darkened and became visible on her skin, consistent with a thermal contact burn," the lawsuit said.

In December, Mercedes-Benz USA and parent company Daimer AG agreed to pay $149.6 million to settle allegations that the automaker secretly installed devices in hundreds of thousands of vehicles to pass emission tests, according to an announcement by a coalition of attorneys general.

According to the coalition, between 2008 and 2016 the German automaker equipped more than 211,000 diesel passenger cars and vans with software devices that optimized emission controls during tests but reduced the controls during normal operations.

Jeepers creepers!

A New Jersey couple got a terrifying backyard surprise when they discovered an 8-foot Burmese python slithered beneath their shed — and its latest meal made the massive snake even harder to remove.

Leslie Daley was watering flowers at the family’s Freehold home when she spotted the enormous snake moving through the backyard, her husband, Ed, told ABC 7.

The Daleys then spotted a hole in the corner of the shed, where they believe the python crawled inside. They called the Monmouth County SPCA, setting off an unusual rescue operation.

“When the homeowner sent us a video of what we were actually dealing with, and when we all saw it, our jaws kind of dropped a little because that is a Burmese python, which definitely does not belong out in the wild in New Jersey,” Scott Crawford, an Animal Control Manager with the Monmouth County SPCA, told the news outlet.

open image in gallery A New Jersey couple found an 8-foot, 40-pound Burmese python under their shed, and its full belly made the massive snake even harder to remove ( Monmouth County SPCA )

open image in gallery A contractor had to come remove the shed's floorboards for rescuers to safely remove the animal ( Monmouth County SPCA )

It’s not illegal to own a Burmese python in New Jersey, but the animals do require a permit. Officials suspect the snake may have been released by someone who didn’t have one, or by an owner who simply couldn’t handle the snake after it grew too large.

Animal control officers arrived expecting to pull the snake back through the opening it used to crawl under the shed.

But there was a problem: the python recently ate a substantial meal, leaving it with a large and full belly.

With the python’s bulging abdomen blocking the way, rescuers couldn’t simply pull it out without risking injury.

The Daleys called in a contractor friend, who tore up the shed floor to give rescuers access from above.

But even with the floorboards gone, the python’s latest feast was still standing in the way.

“So we had to dig around him a little bit to free him up,” Crawford said. “Still couldn't tell exactly where his head was.”

open image in gallery X-rays revealed that the snake recently ate an opossum for dinner ( Monmouth County SPCA )

Eventually, the team managed to get the massive reptile out from beneath the shed. The Monmouth County SPCA’s medical staff performed X-rays on the snake to determine what was inside its stomach and make sure its recent meal had not caused any complications.

The images revealed the answer: an opossum.

Fortunately for the family, the python did not eat someone’s pet, which Crawford said could’ve been a real possibility for a snake that size.

The snake will eventually be placed in a zoo or transferred to a private owner with the proper expertise and permits to care for it.

“I’m not a big snake person myself,” Ed Daley told ABC 7.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to a 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head intothe break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto. Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.content:

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

Sports.title: South Korea FA forced to apologise over 'sexual services' provided to referees
Sports.content:
South Korea FA forced to apologise over 'sexual services' provided to referees

The South Korean FA are being enveloped by controversy following reports of referees being provided with 'sexual services' and a probe into the appointment of former coach Hong Myung-bo

View 2 Images South Korea's Football Association has apologised (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

The Korean Football Association has released an apology after allegations emerged that it provided 'sexual services' to foreign referees. The governing body responded to the controversy on Saturday after it was revealed in a government audit, as police investigate the KFA in a separate probe.

‌



The KFA are reported to have used corporate cards to pay for 'sexual entertainment' for visiting referees during seven international fixtures in 2011 and 2012. A 2016 Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism report was uncovered by JTBC that showed 10 foreign officials were involved, with trips to massage parlours where fees covered the costs of sexual services, according to the report.

‌



Two to four referees were provided with entertainment in six of the seven matches, while a single official was in the remaining game. Incidents are said to have been recorded in Seoul's Gangnam district as well as Ulsan and Changwon in Gyeongnam, per International Business Times.

‌



The matches included Olympic qualifiers against Qatar and Oman, and a World Cup qualifier against Kuwait. Friendly matches against Honduras, China's Olympic side, Poland and an A-team match against Serbia were also revealed.

The officials were reportedly from Japan, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Uzbekistan. The KFA offered their apologies in a statement and declared that such activity was not currently taking place.

Violent brawl breaks out between fans in EFL Cup clash as police rush to intervene READ MORE :

"We deeply apologise for causing concern over various issues ⁠involving the association, which emerged from a parliamentary hearing and an unprecedented search and seizure, and from reports about events from more than a decade ago, that even many within the organisation were unaware of," it read.

‌



"The association makes clear that inappropriate conduct of this kind, or the use of corporate cards for such purposes, is absolutely not currently taking place,' the KFA said in its statement," they added.

A parliamentary hearing was held last month to question former KFA president Chung Mong-gyu and Hong Myung-bo, who quit as Korea's head coach following the side's World Cup exit. Seoul police raided the KFA's offices on Thursday as part of an investigation ⁠linked to the latter's appointment.

View 2 Images Police raided South Korea's football association on August 6, as part of an investigation into the appointment of the coach in charge during their dismal World Cup campaign. (Image: Photo by GREG BAKER / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Hong was appointed as South Korea's coach in 2024, having previously led the team from 2013 to 2014. There was a great deal of scrutiny over the decision after the KFA dropped their search involving foreign candidates to select Hong following a brief meeting.

South Korea failed to get out of the group during the World Cup in Mexico, Canada and the United States, and Hong resigned from his post. That result saw scrutiny over his appointment intensify. Death threats saw extreme security measures required upon his return from the tournament.

‌



South Korean President Lee Jae-myung provided a damning assessment on social media. He wrote: "I ‌am not just taken aback by this unexpected outcome, I am utterly baffled.

"Once again, it has been proven that personnel decisions are everything. When loyalty and factionalism are valued over competence, and an incapable person is appointed as a leader, the outcome is as predictable as fire."

Sports.title: FIFA urged to change rule after 'criminal tackle' leaves star with shattered knee in pre-season
Sports.content:
FIFA urged to change rule after 'criminal tackle' leaves star with shattered knee in pre-season

Football clubs across Europe are in the middle of their pre-season preparations, and will be eager to keep their players fit and fresh for the new campaign

View Image Christantus Uche will miss the season through injury (Image: Getafe CF / X)

FIFA have been urged to change the rules surrounding red cards after a 'criminal tackle' which cut short Christantus Uche's season before it had even begun. Monaco ran out 1-0 winners of Getafe in a pre-season fixture at the Stade Louis-II on Thursday, Paris Brunner making the difference from the penalty spot in the second-half.

‌



However, what was meant to be a friendly quickly turned cynical for one pair of players, with Getafe's Uche left with a devastating knee injury following a late challenge from Christian Mawissa. Uche was left in a heap and in need of treatment when the Monaco defender caught him late with a lunging challenge.

‌



Uche's knee looked to be hyperextended as Mawissa caught him studs up on the shin, before flipping over onto his back, writhing in pain. Medical assistants were quickly called onto the pitch to give Uche treatment, as Mawissa was shown a straight red card.

‌



Violent brawl breaks out between fans in EFL Cup clash as police rush to intervene READ MORE :

Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

Uche was ultimately taken off the pitch, unable to continue, with Getafe confirming the worst shortly afterward. While initial examinations pointed toward a contusion on Uche's kneecap, further tests revealed that not only was the 23-year-old forward's knee dislocated, but also in need of surgery after sustaining a number of torn ligaments.

It means that Uche is expected to miss the entirety of the upcoming La Liga season with Getafe, who will now have to scour the market to search for a late replacement. While Mawissa was rightly sent off for the challenge, a number of social media users were quick to call on FIFA to make changes to their rules surrounding red cards.

One wrote: "According to various newspapers, Uche will miss the entire season with Getafe due to this criminal tackle by Mawissa (Monaco) in a friendly match. His knee is shattered. Mawissa shouldn't play until Uche has recovered."

‌



A second, meanwhile, added: "It should be a FIFA rule. Whoever injures another player with a reckless or excessively forceful tackle shall be suspended from all competitions until the injured player returns to play, and during that time, they will earn the minimum salary of their league. THIS is how these absurd tackles would end."

Meanwhile, a fifth explained: "When are they going to drop this proportionality between the challenge, the injury, and the sanction, but with the latter on a one-to-one basis, sanctioned and sidelined from playing until the injured player returns? We never want to see this kind of thing happen on the pitch. I wish him a speedy recovery and hope he can return as soon as possible."

Sports.title: Man Utd stars give Michael Carrick food for thought in PSG draw as transfer dilemma grows
Sports.content:
Man Utd stars give Michael Carrick food for thought in PSG draw as transfer dilemma grows

PSG 1-1 MANCHESTER UNITED: Bryan Mbuemo's first-half strike ensured the Premier League side held their own against the champions of Europe

View 3 Images Bryan Mbuemo impressed as Man Utd fought back against PSG

Talk of Marcus Rashford's possible return to the Manchester United fold has dominated the summer, but some of his team-mates showed that he's a way to go before he can start thinking of playing in red once more.

‌



Rashford is back at Old Trafford following the end of his Barcelona loan and, with Ruben Amorim now gone, Michael Carrick could offer him fresh hope. Two of the immediate problems to Rashford's starting XI ambitions are Bryan Mbeumo and Amad.

‌



Mbeumo was on target in their draw with PSG and was a constant menace for the Red Devils. On one of the flanks was Amad, who dovetailed impressively with the Cameroonian.

‌



United responded well to an early onslaught, that saw PSG teenager Ibrahim Mbaye open the scoring inside two minutes at the back post. Mbeumo had the Premier League side level before half-time as he finished neatly after Amad had set him away.

Mason Mount forced off through injury as Man Utd suffer blow in PSG friendly READ MORE :

Ex-Man Utd title winner back in England looking for new club as a free agent READ MORE :

Patrick Dorgu was another element of the United attack. Signed by Amorim as a wing-back, the return to a more conventional formation may have left him wondering where his future lied in the team. Carrick is understood to prefer him in a more advanced role, giving Rashford yet more competition.

Dorgu also has the added luxury of having a body of work under Carrick, which the United boss will no doubt factor in to his selection decisions. Rashford was afforded an extended break having been involved with England at the World Cup, but that may well have him on the back foot.

‌



This was a United XI that left Bruno Fernandes on the bench initially, has Benjamin Sesko still recovering from injury and Matheus Cunha still to come back into the picture.

View 3 Images Amad began out wide and impressed with Patrick Dorgu and Shea Lacey also being used on the wings

Youngster Shea Lacey moved out to the left once Fernandes came on to occupy his usual role as the team's playmaker, meaning the teenager is another player Carrick wants to look at in one of the wide roles. This United depth is starting to look more and more impressive, even if Rashford's task is being made all the more challenging.

‌



The Englishman is still United's top earner and, if he is going to play a squad role, then the club may have to look at moving him on. His salary will make that a challenge, but the club can ill-afford to pay someone who pops off the bench more than £300,000-a-week.

This was a game that showed United, who still have questions to answer given the impact of the well renowned 'new manager bounce', can at least mix it in the pre-season environment with PSG.

The French champions were certainly showcasing their depth and sone of the next generation. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Willian Pacho were the only two men to start in the Champions League final that began from the off in Sweden.

‌



View 3 Images Shea Lacey is looking to stake his claim to become a regular

It means it was not the type of Parisian test that Arsenal faced when they tried to beat them to win the European Cup, but it was still a well coached side that began flexing their muscles on the hour mark. Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, Vitinha and Joao Neves all came on once the hour mark hit.

United sent on summer signing Youri Tielemans in the second-half and the Belgian quickly set about trying to conduct proceedings. He found Fernandes with a neat ball, but his effort in the final ten minutes went wide.

Article continues below

It was actually United who had the better of the final stages, but they were unable to find the winner that would've landed them a morale-boosting scalp, even if this was a PSG side not a full strength.

Sports.content:
Darwin Nunez has given thumbs up to Liverpool transfer as deal gets seal of approval

Former Liverpool striker Darwin Nunez has already shared his thoughts on Ronald Araujo, who is set to join the club from Barcelona

View 2 Images Darwin Nunez has previously discussed his Uruguay teammate Ronald Araujo (Image: Luis ROBAYO / AFP via Getty Images)

Former Liverpool star Darwin Nunez has already lauded Ronald Araujo's key traits as the defender edges closer to a move to Anfield. The Reds have pursued the Barcelona star to shore up their defensive concerns.

‌



Araujo is on the verge of completing a loan move from Barcelona to strengthen Liverpool's backline. Andoni Iraola's side need more options in defence, with skipper Virgil van Dijk currently the only senior centre-back available to the manager.

‌



Araujo predominantly operates as a central defender but can also fill in at right-back, addressing issues in two positions. The Liverpool ECHO has reported that the loan deal includes a buy option, with the defender due to undergo a medical on Sunday.

‌



The 27-year-old featured in Uruguay's World Cup squad this summer, although he remained on the sidelines due to a calf problem. Former Liverpool striker Nunez is a friend of Araujo's and has previously spoken glowingly of the defender's character off the pitch.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero faces furious backlash as Tottenham captain 'wants Arsenal transfer'
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero faces furious backlash as Tottenham captain 'wants Arsenal transfer'

Cristian Romero is expected to leave Tottenham this summer and whilst Arsenal are interested in the central defender their arch-rivals will not entertain the prospect of a move

View 2 Images Cristian Romero is tipped to leave Tottenham this summer (Image: Alex Pantling, Getty Images)

Cristian Romero is open to joining Arsenal this summer - but Tottenham are adamant their defender will not be crossing the north London divide.

‌



The Argentine wants to call time on his five year spell with Tottenham and there is interest from Atletico Madrid and Inter Milan, but the Gunners too are keen on the centre-half in a move which would spark a furious backlash from Spurs fans.

‌



Despite Romero's stance on the move, Tottenham bosses have made it clear that there is no scenario where they will allow their defender to move to the Emirates, claims The Sun.

‌



A transfer would see Romero emulate Sol Campbell's move from Tottenham to Arsenal in 2001, which remains one of the most controversial transfers in the history of the Premier League. Campbell was a leading light at White Hart Lane but chose to leave when his contract expired, which effectively left Tottenham powerless to prevent the move.

Bruno Guimaraes reveals private Declan Rice message after sealing Arsenal transfer READ MORE :

Four left-backs Man Utd can sign after Newcastle block Lewis Hall transfer move READ MORE :

However Romero still has a contract at Tottenham, which has three years left to run, and that puts his club in a strong position when it comes to his future. The 28-year-old's departure is expected but the north Londoners will not be letting him make the 4.5 mile trip to their rivals.

William Gallas was the last man to make the switch, that coming in 2010, but like Campbell his move came upon the expiry of his contract rather than the two clubs actually coming to the negotiation table.

‌



Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi has already signed Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton for £52million with the Dutchman effectively serving a Romero's replacement. Van Hecke is part of a summer spree that has seen the club spend over £200m on new talent, which includes Sandro Tonali.

View 2 Images Sol Campbell caused uproar when moving from Tottenham to Arsenal (Image: Jamie McDonald/ALLSPORT)

Atletico have a long-term interest in Romero and any move to the Spanish capital would allow him to work under Diego Simeone, who is known to be a huge fan of his fellow Argentina. He is thought to be readying a £40m bid for Romero.

‌



The La Liga side tried to sign Romero last summer, but former Tottenham boss Thomas Frank convinced the defender to sign a new deal and made him the club captain.

Romero was heavily criticised when it emerged that he was going to miss Tottenham's must win final game of last season. He headed back to Argentina to watch boyhood club Belgrano face River Plate in a title decider, but made a late u-turn and was present for the win over Everton.

Sports.title: PSG boss Luis Enrique exposed new Liverpool signing Ronald Araujo in brutal clip
Sports.content:
PSG boss Luis Enrique exposed new Liverpool signing Ronald Araujo in brutal clip

Ronald Araujo is set to join Liverpool on a season-long loan from Barcelona, where one of his lows came in a Champions League quarter-final loss against Luis Enrique's Paris Saint-Germain

View 2 Images Luis Enrique wasn't surprised by Ronald Araujo's error against Paris Saint-Germain in 2024 (Image: DAX Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique once described Ronald Araujo as Barcelona's biggest weakness in a brutal piece of analysis. A clip of Enrique's criticism has resurfaced after Liverpool agreed a deal to sign Araujo, 27, on a season-long loan.

‌



The deal includes an option to buy for €55million (£47m), with the Reds covering his wages in full. Liverpool supporters are keen to get the lowdown on their newest signing, who is set to have a medical on Sunday before linking up with his team-mates.

‌



But they won't be enamoured by listening to what Enrique told his players about Araujo in 2024, especially since PSG have knocked Liverpool out of Europe in each of the last two seasons. The PSG manager was preparing his side to face Barcelona in the second leg of their Champions League quarter-final, as they trailed 3-2 on aggregate after losing the home leg.

‌



Firstly, during a staff meeting which was later shown in a documentary about Enrique, he said: "Let Araujo come with the ball. When he comes with the ball, when he releases it, we pressure him."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jamie Carragher admits Liverpool transfer 'worry' and issues Man Utd warning READ MORE :

When it came time to address his squad, the Spaniard explained: "Let this gentleman (a magnet on a board) be Araujo, who is a high-level player, no doubt about it. But he is the player with the most problems. Every time the ball gets to Araujo - whether it's a support, a pass and so on - when the ball comes in motion, cover the passing line and go."

‌



Enrique's game plan looked to be out of the window when Raphinha gave Barcelona the lead on 12 minutes, extending their advantage. But then came the turning point, as Araujo played a misplaced pass after being pressed by Bradley Barcola exactly in the way Enrique had instructed him to.

Scampering back as Barcola raced away, Araujo clumsily fouled the French winger and got himself sent off, paving the way for PSG's comeback. Enrique's team ran out 4-1 winners on the night and progressed to the last four.

Will Ronald Araujo prove his doubters wrong? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The incident has haunted Araujo's career at Barcelona ever since, and he was also culpable for a crucial goal in their Champions League semi-final defeat to Inter Milan in 2025 when Hansi Flick's men were seconds away from going through. The Champions League has been a particular source of frustration for Araujo, who was also sent off against Chelsea last season.

That red card prompted him to take a mental health break which Barcelona granted him, telling Mundo Deportivo: "I'd been dealing with anxiety for a year and a half that turned into depression, and I was playing like that. That doesn't help, because on the field you don't really feel like yourself."

‌



Barcelona faced PSG in the Champions League again last season, and when Enrique's comments were put to Flick, he replied: "What happened in the past is no longer valid; now is different. I have full confidence in all my players. He's incredible and has proven it in recent games. I'm very happy with him."

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola was fouled by Ronald Araujo and it changed the tie (Image: Xavier Laine/Getty Images)

Araujo will hope that his move to Anfield serves as a fresh start. Blessed with pace, strong and boasting a towering 6ft 3in frame which makes him a threat in both boxes, Andoni Iraola likes what he sees from the Uruguay international, who didn't feature at the World Cup due to a calf injury.

Article continues below

His ability to play at right-back should also come in handy for Liverpool, who need cover in the position due to Conor Bradley's injury. Last month, centre-back Joe Gomez suffered an injury, making it a bigger priority to recruit a defender.

Sports.title: Wissa double gives Newcastle boss Jaissle winning start at 10-man Valencia
Sports.content:
Substitute Yoane Wissa scored twice to give Matthias Jaissle a winning start as Newcastle boss with a 2-1 comeback pre-season win at 10-man Valencia.

But the friendly at the Mestalla threatened to be overshadowed by Jose Gaya's red-card horror tackle on Anthony Elanga, which saw the Newcastle winger stretchered off in the first half and led to both sets of players clashing.

Fortunately for the Sweden international, his injury does not appear to be serious, with Elanga later up and walking after a contusion to the shin.



Image: Tempers flared after Jose Gaya's challenge saw Anthony Elanga stretchered off

Speaking at his post-match press conference, Jaissle was "relaxed" over Elanga's injury.

The German said: "It seems to be not bad, so we are pleased. I hope it's true, then he can start again next week."

He added: "Of course I was in fear [it was a serious injury], definitely, but now I'm more relaxed as the medical department is showing almost green lights, and there's nothing serious."

Who played for Newcastle? Hornicek; Shahar (M Miley 46), Thiaw (Johnson 72), Botman, Pivas (Charlton 67); Bamba (Steur 46), Ramsey (Joelinton 67); Elanga (J Murphy 39), Woltemade (Willock 67), Barnes (Toure 46); Osula (Wissa 46).

Unused subs: Gillespie, Harris, Finneran, Neave.

Elanga's injury after Valencia's Filip Ugrinic's stunning fifth-minute opener had given Jaissle a nightmare start to life in the Newcastle dugout.

But his half-time changes sparked a Toon turnaround with new signings Bazoumana Toure and Sean Steur impressing.

It was last summer's signing Wissa who pounced on a mistake to level in the 52nd minute.

New arrival Toure then broke clear of the Valencia defence to unselfishly set up Wissa for a tap-in to complete the comeback in the 76th minute.

Toure should have had a second assist after fine work down the left, but Jacob Murphy put over his cross in stoppage time.

The win brings some relief to Newcastle on the day they lost their captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal.

Jaissle's next pre-season test will come on Wednesday as his new side face Everton at Murrayfield in Edinburgh.

Image: Newcastle's Nick Woltemade (left) started at the Mestalla

Wissa's fresh start under Jaissle

Sky Sports News' Keith Downie at the Mestalla:

"A good end to a positive week in Spain for Newcastle - and a trophy for Jaissle in his first match in charge as they lift the 'Orange Cup'.

"Some impressive signs from new signings Aladji Bamba, Steur and Toure.

"Newcastle's travelling fans sent home from The Mestalla with a spring in their step.

"One major positive was Wissa's performance.

"Newcastle really need him to come good this season. It was a huge £55m outlay on a 29-year-old, and last season was a nightmare for him.

"He looks sharp and is coming off a good World Cup showing. Maybe this could be a fresh start for the striker."

Jaissle keeping 'balanced' after debut win

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle speaking at his post-match press conference:

"First of all, I'm really happy that there are no serious injuries. Anthony, we are happy, and it seems to be okay, actually - that was the most important thing.

"Of course, winning games always helps to gain confidence, but we also knew that we had a hard week behind us. The players did well in the camp; there was a pure commitment in each session.

"We had a hard load, so therefore now we deserve two days off, and then we start again.

"It was a friendly today; we will not smash the locker room now and celebrate a lot.

"We're quite balanced; we know what it is about. Now it's pre-season, and we're still looking to work on it.

"It's just a journey; we don't want to hang onto that.

"The victory is higher than it is, but also we don't see the losses lower than it is then, so we should be quite balanced in our approach.

"We should just analyse the situation and develop from there, and that's what we're going to do.

"Now next week, there are things we need to work on, definitely."

Sports.title: McKenna becomes middleweight world champ with dream homecoming win
Sports.content:
Ireland's Aaron McKenna defeated Etinosa Oliha to become a middleweight world champion.

For McKenna this fight in Dublin was a dream homecoming. The Irish middleweight had pursued his career across America, sparring in some of the world's best gyms and amassing an undefeated pro record.

This contest, for the vacant IBF middleweight title, was his first world title fight and his first professional contest in Ireland.

With brother Stevie taking a spectacular knockout earlier, McKenna made a memorable entrance, wildly cheered into the ring by the 3Arena crowd, so loudly that the floor was almost rumbling.

But he didn't let emotions carry him away at the start of the fight. He edged forward onto the front foot, feinting. He timed a left hook as Oliha, unbeaten himself coming in, stepped to him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna had an incredible entrance ahead of his IBF world middleweight title fight with Etinosa Oliha, first coming into Sinead O'Connor's The Foggy Dew and then Faithless' Insomnia!

McKenna let his jab flicker out. His hands were quick, his right streaked in and McKenna used his left hook to let a cross blast through.

But the Italian wrested the second round his way, thumping through right hooks, punches McKenna felt, to show that he too could launch meaningful attacks.

McKenna ground forward, stifling his own long-range work but bodily forcing Oliha back.

When he did strike his opponent with a reaching right, the crowd roared and as the fight progressed into its second half McKenna did move more on his toes, darting back to scrape his left hook into the side of Oliha's head.

The Italian looked to rip hooks into him but McKenna marshalled him to the ropes and slugged Oliha with a left hook.

Image: McKenna and Oliha were both unbeaten coming into this world title fight

McKenna imposed himself again in the ninth round but Oliha, a solid operator, showed little sign of wilting.

In the 10th round McKenna circled out and reeled off double jabs. As they grappled in a clinch though, Oliha unleashed a flurry that caught the Irishman.

McKenna briefly put space between them with a cross to the chin. He scored to the body with thudding right hooks too.

Oliha charged from his corner with a long one-two to start the 11th round. With flashier work, McKenna landed a left uppercut off his jab. Oliha though hacked back at him with a right hook up close.

McKenna continued to punch in greater volume. A clash saw him cut on the forehead just before the end of the 11th. He trusted in a hefty right hook as a response.

Image: McKenna tears into Oliha.

He didn't want or need to take risks in the last round. He moved sharply, striking an increasingly desperate Oliha with jabs and the crowd all around him stood up cheering, clapping and chanting his name.

McKenna worked an uppercut, Oliha drove in a right but even when McKenna took shots he didn't let them shake him as he closed out a unanimous decision.

When that final bell chimed, McKenna rushed to the corner post and jumped up onto the ropes to celebrate.

As soon as the words "from Monaghan" were declared by the ring announcer, confirming McKenna a 118-110, 117-111 and 116-112 victor, the arena burst into deafening cheers once again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna was in buoyant mood after beating Etinosa Oliha to become IBF world middleweight champion in front of his home crowd in Dublin.

"A new world champion. I've been saying it for years. A big thank you to Zuffa Boxing for giving me this platform and bringing a fight back to Ireland for me," McKenna beamed afterwards.

"I've been a professional for nine years and never got the chance to fight in Ireland. Why? Just look at these beautiful fans.

"I never lost discipline in training. There were times when I wondered whether I'd ever get the chance.

"My dad [their trainer] sacrificed his whole life for me and my brother, dedicating everything to helping us chase our dreams.

"Finally, I've got my hands on this."

Sports.title: 'Good signs' for Man Utd as Mbeumo scores in encouraging  draw with PSG
Sports.content:
Bryan Mbeumo earned Man Utd a 1-1 draw with Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg, a pre-season friendly which left boss Michael Carrick encouraged by the "good signs" from his side.

A slow start, which saw Liverpool-linked Ibrahim Mbaye tuck in a PSG opener after just two minutes and the European champions - despite missing many of their star names - stretch United, was overcome and fears of an injury to Mason Mount were also allayed, with the midfielder later seen walking freely after being forced off during the first half.

The standout Amad Diallo was key to United shifting the momentum. He won the ball back high up the pitch to tee up Mbeumo for a fine finish for United's equaliser and proved too hot to handle for the PSG defence into the half-time break.

Mbeumo would have added to his tally had PSG's Matvey Safonov not been in such sharp form, although the goalkeeper left the pitch to jeers after escaping punishment for clattering Joshua Zirkzee way outside of his area.

Image: Youri Tielemans made his first appearance for Man Utd against PSG

At the other end, United goalkeeper Tom Heaton suffered a hamstring issue and had to be replaced. It was a problem which appears more significant than the injury Mount seemingly got to his left foot, which Carrick later suggested was just a kick. With Altay Bayindir loaned to Celta Vigo and Radek Vitek sold to Middlesbrough, 23-year-old Dermot Mee came on for his debut.

There were late chances for Tyler Fletcher, Shea Lacey and captain Bruno Fernandes - who linked up excitingly with new signing Youri Tielemans. United weren't able to find a winner but this was a performance to be positive about.

Man Utd team news: Tielemans on for debut as Bruno returns Youri Tielemans came on as a second-half sub to make his Man Utd debut in Sweden. Captain Bruno Fernandes also entered the action for his first minutes of pre-season.



Michael Carrick had made just one change from the side which started the win over Atletico Madrid last weekend, with Noussair Mazraoui coming in for Leny Yoro.



PSG were without their France stars Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue or Bradley Barcola.

The key moments from Gothenberg...

2: GOAL! Ibrahim Mbaye tucks in the opener at the back post from Dro Fernandez's cross after Ayden Heaven is unable to cut it out.

4: SHOT! PSG threaten again with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia denied from distance by Tom Heaton.

16: BLOCK! Andrey Santos slides in to block Mbaye's shot over the bar with United stretched.

20: INJURY! Mason Mount is forced off injured with an apparent foot injury.

32: GOAL! Amad Diallo wins the ball back high up the pitch and feeds Bryan Mbeumo who cracks an equaliser across goal and into the bottom corner.

Man Utd on the front foot Man Utd had 24 touches in the opposition box. PSG managed just seven.

36: NO PENALTY! Amad's appeals are waved away when Willian Pacho nudges him as he goes for a header.

38: SAVE! For the second time in the match Mbeumo tests PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov with a free-kick shot.

48: INJURY! Heaton injures his right hamstring making a clearance and Dermot Mee comes on in his place.

54: SAVE! Stunning stop from Safonov to deny Mbeumo's shot towards the top corner from outside the box.

72: DRAMA! Safonov rushes out of his box and clatters Zirkzee with his shoulder as United try to counter no foul is given and after Jack Fletcher declines a long-range shot at the unguarded goal, Shea Lacey's effort is blocked behind.

87: CHANCES! Dalot's cross is met by Tyler Fletcher but he twice has efforts blocked before Lacey lashes over from a tight angle

89: CLOSE! Fernandes whips a shot just wide of the far post with a bouncing shot from outside the box.

Carrick 'enjoyed' PSG draw: 'We should have scored more goals'

Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick to MUTV:

"I enjoyed it. Good challenge. Slightly different with the way they play. We should've scored more goals.

"Very different to what we've played against, the boys adapted really well, so there were a lot of positives from the game. The things we were trying to get out of the game, a lot of it was there.

"It's good for the boys sometimes to have to problem solve and find their own way and I thought we did that. That prepares them for the season as well. In that respect there were a lot of things that maybe people don't always see that we were quite happy with. There were some good signs there."

Attacking positives for Man Utd in PSG draw

Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

"Man Utd's attack caught the eye on Saturday, with Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo looking sharp and the connection between Youri Tielemans and Bruno Fernandes already clicking.

"Amad played a big part in shifting the momentum United's way after PSG's fast start. In the final third he won the ball back and passed it more than any other player on the pitch.

"That impact with and without the ball was clear when he found Mbeumo for the equaliser - and the striker's finish was excellent.

"Mbeumo could easily have scored more but for some good goalkeeping, landing four shots on target. No other player managed more than one.

"Debutant Tielemans and returning captain Fernandes could not be expected to be so sharp making their first minutes of pre-season - but still they produced some nice link-up play and signs they will be a big influence in this coming campaign.

"Tielemans' passing from deep was classy; Fernandes was immediately a threat around the edge of the box.

"As Michael Carrick said afterwards, 'good signs' for the season ahead."

July 24: Man Utd 5-0 Rosenborg - Trondheim

August 8: PSG 1-1 Man Utd - Gothenburg

Sports.title: Walsh battles through cuts and knockdown to drop Denny and take victory
Sports.content:
Callum Walsh maintained his unbeaten record and top contender status with a unanimous decision victory over Tyler Denny.

Denny, a former European champion, is a tough veteran and proved a test for the Irish middleweight at Dublin's 3Arena.

Walsh prevailed on points, winning 98-91 twice and 96-90.

The bout didn't progress without its pitfalls as Denny gave him hard rounds.

The first round suddenly went south for Walsh. Awkwardly positioned in front of Denny, he found himself bending low. Denny attacked and Walsh took a shot before slipping to a knee. The referee ruled that a knockdown.

Image: Walsh has a knockdown scored against him.

Walsh found the perfect riposte in the second round. As Denny came after him, Walsh launched a lovely arching left cross to the point of the Englishman's chin, dropping him heavily to the canvas.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Callum Walsh put Tyler Denny down in the second round with a huge left hand punch.

Denny, brave as ever, rose and fought on. But Walsh popped up from beneath an attack to land a fine right hook and he finished the round slugging Denny into the ropes.

The Briton shook off the effects of that round and advanced. By the end of the fourth round, Walsh was backing up, letting his southpaw opponent come on but picking out accurate punches to catch Denny.

Walsh maintained his control, moving, hitting and letting Denny work to try to pin him down.

The Briton kept scrapping forward and managed to land solidly in the sixth round.

Denny trudged on swinging wildly, but Walsh manoeuvred well. The Irishman caught Denny to the head with a left-right combination. Denny felt those shots but remained doggedly determined. He cleaved away with uppercuts in close.

Image: Walsh readies to uncork his southpaw left

The referee took a point off Walsh for holding, before evening up it by taking a point off Denny for hitting behind the head.

Walsh exploded forward with a savage sequence of punches to the head, leaving Denny stranded, standing still on the end of them.

But Walsh emerged from a clash with a cut over his left eye. It bled badly at once. Denny was leaning into him in scrappy collisions and Walsh looked frustrated after picking an additional nick on his cheek.

In the 10th round Walsh landed a great lead right uppercut. Denny got after him with hooks, catching the Irishman with his southpaw left and right.

Another hard left from Walsh though snagged Denny. He couldn't put the Englishman down a second time but made sure he finished the fight in the ascendancy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of Callum Walsh's clash with Tyler Denny from Zuffa Boxing 10 in Dublin.

'I think he broke my orbital bone'

Walsh told Sky Sports: "It was a lot harder than I thought. In the second round we clashed heads. I think he broke my orbital bone. It was crunching the whole time.

"It was very tough. I'm very critical of myself. I should have been a lot better. I wish I could have been better.

"He's tough, awkward and tricky, but we'll go again."
