Sports.title: Why Honda only realised the scale of its F1 problems in January
Sports.content:
Heading into Formula 1's major technical overhaul, expectations at Aston Martin were high. With a state-of-the-art factory in Silverstone, legendary designer Adrian Newey and a works partnership with Honda, all the ingredients for success appeared to be in place.

That may still prove to be the case in the longer term, but the start of the new era has proved far more challenging than anticipated. Mike Krack recently admitted that Aston Martin had barely been racing before the summer break, simply because the gap to newcomer Cadillac amounted to around one second.

That changed when the AMR26 received its first major upgrade package in Hungary, although the chassis is naturally only part of the story. Honda has also encountered numerous problems since officially returning to F1, ranging from vibrations that troubled the drivers during the opening weeks of the season to a significant deficit in outright performance.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with Autosport, trackside manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara explained that the full extent of those problems only became clear in January.

“So, probably at the end of last year, our position was not so bad,” he said. “Still, performance and drivability were in the development stage, but it looked okay.

"But in January, we realised that in some of the areas we found some, not issues, but we realised that performance was always up, down, up, down. So we found some performance, but then we also found some reliability issues."

Shintaro Orihara, Honda Photo by: EYE4images / NurPhoto via Getty Images

Because reliability is always a top priority, Honda had to take a step back on several performance gains to ensure reliability at that performance level. Naturally, that slowed down its overall development.

"In January, we realised that our performance and reliability would not be competitive,” Orihara added. “When we started running in Barcelona, we realised that our performance was definitely poor compared to the other manufacturers. And also, we found some issues on the battery side."

Those battery-related issues made the development process more complex. They cost valuable track time during winter testing, something that was especially painful given Aston Martin and Honda's need to gather data to recover from their deficit.

"So we realised that we were not in good position, maybe at beginning of this year. Last year, at end of last year, we already saw that we were not competitive, but we didn't expect it so bad," Orihara admitted.

What has been Honda's biggest challenge?

Part of the explanation is that Honda's current F1 project is very different from its successful years with Red Bull, something that ties in with the company's philosophy of transferring F1 knowledge to other parts of the company.

Another part of the explanation is, according to Honda, the complexity of the current regulations. Orihara stressed that there has not been one single stumbling block ahead of 2026, but rather the combination of all the changes introduced at the same time.

Honda Power Unit Launch

"It's difficult to say which component of the power unit is most challenging because in this regulation, everything has changed a lot,” said Orihara. “For example, MGU-K power changed from, let's say, [120] to 350 kilowatts. That is a significant change.

"But also on the internal combustion engine side, we have changed the fuel flow rate. So in this regulation, everything has been changed so much. So, a challenging point for Honda is just the combination of a lot of changes happening at the same time."

That means Honda is lacking outright power from its internal combustion engine, something the long-awaited Zandvoort upgrade is specifically designed to address. It is intended to be the first step towards reducing the brand's still significant performance deficit.

On the electrical side of the power unit, the emphasis is on efficiency. However, Orihara explained that the changes there have also had a major impact on drivability – one of the areas that has been a recurring topic for Honda and Aston Martin in the opening months of the season.

"Removing the MGU-H has also been quite challenging on the power unit side,” he said.

“Probably that is the most exciting point for power unit manufacturers. I have always been mentioning drivability. That is, maybe not mainly, but the majority of that is coming from removing the MGU-H.

"So that is a challenging point for us as a power unit supplier, to keep the boost pressure at a target. Again, it's difficult to pick one component that has been most challenging for us, but it has been the combination of all changes at the same time."

Although Honda knows that returning to the competitive level it is targeting will take time - a lot of time - it hopes to make a first step at Zandvoort. That upgrade is focused purely on improving the internal combustion engine and was already tested during a filming day at the Hungaroring.

Sports.title: Why McLaren has been coy about introducing its rotating F1 rear wing
Sports.content:
McLaren will race its version of the so-called 'Macarena' rear-wing concept – but not until an unspecified point in the future, according to team principal Andrea Stella.

It's understood that the reason for not rushing to race the new rear wing is not linked to Red Bull's well-documented issues with its similar design. Instead, McLaren is being cautiously pragmatic, since the rotating rear wing adds to the complexities of managing car behaviour as it moves in and out of Straight Line Mode (SLM).

McLaren planned to test its new wing in Austria but made a late decision to abandon the evaluation. It then waited until Hungary to run it for the first time in FP1 on Oscar Piastri's car, driven by Leonardo Fornaroli, before parking it for the remainder of the event.

Max Verstappen crashed at the Red Bull Ring and Silverstone, prompting his Red Bull team to temporarily shelve its pivoting rear wing based on suspicions that a delay in airflow reattachment when the wing returned to cornering mode made Verstappen's car unstable.

"I have to say it's been a complicated project," Stella told media including Autosport.

"Which was no surprise because when we saw Ferrari introducing the wing in Bahrain test and testing it in China in the first lap, [Lewis] Hamilton spun. And then it took a few more events to actually being in condition to race it.

"We knew it was going to be a complex project, so I have to say that our engineering department has delivered this project in a way that looks well-behaved – like the wing in terms of mechanical actuation, times of the actuation, because there's some limitations by the regulations, not only for aerodynamic reasons.

Ferrari was the first team to run its rotating rear wing, which operates differently to the McLaren and Red Bull examples Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"And then the overall behaviour from an aerodynamic point of view, reattachment – so the time it takes for the car to regain the load, not only the load on the wing, the load on the entire car as driven from the wing.

"All this I have to say has been pretty consistent with expectation, so it's been a positive sign off of this concept and we look forward now to introducing this concept at some future events."

These concepts are a classic example of thinking-outside-the-box creative engineering that is possible for the first time this season because the regulations are relatively open. F1 first adopted the principle of legally shedding drag in a straight line with the Drag Reduction System (DRS) in 2011, which permitted the upper rear wing plane to flatten in prescribed areas of the track.

The speed and actuation procedure for this was clearly defined, along with the dimensions of the wing planes themselves. But under the new ruleset introduced this season, in which front and rear wing flaps can open in specified Straight Line Mode zones, the speed of transition from one state to the other is defined (within 0.4s), but not the means by which it moves between open and closed.

McLaren's pivoting rear wing is closer to Red Bull's than Ferrari's, in that it uses a central actuator to manage the rotation rather than having a mechanism built into the endplates. Also like Red Bull's, it pivots forwards rather than backwards.

The means of actuation gives it an element of air braking as it closes. The trade-off between the two concepts is that Red Bull and McLaren accept a degree of aerodynamic blockage from the actuator and its shroud in exchange for having a wider space between the upper and lower planes when SLM is active.

Ferrari's also has to take a longer path between open and closed because of the angle of rotation.

Verstappen shunted in qualifying in Austria, and a delay in airflow reattachment to the rear wing was cited as one possible contributory factor Photo by: Getty Images

One of the less predictable effects of the new regulations has been the shift in tyre loading during the transition between SLM being on and off. This is because the airflow doesn't reattach to the wing planes instantly, but takes fractions of a second to re-establish its path.

Teams knew ahead of the season that this would be a significant performance factor, but were unable to measure it accurately with simulation tools such as the wind tunnel and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD).

The true extent of the shifts in loadings, and their effect on car behaviour, could only be measured at the track.

This also applies to the theoretical benefits of the rotating rear wings. The airflow around the rear of an F1 car is tremendously busy because of the interaction between the car's aerodynamic surfaces and the turbulent wake of the rear wheels.

Simulating this with great accuracy is very difficult in the wind tunnel, where model size is capped at 60% scale and the wind is generally blowing in one direction. Historically it is difficult to access a car's aerodynamic performance when it's in a state of yaw (i.e. turning), or facing different wind directions. The different deflection properties of the model tyres, as well as their smaller size, also has a tendency to skew results.

Hence McLaren has done a lot of FP1 running with large aero rakes fitted behind the rear wheels to validate substantial bodywork changes such as the latest-spec floor, introduced in Hungary, as well as its pivoting wing. Practical measurements trackside are the real proof (or otherwise) of any theoretical gains.

"There was a question about comparison with Red Bull, but I don't think the wind tunnel is a major factor in terms of determining the aerodynamic behaviour in reattachment," Stella said.

"I think you can use some other tools for that, and then the most important tool, especially when you have this sort of complicated project, even from an aerodynamic point of view, remains what you observe at the track. So it was important for us to acquire data here trackside, because you would have never relied on a wind tunnel only for such a delicate project."

Sports.title: Why the FIA couldn't intervene sooner over F1's 2026 rules
Sports.content:
With the first Formula 1 season under the new technical regulations approaching its halfway point, the summer break provides a good opportunity to take stock. The 2026 rules, with their much greater emphasis on electric power, have sparked considerable debate both in and outside the paddock.

F1 insists that fan ratings – for example in its own Formula 1 Fan Voice programme – have been largely positive, but drivers have been far more critical.

Max Verstappen described the power unit regulations as "Formula E on steroids" during winter testing in Bahrain, while Oscar Piastri spoke at Spa-Francorchamps about the "self-learning elements" of the power units and "qualifying grids being decided by computers behaving or misbehaving".

Asked by Autosport whether the criticism from drivers over the past few months had been stronger than the FIA expected, Tombazis responded: "I think drivers are, by definition, quite demanding clients. I don't think we expected them to have a sugarcoat or to not speak their minds. So to say that it's been more than expected, no, I wouldn't say so."

The complaints from drivers about energy management, super clipping and algorithms were also in line with what the FIA had anticipated, according to its single-seater director.

"We did anticipate a lot of these things that they have complained about in the two years before the launch of the season. We did try to make some adjustments, but we failed with the governance that was in place," Tombazis said. "So I think it was realistically only to be expected."

Energy-starved circuits such as Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps have highlighted the shortcomings of the 2026 regulations Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

FIA tried to listen to F1 drivers' criticism in build-up to 2026

If it had been up to Tombazis, the changes to the regulations that have now been agreed for 2027 and 2028 – to gradually move to a 60-40 split – would ideally have been introduced much earlier.

"I think it's a bit of a shame that we had to wait until we discussed things in May and get to a package for 2027 and for 2028. I think we could have ideally done that a couple of years before and then there wouldn't have been all of this discussion," Tombazis said.

Several drivers warned about potential problems with the new engine regulations before 2026. Verstappen was the first to do so publicly during the 2023 Austrian Grand Prix, when Autosport asked him about his initial simulator runs with the new engine formula.

That has perhaps created the impression that drivers were not listened to in the years leading up to 2026, but Tombazis insists the reality is different. According to him, the initial feedback was taken seriously, but the governance framework meant the regulations could not be significantly revised.

"When OEMs decide to participate as PU manufacturers, they sign a governance agreement that is binding towards all parties, so the FIA, FOM and the PU manufacturers. It's similar to what the Concorde Agreement does for the team side of things," Tombazis explained.

"And there was a separate governance agreement signed in 2022 in order to basically outline the requirements for the PU manufacturers during the years of 2023, 2024 and 2025. That is before the championship started because there's such things like financial regulations for the first time."

The FIA states that governance, even with new manufacturers such as Audi, has made intervention impossible Photo by: Pirelli

Among other things, that agreement stipulated that new entrants would not be allowed to spend unlimited amounts of money to develop their 2026 power units.

"If a PU manufacturer who was not participating in Formula 1, let's say Audi, they still had to be bound by regulations and not come to us and say, well, we're not participating, hence we can spend five times the money. That would be unfair," he said.

"So that's why there was a governance agreement that on the one hand forced them to be bound by the regulations, including the financial and operational rules and all of that."

At the same time, that document made it much harder for the FIA to reopen the regulations in the years leading up to 2026 without securing a supermajority.

"On the other hand it put limitations as to how much we could change things unilaterally as the FIA. And therefore any change had to be approved by a significant number of the PU manufacturers," Tombazis explained.

"So for the sort of changes we did [in May], we needed at least four of them to agree. And quite simply, four of them did not agree during the years when we discussed some adjustments."

Tombazis had hoped that the changes for the coming years could have been implemented sooner Photo by: Lars Baron / Getty Images

Challenges known since 2022, but races still entertaining

Part of the reason for that was that the reality of the automotive industry looked very different at the time, with manufacturers placing a much greater emphasis on electrification.

"Overall, it was always a challenging target to have a close to 50-50 power split between the two units," Tombazis said.

"But that was a very important position for the OEMs participating, and frankly having to decide whether they want to be in Formula 1 or not. Don't forget that if we didn't have them in, we would have just two power units in Formula 1, which I think would have been a bit of an issue. So that requirement to have a much stronger electrical part did create these difficulties."

Tombazis explained that the FIA had already become aware of these challenges in 2022, a year before Verstappen publicly voiced his concerns, but by then it was simply too late to fundamentally alter the regulations.

"As simulations came in back in 2022 or so, we knew there were these issues, but we were a bit too far down the line there to change things and some people had committed too much resource," he said. "So that left us slightly on the back foot at the start of the season, discussing that."

Tombazis concluded by stressing that, despite all of this, the races themselves have still provided good entertainment during the first half of the season.

Tombazis feels despite the problems with the F1 regulations, the racing has been exciting Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"Now with that said, I think most races have been pretty exciting, I would say. There's been quite a lot of fighting," he said.

"I would even say that currently we still have, I don't know if I would go quite as far as to call it domination, but we do have a clear advantage for one manufacturer. And in the past when we've had that at the early start of the regulations, races have been very processional.

"Now I think, even despite the fact that Mercedes have been doing most of the winning, I think the races have nonetheless been quite exciting with quite a lot of changes and so on."

Sports.title: Domenicali resists Briatore’s call for sprint races at every round | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali will not move to add sprint races at every round next season, but still plans to hold more than the current six.

Alpine consultant Flavio Briatore recently argued for F1 to hold sprint races every week and, as is done in Moto GP.

Speaking in Liberty Media’s latest earnings update call for investors, Domenicali said limiting the number of sprint rounds gives them scarcity value.

“Sprint races is an opportunity that, first of all, started because we wanted to produce something that could create action on the track, creating leverage for the promoter and ourselves to create action on the tracks starting for the weekend,” he said. “We’re going to have more sprint races next year, yes. We’ll inform when we will announce the calendar, how many.

“The principle is very simple. This is also an opportunity to increment the revenue stream, for sure. This is an opportunity for us to have new deals, as we have already seen, and moving in this direction will be our future. We want to do in the right way because, of course, this will allow us also to make sure that the scarcity is a value.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Antonelli says he ‘let pressure destroy me’ in mid-season slump last year | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he succumbed to pressure when he suffered a slump in form during the middle of his debut season last year.

The Mercedes driver went through a seven-round spell when he finished in the points just once – albeit on the podium. His dip in form coincided with changes to Mercedes’ car which he struggled to get to grips with.

“I had a good start to the season, then I had a difficult period,” said Antonelli in a recent interview. “In the European season I really struggled and in that moment I let the pressure kind of destroy me as well during that period.

“I felt like I was letting down so many people who had believed in me. Of course especially Toto [Wolff, Mercedes team principal], because he was the main one who took the decision [to promote him].

“Obviously I didn’t feel good in that period. I wasn’t doing well. But then I had a big meeting with the team after the European season and it kind of allowed me to reset and just start again.

“Then I slowly found my way back. I had a good second half of the season and that gave me confidence, being able to overcome those difficult moments and gave me the confidence ahead of this year. It also made me learn a lot about myself, not only as a driver, but as a person as well.”

Antonelli said the experience taught him useful lessons about coping with adversity. “Obviously [during] that European season, I think probably most of the things I did, didn’t help me at all,” he said.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But also I learned about how my body responds to those moments, how my brain responds, what helps me to get back into the right focus, the right mindset, what helps me to stay 100% in terms of energy during the whole weekend. So how to manage myself with events, obviously the driving and everything. So I’ve learned a lot about myself and how as well to respond to difficult moments.”

Mercedes promoted Antonelli directly to their top team, in the seat formerly occupied by Lewis Hamilton, at the age of 18. Antonelli said making his F1 debut with a front-running team left him feeling depleted by the end of the 24-round championship.

“I was so drained at the end of the year,” he said. “Obviously the team did an incredible job in trying to protect me. But the learning curve – I think I’ve learned much more than if I would have done in a smaller team.

“The learning curve was incredible, it was like doing three years at once. It was overwhelming, physically, mentally, because I’ve made so many new experiences as well.

“Also, doing a full F1 season for the first time, you don’t really know where you’re going, what you’re about to face. Obviously the year prior to F1, I’ve been doing race shadowing and everything, but it’s not the same.

“When I was doing shadowing, I was watching, I wasn’t there on track doing the job. So I felt very overwhelmed at the end of the year. And it was good to have a bit of a break to just have a little bit of time to analyse and reflect on the year and understand what were the good things and why and why some things went not in the right way.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Having become the youngest driver to lead the world championship, Antonelli says he is trying to enjoy the position and the attention which comes with it, particularly in his home country.

“It’s like in any sport at the highest level, there’s always pressure and of course, being Italian, Italy has been missing an Italian driver for quite a long time and obviously also knowing myself because I’m Italian.

“We know how as Italians we can get very excited about things and how expectations can get over the moon. But obviously that comes with a bit of a extra pressure. But I’ve been enjoying, I have been enjoying. I think what I’ve been trying to do as well is to embrace the pressure and trying to actually shine under pressure.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Norris vs Piastri: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The super-close contest between the McLaren team mates last year would have made for a thrilling world championship fight even if Max Verstappen hadn’t got involved.

Now in their fourth season as team mates, with a completely different type of McLaren to get used to, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have been fairly well-matched on the whole. However in individual races their relative performance has varied, most notably in Hungary last weekend, where Norris was clearly much quicker.

Norris has been on a strong run lately, out-qualifying his team mate for the last five rounds in a row. Though it bears pointing out that Piastri missed first practice at the last round and was badly baulked by Lewis Hamilton when he began his final run.

It took Piastri until the third round of the season merely to start a grand prix, suffering a mortifying pre-race crash at home, then retiring before the start along with Norris in Shanghai. He rebounded magnificently at Suzuka and might have won had it not been for the timing of a Safety Car period.

McLaren have had further technical trouble since then: Norris had back-to-back failures while Piastri’s retirement in Hungary capped a frustrating race where a wayward backmarker had already cost him the lead. Piastri had a rough race in Canada as well, where both McLaren drivers paid the price for a tactical gamble which backfired.

It was therefore fitting that Norris delivered the team’s first win as F1 headed into the summer break. His 36-point lead over Piastri looks like a fair reflection of their relative performances given the various setbacks both drivers have suffered. The world champion holds the upper hand so far but Piastri is keeping him honest as always.

Sports.title: Hamilton vs Leclerc: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Does Lewis Hamilton have an eighth world championship in him? Has he not recovered from the blow of 2021 or did he simply never gel with the ‘ground effect’ cars of 2022-25?

Those hoping to see the seven-times world champion fight for another title will have drawn great encouragement from what they have seen so far in 2026. Last year, in his first season at Ferrari, he came off badly in comparison to Charles Leclerc , taking a 19-5 pasting in qualifying and making zero podium appearances to his team mate’s seven.

Hamilton has given full credit to team principal Frederic Vasseur for implementing the changes he needed to make a success of his transition to Ferrari, whether that has involved different brake material or swerving the simulator. On the face of it, it has paid off, and Ferrari now have two A-list drivers performing at their peak.

Leclerc is still shading Hamilton on average in qualifying, but the fight between the two has been much closer. Hamilton has delivered more consistently on race day, including that breakthrough victory in Spain.

Both drivers have misfired at times. Leclerc had a spate of errors including costly crashes in qualifying at the Circuit de Catalunya and during his home race.

Hamilton, meanwhile, has picked up a bad habit of incurring the stewards’ wrath, collecting a series of needless penalties in recent races. Though some may not have been his fault or were debatable calls, many others were straightforward, and he was fortunate to avoid a worse penalty for his yellow flag slip in Silverstone.

For all that, Hamilton is Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s closest rival in the championship at the summer break. “Has the time finally come for Hamilton to hang up his helmet?” we asked in May, in what already looks like one of the most poorly-timed polls ever featured on RaceFans.

Sports.title: Antonelli vs Russell: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Early in the season it seemed certain that whichever of the Mercedes drivers came out ahead would be crowned world champion. That remains likely, but the threat posed by rival teams has grown in recent races.

Little about Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s form in his rookie season indicated that 12 months later he would be beating his team mate quite as emphatically as he is. But heading into the summer break, Antonelli holds a valuable 59-point lead over the other Mercedes driver.

It’s a far cry from the situation around 12 months ago. At the end of the ‘European season’, Antonelli was 15-1 down against George Russell in qualifying. He ended the season still with less than half his team mate’s points tally.

But after a difficult mid-season, following a Mercedes upgrade which did not go as intended, Antonelli rebounded impressively with the end of the year in sight. He reached the podium twice over the final four rounds.

So while Russell’s season-opening victory in Australia looked like the shape of things to come, Antonelli shattered those illusions by winning the next five rounds in a row. He got the rub of the green at times – technical trouble hit Russell in qualifying at Shanghai and took him out while he led in Montreal – but he has also seemed fundamentally more at ease with Mercedes’ W17 than his team mate.

The unusually high rate of problems on Mercedes’ cars, and Russell’s particular problems with poor straight-line speed at Silverstone and Spa, have further complicated the picture. Antonelli’s car has not been immune, breaking down in Spain and breaking an aerodynamic component at Silverstone. Overall, Russell has probably had slightly worse luck, but not 59 points’ worth. Antonelli is leading this championship on merit, and Russell will have to dig deep in the second half of the season if he is going to avoid a painful defeat.

Would Top Rank Risk Emanuel Navarrete Against William Zepeda?
Sports.content:
“Man, that’s CTE at its finest. It’s a bloodbath waiting [to happen],” Crawford said during the post-fight show on DAZN and TNT’s “The Fight.”

While Crawford envisions both men doing serious damage, Navarrete may be the one taking the brunt of it.

Navarrete moved up to 135 pounds in May 2024, dropping a split decision to Denys Berinchyk for the vacant WBO belt. He struggled to find his rhythm against the Ukrainian, looking far removed from the fighter who captured titles at 122, 126 and 130 pounds.

Zepeda presents a completely different style of threat. He gives opponents little time to rest or set their offense. Roach discovered that early as Zepeda stayed in his face and dictated the pace for all 12 rounds.

Navarrete never shies away from trading punches, but slugging with Zepeda at lightweight favors the naturally larger man. Moving up from super featherweight to face a champion who breaks opponents down through sustained volume carries enormous risk.

Top Rank must decide if the reward justifies taking that chance. Navarrete holds the IBF and WBO titles at 130 pounds, where a unification against WBC champion O’Shaquie Foster remains an attractive option.

Top Rank has another route into the lightweight picture. WBO champion Abdullah Mason sat ringside for Zepeda’s win over Roach and is already an obvious choice for a unification bout.

If Top Rank wants one of its champions in with Zepeda, Mason can take the fight without changing divisions. Sending Navarrete back to lightweight after his previous loss is the riskier move, especially against a relentless pressure fighter who would force him to work every minute.

Sports.title: McKenna Declares Himself World’s Best Middleweight
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames remains one of the division’s toughest established champions. Yoenli Hernandez has been rapidly moving toward a title opportunity and has made the same claim about being the world’s best middleweight. Erislandy Lara remains a difficult stylistic test despite his age, while Tim Tszyu’s move into the division brings another proven fighter into the mix.

McKenna certainly looked the part against Oliha. His jab controlled the fight, his movement kept Oliha from establishing consistent pressure, and he remained composed after suffering a cut late.

The question is what happens when the opposition gets better.

Oliha came to Dublin with a 22-0 record, but he lacked the speed and variety needed to disrupt McKenna. Adames would bring considerably more pressure and power. Hernandez presents a different challenge with his Cuban amateur background and physical tools. Tszyu would test McKenna’s ability to deal with sustained pressure from a much more accomplished offensive fighter.

McKenna has the belt now. If he wants the distinction he claimed Saturday night, there are plenty of middleweights available to help him prove it.

Sports.title: Aaron McKenna Dominates Oliha, Wins IBF Middleweight Title
Sports.content:
McKenna established the pattern early. The 27-year-old used his height and reach to spear Oliha with jabs upstairs and to the body, then moved before the Italian challenger was able to answer effectively.

Oliha tried to close the distance and turn the fight into something more physical, but McKenna rarely remained stationary long enough for him to sustain an attack. When Oliha came forward, McKenna frequently met him with right hands, uppercuts and combinations.

The difference became increasingly clear through the middle rounds. Oliha continued pressing, occasionally getting to the body, but he struggled to deal with McKenna’s activity at long and intermediate range.

McKenna wasn’t limited to boxing from the outside. He was comfortable exchanging at close range when necessary before creating space and returning to his jab.

A clash of heads left McKenna with a cut on his forehead later in the fight, but it did little to change his approach. He remained composed as the Dublin crowd chanted his name and continued picking Oliha off as the rounds disappeared.

Oliha needed something dramatic late and never found it. McKenna refused to give him the stationary target required to change the fight with one punch, closing out the championship rounds without surrendering control.

The victory gives Ireland its first middleweight world champion since Andy Lee and turns McKenna into a major player in the division.

The IBF championship became vacant after Janibek Alimkhanuly was stripped of the belt, giving McKenna and Oliha their opportunity in Dublin. McKenna took full advantage, producing a disciplined 12-round performance when the biggest prize of his career was at stake.

Sports.title: Simpson Avenges Williamson Loss, Reclaims British Titles
Sports.content:
Williamson started well in the opening round before Simpson came on during the final minute, forcing him toward the ropes. Simpson continued applying pressure in the second, landing effectively before the action repeatedly fell into clinches.

The third produced Simpson’s strongest attack of the early rounds. He hurt Williamson badly during the final minute and had him struggling to remain upright, but Williamson recovered and fought his way through the trouble.

Williamson responded in the fourth, finishing strongly with Simpson against the ropes. Simpson regained the advantage in the fifth before the two spent much of the sixth trading at close range and wrestling for position.

Simpson hurt Williamson against the ropes again midway through the seventh, but Williamson recovered and finished the round strongly. Williamson then produced one of his better rounds in the eighth.

The action remained competitive in the ninth, with Williamson hurting Simpson near the ropes during another series of exchanges. Williamson continued having success in the 10th before Simpson finished the round better.

Both fighters continued punching and clinching throughout the 11th. Early in the 12th, Williamson threw Simpson to the canvas during a physical exchange and received a warning from referee Steve Gray. Simpson finished the fight having done enough across the 12 rounds to regain his titles.

Kraus Stops Hemphill in First Round

In the co-feature, Gradus Kraus (12-0, 11 KOs) stopped Sean “Silky” Hemphill (19-4, 11 KOs) at 1:03 of the opening round to capture the WBA Continental light heavyweight title.

Kraus trapped Hemphill in the corner and unloaded with a series of unanswered punches. Referee John Latham intervened with Hemphill no longer returning fire.

Eales Decisions Krasimirov

Ashlee “Real Deal” Eales (13-2, 4 KOs) defeated Diego Krasimirov (10-1, 5 KOs) over eight rounds in their super welterweight bout.

Referee Michael Alexander scored the contest 76-74 for Eales.

Hassan Azim Stops Jack Martin

Southpaw Hassan “The Hit Man” Azim (10-0, 6 KOs) needed just 68 seconds to stop Jack “Ginger” Martin (10-3, 4 KOs).

Azim hurt Martin with a left hook and drove him toward the ropes. Another left hook dropped Martin moments later, and referee Michael Alexander stopped the contest after Martin regained his feet.

Mauro Silva Hands Christopher First Loss

Mauro “Super Mario” Silva (10-0, 4 KOs) defeated Tyler “Mike” Christopher (12-1, 2 KOs) over eight rounds in middleweight action.

Silva controlled much of the first three rounds and occasionally switched to southpaw. Christopher had greater success late, but Silva had already built a sufficient advantage. Referee Michael Alexander scored it 78-75.

Billy Pickles Wins Six-Round Decision

Billy “The Kid” Pickles (19-1, 1 KO) defeated Max Curtis (10-1, 1 KO) over six rounds at light welterweight.

Referee Mark Lyson scored the fight 58-55.

Ben Rees Scores Quick Knockout

Light heavyweight southpaw Ben Rees (8-0-1, 4 KOs) stopped Marvin “Black Mamba” Tomlinson (4-1, 2 KOs) just 13 seconds into the second round.

Tomlinson switched between orthodox and southpaw during the opening round and frequently tied Rees up. Rees ended matters almost immediately in the second, dropping Tomlinson with a right hook. Referee Mark Lyson stopped the fight without completing a count.

Billy Deniz Stops Alex Carter

Billy “Turkish Tyson” Deniz (16-0, 6 KOs) stopped Alex Carter (5-3) after the second round of their scheduled six-round super middleweight bout.

Bradley Casey Gets Decision Win

Cruiserweight Bradley “Bad Brad” Casey (6-0, 2 KOs) defeated Ross McGuigan (7-14-1, 1 KO) by decision.

Referee Mark Lyson scored the bout 39-36.

James Dean Fury Wins

James Dean Fury (1-0) defeated Dzmitry Atrokhau (16-37, 7 KOs) by decision.

Fury, a cousin of former heavyweight champion Tyson Fury, switched stances and used his jab effectively. Atrokhau landed several right hooks late in the opening round, but Fury generally produced the cleaner work.

Referee Mark Lyson scored the contest 60-54.

Frazer Clarke Stops Lamah Griggs

Heavyweight Frazer “The Eraser” Clarke (10-3-1, 8 KOs) stopped Lamah Griggs (3-14-1) at 1:41 of the second round of their scheduled six-round bout.

Referee Michael Alexander officiated the contest.

Sports.title: Callum Simpson Gets Revenge, Beats Troy Williamson
Sports.content:
Williamson had stopped Simpson in the 10th round of their first meeting last December after dropping him four times. Rather than trying to erase that loss with an immediate knockout, Simpson fought with greater control in the rematch and made his size and work rate count.

The biggest danger for Williamson came in the third. Simpson hurt him badly with heavy punches at close range, forcing the former champion to grab and survive until the bell.

Williamson recovered and gradually turned the fight into the physical battle he needed. He had success when he forced Simpson backward and landed the cleaner punches, particularly during several of the middle and later rounds.

Simpson never allowed the fight to deteriorate the way the first one had. The 29-year-old continued throwing in combination, leaned on Williamson during the inside exchanges and generally avoided giving him the clean opportunities that produced four knockdowns eight months earlier.

By the 10th, Simpson was doing a better job controlling the distance rather than simply meeting Williamson punch for punch. That proved important as Williamson continued pressing and trying to reproduce the dramatic finish from their first fight.

There was no repeat.

Both fighters made it through the championship rounds, leaving the outcome to the judges. Simpson had done enough across the 12 rounds to take back the two domestic belts and even their series at one victory apiece.

A third fight would be easy to sell. Williamson owns the far more decisive result with his four-knockdown stoppage, while Simpson now has the titles and a clear points victory. The rivalry is 1-1, and neither result completely settles which fighter is better.

Sports.title: Callum Walsh Survives Knockdown, Beats Tyler Denny
Sports.content:
The 25-year-old Walsh (17-0, 11 KOs) was fighting in Ireland with considerable expectations attached to him. White has been high on the Cork southpaw, and Denny was selected as the experienced opponent who could force him to deal with situations he had not regularly encountered during his rise.

That happened almost immediately.

Denny (21-5-3, 1 KO) dropped Walsh with a flash knockdown in the first round, putting the favorite in an early hole. Walsh responded well, sending the former European middleweight champion down in the second to quickly erase some of the damage.

From there, Walsh produced the cleaner work for much of the fight, but Denny never allowed him to settle into an easy rhythm. His awkward southpaw style and experience made Walsh work throughout the 10 rounds.

Things became messy in the eighth when referee intervention resulted in point deductions for both fighters. Walsh lost a point for holding, while Denny was penalized for hitting behind the head.

Denny then had one of his better rounds in the ninth, applying pressure and opening a cut near Walsh’s left eye. It gave Walsh another late test before he made it through the final round.

The official cards did not fully reflect how difficult the fight became in spots. Walsh deserved the decision, but Denny gave him considerably more resistance than scores of 98-91 twice might suggest.

That may ultimately make this more useful for Walsh than another quick knockout. He was dropped, forced to adjust against an awkward veteran, dealt with a cut and completed 10 competitive rounds.

Walsh remains perfect at 17-0, but tonight’s performance also showed there is still development needed before White’s highly regarded prospect is ready for the leading middleweights.

Sports.title: Frank Martin Open To Fighting Raymond Muratalla At Light Welterweight
Sports.content:
Martin heard the comments and welcomed the matchup.

“They mentioned my name first. He coming up to 140 or whatever, so I think they got their eyes on me or a fight with me. I’m really with fighting anybody. If everything makes sense and things like that, I’m with fighting anybody,” said Martin to Fighthype.

Promotional politics shouldn’t present much of an obstacle. Martin recently signed with Top Rank, putting him under the same banner as Muratalla. His priority, however, is following the plan his team already has in place.

Martin is targeting a return in October before pursuing a light welterweight title opportunity early next year.

“Hopefully I fight in October, and then we shooting for early next year to get the belt. I want to stick to what me and my team talked about and what we plan on working on. I want to stick with that route,” said Martin.

The timing will determine how quickly the fight becomes realistic. Martin wants his autumn bout first, while Muratalla has only recently decided to leave 135. Both being with Top Rank makes the fight relatively easy to put together if their plans eventually cross.

Muratalla would give Martin a credible test as he works toward a title opportunity at 140. Martin would offer something similar for Muratalla, who wants to move directly into meaningful fights rather than spend several bouts working his way into the division.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Praises Andre Ward, But Has He Proven Greatness?
Sports.content:
Shakur never revealed what Ward told him, leaving the advice open to interpretation. His comments, however, sound like they are coming from a fighter who has done it all. Shakur has called himself “the best,” but he hasn’t beaten enough top fighters to make that case.

William Zepeda last year was arguably the closest Stevenson has come to facing one of the elite fighters in his division. Shakur won, but it was hardly a performance that separated him from the field at lightweight. Zepeda connected repeatedly to the body, outworked him for long stretches and forced Stevenson into a difficult fight.

Moving to light welterweight brought another title when Shakur defeated Teofimo Lopez for the WBO belt. It did not make him the clear No. 1 at 140.

Ernesto Mercado has called Stevenson out and claims Shakur blocked him on social media. Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela and Oscar Duarte provide other dangerous options in a division filled with younger, hungry punchers capable of testing the champion physically.

Yet Shakur recently concentrated on moving up again to face WBO welterweight champion Devin Haney while requesting a 144-pound catchweight. Haney refused to surrender three pounds, leaving Shakur frustrated when the fight went nowhere.

Ward retired at 33 in 2017 after consecutive victories over Sergey Kovalev, just as Dmitry Bivol and Artur Beterbiev were becoming major threats at light heavyweight. He had already accomplished far more than Stevenson has today, but his retirement meant those fights never happened. Bivol and Beterbiev later became the dominant fighters at 175 pounds.

Stevenson still has time to take a different route. If Shakur wants to call himself the best, he needs to beat the best fighters available. Rather than asking Haney to come down to 144 pounds, Shakur can prove how good he is against the fighters waiting for him at 140. He can prove it against the fighters in his own division who want his title.

Ghana News.title: Open SOS call to President Mahama for justice
Ghana News.content:
Our elders have said it, owo ka aniberee meaning a snake bites or stings out of frustration or distress.

The last time the Minister of Finance, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, appeared in Parliament, he said, among other things, that there was no arrears and boasted that so much has been saved towards the settlement of the first batch of payments under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP), for which he was highly praised and applauded for the sound management of the economy.

However, because the DDEP was used as a major political tool, the government is doing everything possible to meet commitments.

But that is not the case for some ordinary Ghanaians, who instead of investing their finances in financial instruments or bonds, decided to supply food items under the Free Senior High School Policy in the Fourth Quarter of 2024.

Because of our obsession with partisan politics, our simplistic understanding is that anybody who does business under a certain regime, willy nilly, is a member or fanatic supporter of the political party that is in control under that regime.

However, it is a basic fact that not every such person is a political animal but a prudent individual who wants to deploy their finances prudently.

More imperative, in our country, services and supplies for government business in the fourth quarter, are usually paid for in the First Quarter of the ensuing year.

So, it happened that in September 2024, the Minister of Education, Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum, spoke to me personally to help supply maize to senior high schools in the Ashanti Region.

He did so because most members of the Conference of Heads of Assisted Senior High Schools (CHASS) had recommended a company, Rostella Enterprise, as a dependent, committed and reliable supplier of domestic food items to the schools and the manageress of the company happened to be my wife.

She was initially reluctant but I prevailed upon her, pointing out that the Free SHS programme is one of the most transformative policy initiatives of the government, whose full impact would be realised after more than a decade of implementation, when the literacy rate of the country is assessed.

I also assured her that once it was a government project, payment could not be repudiated by any future government once it was established to be genuine.

As a micro businesswoman, she had more discernment than myself, an innocent public servant who had an idealistic appreciation of our fundamentalist partisanship considerations.

However, after much persuasion, she mobilised resources and supplied the food items.

Her initial fears started to crystalise when the new government in 2025, decided to undertake a forensic audit into those supplies before going on with payments.

Thankfully, the audit was concluded and in July last year, the President announced that all such outstanding payments were to resume.

Both the National Food Buffer Stock Company and the Ghana Commodity Exchange, because of her record and the comments from members of CHASS in the Ashanti Region, encouraged her to register for new supplies, which she did by paying the respective registration fees of GHc5000 each.

However, due to the infantile and puerile thinking that all such suppliers were partisan and loyal to the previous government she has not since been given a contract for supplies.

When implementation commenced and allocations began, otherwise cooperative officials in both institutions became elusive and hostile to her enquires including a comment by one of the key officers at Buffer Stock, that he was not a member of the allocation committee and should not thus be disturbed any more.

A few weeks back, she had assured that she was on the approval been list.

This can only be a reflection of our warped thinking that those who get contracts under a government programme are loyalists or fanatical party supporters.

The irony though is that when public, political and government officials get the opportunity to speak publicly, they openly proffer sentimental nationalistic slogans and regurgitate the false narration that the country belongs to all of us and no one would be excluded from the sharing of the national cake or resources and that government business is not based on nepotism nor partisanship but on competence, quality of work and value for money.

Thus for the past 19 months the debt owed to Rostella Enterprise and others like her, whose only crime was that they did good business with the past administration, have had their money in arrears and each time they call to find out, the refrain is that we are waiting for releases from the Ministry of Finance.

What is devilish is the fact that new suppliers appointed since 2025; ostensibly loyal partisan members of the government are paid from the Ghana Education Trust Fund.

The question is, if government is raising money and depositing it towards the future payments under the DDEP, why has the same government failed to pay for supplies, forensically audited and established to be legitimate.

What the hell is the difference between legitimate food supplied to Ghanaian senior secondary school students under the Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo regime and those supplied under President John Dramani Mahama, if not because of fanatical partisanship consideration.

In an interview on Ghana Television last Tuesday, August 5, the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, my Law Class 2002 mate, pointed out that the uncapped portion of the GETFund, is being applied to pay for food supplies under the Free SHS programme.

During the past administration, when suppliers under the same programme were owed and besieged the offices of Buffer Stock, it became justifiably a political matter and the Speaker of Parliament visited Buffer Stock to understand issues after which he appealed to the government to pay the suppliers, ordinary micro and small scale business men and women.

It worked.

For my part, when the Ministry of Education resorted to what was termed emergency supplies, which attracted prompt payments but cost higher, I complained directly to the Chief of Staff to draw her attention to the injustice and the travesty of the act, where those who had their supplies in arrears were paid less whilst emergency suppliers who were paid promptly received higher.

She agreed with my submission that things bought on credit must cost more than those paid for instantly.

Things began to work thereafter.

Personally, what this government, through the Ministry of Finance has done to me is that, they have beaten me and compelled me from crying, but “anka wonua womu a yennyi wo mfiri mu.”

It is simple.

Beyond not paying my wife, as Chairman of the National Media Commission from 2018 to 2024, since the last Commission ended its tenure on December 24, 2024, we have not received our arrears for 2022, 2023 and 2024 although new members have been paid part of their allowance since they assumed duty in May 2025.

The Minister of Finance and his colleagues who were MPs together with other Article 71 office holders have received their full salary arrears together with ex gratia awards whilst members of the NMC, the least remunerated among Article 71 office holders, are waiting endlessly for payment.

Members of the NMC are unqualified for ex gratia because they are said to be part-time, although Council of State members, equally non-permanent, receive ex gratia, as per the denunciation made by Togbe Afede, against the lodgement of ex gratia money into his account some time ago.

Whenever any of the former members of the NMC call me as Chairman to find out when the arrears would be paid, I call the accountant who keeps on telling me that they had not heard from the Ministry of Finance although the ministry collected the details for the payment in March 2025.

Nsuo fono aponkyereni a ogye woo and more so, se kokoram amfere se obeto wo nan ho a wo nso wo mfere se wode asaawa anaa ntomago bekyekyere so.

That is why I am openly appealing and reaching out to my former Roommate President John Dramani Mahama to ensure that justice is done to the previous NMC members, and more so, suppliers under the Free SHS programme, whose supplies have been in arrears since September 2024, knowing that it is the tradition of our country to meet outstanding payments from the Fourth Quarter in the First Quarter of the ensuing year, and especially because all funds sitting in the accounts of public agencies between January and March 2025 were swept back into the Consolidated Fund at the end of March as it is usual.

By: Yaw Boadu Ayeboafo

Ghana News.title: Sir Sam Jonah takes Abuja land dispute with Nigeria to ICC arbitration
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian businessman and mining executive Sir Sam Jonah has commenced international arbitration proceedings against the Nigerian government over a 501-hectare property in Abuja, escalating a long-running dispute over one of his major investments outside Ghana.

The case, being heard under the auspices of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) in Paris, concerns the termination of a development lease covering the property near the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport.

The investment is held through JonahCapital Nigeria Limited, a subsidiary of Sir Sam Jonah’s investment group. The financial value of the claim has not been publicly disclosed, although estimates have put the value of the property at about US$500 million based on prevailing property values in Abuja.

River Park Estate at centre of dispute

At the heart of the dispute is Plot 4 in Cadastral Zone E30, Lugbe West, a 501-hectare parcel allocated to JonahCapital in 2007 under Nigeria’s Mass Housing Scheme.

The company subsequently developed the property into River Park Estate, a major residential and mixed-use development featuring homes, commercial facilities, healthcare centres, offices and places of worship.

JonahCapital maintains that its development lease was due to remain in force until June 2030.

The Federal Capital Development Authority (FCDA), however, terminated the lease in November 2025. JonahCapital has challenged the decision, describing the termination as unlawful and contrary to the terms of the development agreement.

Infrastructure costs

In its case, JonahCapital contends that Nigerian authorities failed to meet several obligations under the agreement.

The company says the FCDA did not provide key infrastructure, including roads, electricity and water, leaving the developer to finance and construct the facilities at significant cost.

It has also raised concerns about building approval fees and alleged that sections of the disputed property have been fenced off while the arbitration process is underway.

JonahCapital further claims that the development has faced ownership claims from third parties, resulting in years of legal and administrative challenges.

The allegations are yet to be determined by the arbitration tribunal.

Wike: ‘Let arbitration take its course’

Nigeria’s Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has confirmed that the matter has been taken to arbitration and said the government would respect the process.

“The other party has gone to arbitration, and we say, 'Okay, until you finish from arbitration,'" he said.

Mr Wike has maintained that the government acted lawfully in recovering the property after the expiry of the lease.

He has also disputed aspects of the development, arguing that some of the projects in question were undertaken by Paulo Homes Limited, a separate company engaged by JonahCapital to facilitate certain approvals.

Criminal proceedings

The commercial dispute is running alongside a separate criminal case involving Sir Sam Jonah and several other individuals before the Federal Capital Territory High Court.

The 26-count case includes allegations of forgery of company documents and the unlawful allocation of shares in companies associated with the Abuja development.

Sir Sam Jonah has denied the allegations. The charges are yet to be determined by the court.

Ghana intervenes

The dispute has also drawn the attention of the Ghanaian government amid concerns about the protection of Ghanaian investments in Nigeria.

In late 2025, Sir Sam Jonah petitioned Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, over what he described as actions by Nigerian regulatory authorities that threatened his interests in the investment.

Mr Ablakwa subsequently raised concerns about the treatment of Ghanaian businesses operating in Nigeria at an ECOWAS Council of Ministers meeting in Abuja, citing the JonahCapital dispute.

The Foreign Affairs Minister had earlier visited River Park Estate and expressed support for efforts to safeguard Ghanaian investments abroad.

Why the ICC case matters

By taking the dispute to ICC arbitration, JonahCapital has opted for an international dispute-resolution mechanism rather than relying solely on Nigeria’s domestic courts.

International commercial arbitration is widely used in cross-border investment disputes and can provide a mechanism for parties to resolve contractual disagreements before an independent tribunal.

The arbitration hearing date has not yet been announced, while the related criminal proceedings in Nigeria remain pending.

Sir Sam Jonah is among Ghana's most prominent business figures. He rose to prominence through the transformation of Ashanti Goldfields Company into one of Africa’s leading mining companies and later became President of AngloGold Ashanti following the 2004 merger between Ashanti Goldfields and AngloGold.

He subsequently expanded his business interests into sectors including mining, energy and real estate across Africa.

The Abuja development remains one of his major property investments outside Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian paediatric oncologist Dr. Emmanuella Amoako wins 2026 Roux Prize
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian paediatric oncologist Dr. Emmanuella Amoako has been named the recipient of the 2026 Roux Prize, becoming the first Ghanaian to win the prestigious global award for outstanding contributions to population health.

The award, announced by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington, recognises individuals who demonstrate exceptional use of health evidence and data to improve the lives of populations.

Dr. Amoako was honoured for her work in advancing childhood cancer care, particularly efforts aimed at promoting early diagnosis, improving access to treatment and strengthening survival outcomes for children diagnosed with cancer.

Her work has focused significantly on strengthening paediatric oncology services at the Cape Coast Teaching Hospital, where she has championed measures to improve the early detection of childhood cancers, referral pathways and access to specialised care.

IHME said her contribution illustrates the importance of translating health data and locally generated evidence into practical interventions, particularly in resource-constrained settings where access to specialised childhood cancer services remains a challenge.

As part of the recognition, Dr. Amoako will receive a US$100,000 prize for her contribution to improving population health through evidence-based approaches.

Her achievement adds to a growing list of recognitions for her work in healthcare delivery. She was recently named among Channel One TV’s Top 10 Community Legends, an initiative that celebrates individuals whose work has made a significant difference in their communities.

The Roux Prize was established in 2013 by philanthropists David and Barbara Roux to honour individuals who have demonstrated exceptional impact in population health through the innovative application of health evidence and data.

Dr. Amoako’s recognition places the spotlight on the potential of evidence-driven healthcare interventions developed within Ghana to address major health challenges and improve outcomes for vulnerable groups, particularly children.

Her work in paediatric oncology has also highlighted the importance of timely diagnosis and coordinated referral systems in improving the prospects of children with cancer, especially where specialist services are limited.

The 2026 award therefore represents not only a personal milestone for Dr. Amoako but also a significant recognition of Ghanaian expertise in using evidence to strengthen healthcare delivery.

Ghana News.title: Kingsley Atta secures Bantama NPP Chairmanship with slim 4-vote victory in re-run
Ghana News.content:
Delegates of the New Patriotic Party in the Bantama Constituency have elected Kingsley Atta as the new Constituency Chairman in a keenly contested re-run election held on Saturday, August 8, 2026, at the Kumasi Cultural Centre.

Mr. Atta secured victory with a slim margin of 4 votes, defeating his closest contender, Fiifi Mensah, in an election supervised by officials of the Electoral Commission and observed by national and regional executives of the NPP.

In certified results declared by the EC’s Returning Officer, Kingsley Atta polled 570 votes representing 50.2%, whilst the incumbent Chairman, Fiifi Mensah, obtained 566 votes, representing 49.8%.

The tight margin marks a sharp contrast to the annulled election held on Sunday, July 12, 2026, where Mr. Atta had won by a landslide.

The re-run followed the NPP’s National Steering Committee’s decision to annul the initial constituency executive election, citing breaches of party directives and electoral regulations.

In that election, Kingsley Atta defeated the incumbent Chairman, Fiifi Mensah, with 714 votes, representing 72.8% of the 995 valid votes cast. Fiifi Mensah obtained 267 votes, representing 27.2%.

Addressing delegates after his victory, the newly elected Chairman, Kingsley Atta, expressed gratitude to delegates for the confidence reposed in him despite the significant reduction in the number of votes he received compared to the initial election.

“Today, the delegates have spoken. I am humbled by this mandate. The numbers may be different, but the task ahead is the same,” he said.

He pledged to prioritise unity within the party and work to deliver victory for the NPP in the Bantama Constituency in the 2028 general elections.

“We cannot afford to go into 2028 divided. I will be Chairman for all, and my door is open to everyone, including my brother Fiifi. To my supporters, let us celebrate with decorum. This victory belongs to the party,” Mr. Atta added.

In a show of sportsmanship, the outgoing Chairman, Fiifi Mensah, walked straight to the seat of the newly-elected Chairman, Kingsley Atta, and hugged him in a warm handshake.

He congratulated Mr. Atta and all the newly elected executive members on their victory.

Mr. Atta described the gesture as a sign of maturity and unity.

In an interview with the media, Fiifi Mensah pledged to sustain his efforts to help the party secure victory in the next general elections, despite his defeat.

“I accept the verdict of the delegates in good faith. The decision has been made, and I respect it. I will remain committed to the party and will do all I can to ensure victory for the party in 2028,” he added.

Reacting to the annulled election, he said the re-run result had vindicated his claim that the first election was not conducted fairly.

“The outcome of today’s re-run has only confirmed what we raised from the beginning. That election was conducted on unfair grounds and did not reflect the true will of the delegates. In that election I lost by 447 votes, but in today’s election I lost by only 4 votes,” he stated.

Delegates also elected Vincent Kofi Amoabeng as First Vice Chairman, Frank Boateng as Second Vice Chairman, Douglas Acheampong (Unopposed) as Constituency Secretary, Kwadwo Adu as Assistant Secretary, and Eric Mensah as Constituency Organiser.

The remaining elected officers include Nana Boakye as Youth Organiser, Vivian Arthur as Treasurer, Josephine Ama Poma as Women's Organiser, Kingsford Addai as Communications Director, and Afram Tuffour as Nasara Coordinator.

Representatives of the Ashanti Regional and National Executives, as well as the Member of Parliament for Bantama, Francis Asenso-Boakye, were present to observe the process.

They expressed satisfaction with how the re-run was conducted.

Speaking after the results were declared, the Bantama MP, Francis Asenso-Boakye, congratulated the winner and urged all members to unite behind the new executives.

"The time for division is over. The focus now is on unity. Whoever won or lost, we must all rally behind one goal to work together to make Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia the next president in the 2028 general elections in order to continue the good works and legacy of President Akufo-Addo,” the MP stated.

He commended delegates for conducting themselves peacefully and thanked the Electoral Commission and security agencies for ensuring a transparent process.

The new executives are expected to take office in the coming days to immediately begin reorganizing the constituency and mobilising support for the NPP’s flagbearer, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, ahead of the 2028 elections.

Ghana News.title: Hormuz talks positive, Oman says, as Iran warns deal would not open strait
Ghana News.content:
Oman has said positive talks have been taking place with Iran over an agreement to secure a shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, as Tehran warned that any deal would not see an immediate reopening of the vital waterway.

Both sides suggested on Saturday that discussions were progressing, but a timeline on any deal being finalised remained unclear. Oman's foreign ministry warned against attacks on shipping that could hamper that.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said talks were in their final stages but the reopening of the strait remained "subject to other conditions".

Tehran has effectively blockaded the waterway, through which around a fifth of the world's oil and natural gas usually flows, since the US and Israel began attacking it in February.

Talks in recent days have focused on the possibility of a deal between Iran and Oman on a new route through the strait, which they would both have responsibility for and is hoped would lead to progress in resuming shipping traffic.

But Araghchi said a full reopening of the typically busy maritime route depended on other conditions being met, of which he provided a cursory appraisal.

He said the conditions included Iran receiving compensation from the US for what Tehran described as violations of the deal both sides signed in June to cease fighting and advance talks to end the war.

That deal - called a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) - quickly fell through, as did diplomatic talks, with tit-for-tat attacks resuming just days after it was signed.

Separately, Mohammad Baqer Zolqadr, Iran's security chief, told the semi-official news agency Tasnim that the Strait of Hormuz would not reopen until the US "corrects" its behaviour.

He said the US needed to meet six Iranian demands, including a halt to threats against Iran, removal of its naval blockade of Iranian ports and release of Iran's frozen assets.

Another blockade, on Saudi Arabia's ports in the Red Sea, had been imposed by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis since 20 July.

Earlier this week, US President Donald Trump said a deal with Iran "could be soon", but Vice-President JD Vance appeared to be more sceptical on Saturday, telling Fox News that work remained to be done even if progress was being made.

"We're really in the middle of the game here," he said. "This thing is not over."

Vance added that "we're applying a whole host of tools - diplomatic, economic [and] military tools - to ensure that we get the best outcome for the American people".

Additionally, he claimed that the "same amount of oil" will emerge from the Gulf as did before the US military operation began on 28 February, although he offered no details.

"What we're really working through now is how you can actually set up a traffic scheme so that the ships can pass through safely," he added.

One of the main points of disagreement between Tehran and Washington has been Iran's reported threat to impose a fee on vessels wishing to cross the strait.

Reuters - citing an Iranian official - previously reported that Tehran was seeking fees of between 5% and 7% of the price of cargoes from vessels who travel through it.

Vance downplayed those reports, saying: "The Iranians have told us they have no plans to toll the Strait of Hormuz."

Oman's warning against attacks on ships in the strait came as the United Arab Emirates (UAE) said on Saturday that Iran had targeted a tanker affiliated with Adnoc, its state-owned oil company, as it passed through.

The UAE's foreign ministry said in a statement that a "hostile Iranian attack" had hit an Adnoc tanker "with a missile". It added that there were no casualties.

Later on Saturday, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency also reported a ship being struck by "an unknown projectile" off the coast of Oman, causing "a fire that has been extinguished" but no casualties.

It is unclear whether UKMTO was referring to the same ship as the UAE.

Ghana News.title: Nestlé Ghana launches ‘My Coffee, My Vibe’ campus activation
Ghana News.content:
Nestlé Ghana has launched its latest Nescafé campaign, ‘My Coffee, My Vibe’, at the University of Ghana, Legon, as part of efforts to connect with young consumers through music, talent and self-expression.

The activation, held on Friday, August 7, attracted thousands of students who took part in various activities while enjoying Nescafé.

The event featured singing and dancing performances from students, creating a lively atmosphere on campus.

Popular dancer Dancegod Lloyd also made a surprise appearance with his team, delivering a performance that drew excitement from the crowd.

Ghanaian singer and songwriter Adina Thembi also made a surprise appearance, performing some of her songs to the delight of students.

Speaking to the media after the event, Category Development Manager for Nescafé Ghana, Lily Boatemaa Ntim, said the campaign was designed to make coffee part of the lifestyle of young consumers.

“My Coffee, My Vibe is a targeted project that today is a new campaign that we want to outdoor to be able to meet our target consumers where they are most comfortable.

“We want coffee not to be a stimulation or an afterthought but something that is part of their lifestyle, something that is, in quotes, indulgent.”

She said the decision to take the campaign to university campuses was deliberate, as students form a key part of Nescafé’s target market.

Mrs Ntim said the campaign would also provide a platform for young people to showcase their talents by linking coffee consumption with their interests and passions.

“We didn't want to just come here talking about our new communication which doesn't make sense to them.

“But we wanted to merge it into self-expression. We wanted to merge it into what they know best, which is their passion, because that's how they express themselves.”

As part of the campaign, the brand will visit the University of Cape Coast (UCC) and Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), in addition to the University of Ghana.

Students will compete in singing and dancing, with winners eventually battling it out for the top prizes.

According to Mrs Ntim, winners in the respective categories will receive GH¢30,000 in cash as well as mentorship opportunities.

She said the campaign is aimed at recruiting new consumers, showcasing young talent and engaging students in an environment where they feel most comfortable.

“So My Coffee, My Vibe is an activity, one to recruit people into the brand and also to help them showcase their talent through this talent hunt that we are doing.”

“We have the winner for dance and the winner for singing. So that's what My Coffee, My Vibe is about. It's a new campaign that Nescafé is doing.”

She said the campaign would continue across the selected campuses as Nestlé Ghana seeks to deepen its engagement with young consumers.

“One, to bring their culture in. And two, to also recruit. Three, to meet our target consumers where they are most comfortable, which is on campus.”

Ghana News.title: US offers $1bn to Colombia on new right-wing president’s first day of office
Ghana News.content:
The US has pledged $1bn (£740m) to Colombia hours after the country's new right-wing populist president was sworn in.

Abelardo de la Espriella, an admirer of Donald Trump who echoed many of the US president's policies on the campaign trail, used his maiden speech to promise an "all-out war" on drug cartels.

The US state department said the "security package" would help him achieve "our shared goals", which include fighting organised crime and illegal immigration. Trump repeatedly criticised de la Espriella's left-wing predecessor over his approach to both.

The inauguration is the latest in a wider trend of Latin American nations shifting rightwards on a backdrop of economic hardship and concerns about gang violence.

Trump has taken a greater interest in Latin America during his second term, courting politically aligned leaders and spurning those with whom he disagrees.

Before the election, Trump said de la Espriella had the "total support and strength of the United States behind him", predicting a "much better relationship" with Colombia after he was elected in June.

A lawyer and businessman by trade, de la Espriella has cast himself as maverick outsider, vowing to combat crime with an "iron fist".

In a fiery first official speech - addressing troops at a nearby military base - de la Espriella pledged to crush armed insurgents, rebuild Colombia and defend democracy "by reason or by force".

He said in "the age of the Tiger" - a reference to his self-styled nickname - the state would be forceful and decisive against crime, adding: "There will not be a single place in our territory where criminals can feel safe."

Comparisons have been drawn between de la Espriella's plans and similar crackdowns by similar right-wing populists Nayib Bukele and Daniel Noboa in El Salvador and Ecuador, respectively.

This is in stark contrast to his predecessor, Gustavo Petro, whopursued what he called a "total peace" strategy to the country's internal armed conflict between guerrilla groups, the state and cartels, which prioritised negotiation and incentivising farmers to stop planting coca.

Critics say the method failed. Membership of armed groups has expanded in recent years, and a brutal conflict between rival rebel groups along the Colombia-Venezuela border displaced tens of thousands of people last year.

Colombia - and Petro's policies - have been among targets Trump has repeatedly blamed for the flow of drugs and illegal migrants into the US.

De la Espriella has pledged to abandon his predecessor's "total peace" approach to armed gangs

Petro, for his part, was highly critical of Trump's influence on the region, as well as his administration's seizure of Venezuela's socialist PresidentNicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, to stand trial on drug charges in the US, clearing the way for US firms to tap Venezuela's oil reserves.

Petro, who could not stand for another term, and Iván Cepeda, the left-wing candidate he backed, had insisted Colombia should not become another "vassal" of the US.

In one of his first acts as president, de la Espriella said Colombia would join the "Shield of the Americas" security partnership founded by Trump.

The US state department welcomed the move, saying de la Espriella's "pro-growth agenda" had created an opportunity to "increase trade and deepen economic ties between our countries".

It also brings Colombia into league with other right-wing governments that have sought closer ties to the Trump administration, such as Argentina, whose libertarian President Javier Milei de le Espriella has said he admired.

Argentina was the recipient of a $20bn US Treasury bailout, while Trump has said he would feel "a lot differently" about supporting the country if Milei was replaced by a left-wing president.

In contrast, Trump has repeatedly threatened to give Cuba's Communist government similar treatment to Maduro's in Venezuela.

De la Espriella's ascension - along with that of Keiko Fujimori in Peru - means that Brazil's Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva now has fewer political allies in the region as the number of left-wing leaders dwindles.

However, he will face Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of jailed former President Jair Bolsonaro - a far-right populist friendly with the US president - in October.

De la Espriella has also promised a strong military alliance with the US and Israel, in stark contrast to Petro, who cut ties with the Israeli government over its offensive in Gaza and was a vocal advocate for the Palestinian cause.

Who is Abelardo de la Espriella?

He calls himself "El Tigre" - the tiger.

A media-savvy lawyer and millionaire businessman, he cast himself as an "outsider" who refused to govern with "the usual suspects" - a reference to Colombia's pre-Petro political elite.

The hardliner chose to take the oath of office not in Colombia's capital, Bogotá, but in the western city of Cali - signalling his desire to cast himself as apart from the centralised politics of the past.

Before entering politics, he had a successful career as a defence lawyer representing drug-trafficking paramilitaries - the kinds of criminals he now intends to lock up.

De la Espriella announced his candidacy a month after another conservative candidate was shot and killed, and regularly appeared at rallies behind bulletproof glass wearing a bulletproof vest - if not a Colombian football jersey.

He has been a US citizen since 2023 after living and working in Miami for many years.

Among attendees of his inauguration was US Attorney General Todd Blanche and Fifa president Gianni Infantino, who was accompanied by the head of South America's football governing body Conmebol as questions linger over his leadership.
