World.title: Police arrest 10 suspected cultists, recover gun, cannabis seeds
World.content:
The police in Akwa Ibom State have arrested 10 suspected cultists and recovered a locally made pistol, machete, charms, suspected cannabis sativa seeds and cult regalia.

Five suspects were arrested on 4 August at Akpautong Village, Esit Eket Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom, following credible intelligence and an investigation into cult-related activities, the police spokeswoman in the state, Timfon John, said in a statement sent to this newspaper on Saturday.

Ms John, a deputy superintendent of police, identified the suspects as Benjamin James, Moses Asuquo, Isaac Jimmy, Akaniyene Ekpo and Aniekan Samuel, all residents of the community.

Police said a search during the operation led to the recovery of a locally made pistol, charms, a machete, a Point-of-Sale machine, suspected cannabis sativa seeds and N400,000.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Five arrested after alleged cult gathering

In a separate operation, police arrested five other suspects after responding to a distress call about an alleged cult gathering at a guest house on 31 July.

Ms John identified the arrested suspects as Destiny Moses, 20; Boniface Clement, 23; Raphael Offiong, 27; Victor Obot, 27; and Sunday Victor, 23.

She said the group allegedly shot sporadically into the air, causing panic in the area.

A red Mercedes-Benz C300 with visible bullet damage, a jack knife wrapped with a red ribbon, two face caps bearing insignia of a proscribed cult group and three empty bottles of alcoholic beverages were recovered, the police said.

Preliminary investigation, according to the police, indicates that the suspects belong to the proscribed Supreme Vikings Confraternity, also known as De Norsemen Klan.

The police in Akwa Ibom have made several cult-related arrests recently.

In July, police arrested three suspected members of the Vikings Confraternity during a raid on an alleged cult hideout off Abak Road, Uyo, recovering substances suspected to be methamphetamine and cannabis.

Police said the suspects admitted membership of the group, while one was allegedly forcibly initiated during a ceremony at the location.

In June, three suspects were detained over alleged armed robbery and cultism. Police had said officers recovered locally made pistols, a live cartridge and a machete during separate operations in Abak and Etinan. Two suspects allegedly admitted belonging to a four-member armed robbery gang.

In May, police also announced the arrest of two suspected cultists in Ikot Ekpene, recovering a locally made shotgun, two live cartridges and a suspected protective charm. One suspect allegedly confessed membership of the proscribed Ku Klux Klans Confraternity.

World.title: Can NDC Resolve Growing Concerns in Abia State Before 2027?
World.content:
By Phillip Ogbonna

As Nigeria gradually moves toward the 2027 general elections, political parties are expected to strengthen their internal structures, inspire confidence among their members, and present themselves as credible alternatives to the electorate. In Abia State, however, concerns are beginning to emerge within the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), prompting important discussions about fairness, inclusiveness, internal democracy, and the party’s electoral strategy.

Across various parts of the state, conversations among party members have increasingly focused on whether recent decisions concerning the allocation of party tickets reflect the principles of equity, justice, and balanced representation that many believe should guide a growing political movement. While every political party has the right to nominate candidates it considers best positioned to win elections, many stakeholders maintain that the selection process should also foster unity and ensure that all communities feel fairly represented.

One issue receiving considerable attention is the situation in the Abia North Senatorial District, particularly within the Arochukwu axis. According to concerns raised by some party members, both the House of Representatives ticket and the Abia State House of Assembly ticket were reportedly allocated to aspirants from Atani community in Arochukwu. Critics argue that this decision overlooked the aspirant who reportedly emerged victorious in the NDC primary election for the Arochukwu State Constituency and is from Ututu, a clan that, according to supporters, has never produced a member of the Abia State House of Assembly and is widely believed to be due for the opportunity under the principle of political rotation. Although party leaders may have had reasons for their decisions, critics contend that such an arrangement could create perceptions of exclusion among other communities that have equally invested their time, resources, and commitment in building the party.

For many political observers, candidate selection goes beyond choosing individuals for elective office. It is also about managing diversity, promoting inclusiveness, and strengthening public confidence in the party’s internal democratic processes. When committed members begin to question whether fairness and equity have been adequately considered, party leaders have a responsibility to engage with those concerns openly and transparently.

Several stakeholders argue that concentrating key elective positions within a single community may unintentionally weaken the sense of belonging among supporters from other villages and wards. They warn that members who feel marginalized may become less motivated during campaigns, potentially reducing the grassroots support that often determines the outcome of closely contested elections. Political success is rarely achieved through individual popularity alone; it is built on collective effort, shared ownership, and the confidence that every stakeholder has a meaningful place within the party.

These concerns are reportedly not limited to Arochukwu alone. Similar questions surrounding zoning, political balance, and candidate selection have allegedly emerged in other parts of Abia State. Many party members believe that addressing these issues proactively would strengthen, rather than weaken, the NDC. They point to dialogue, transparency, and genuine reconciliation as proven approaches that have enabled political parties to overcome internal disagreements ahead of major elections.

Those advocating for a review insist that their position should not be interpreted as opposition to the party. Rather, they describe their concerns as a constructive appeal for reforms that would make the NDC more united, inclusive, and electorally competitive. They argue that overlooking widely accepted and popular aspirants could diminish the party’s appeal in communities where local acceptance and grassroots support are essential to electoral success. The questions being raised by many members are straightforward yet significant. Is the NDC making decisions that maximize its chances of electoral success across Abia State? Has sufficient consideration been given to equity, inclusiveness, political acceptability, and long-term electoral strategy? Most importantly, can the party reassure its members that every aspirant received fair and equal consideration throughout the nomination process?

These are legitimate questions that deserve thoughtful and transparent responses. Successful political parties understand that unity cannot simply be demanded; it must be built through fairness, accountability, transparency, and mutual respect. Members who dedicate their time, resources, and commitment to building a political platform naturally expect decisions that reflect the collective interest rather than the interests of a select few.

As preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum, many loyal party faithful believe this is the appropriate time for both the national and state leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress to engage members openly, clarify the rationale behind key decisions, and reassure stakeholders that the party remains committed to justice, equity, inclusiveness, and internal democracy. Such engagement could help restore confidence, ease tensions, and reinforce the unity required to effectively compete in the forthcoming elections.

Ultimately, elections are won not only through campaign promises but also through the level of confidence, cohesion, and trust that exists within a political party. How the Nigeria Democratic Congress responds to these growing concerns in Abia State may ultimately determine whether it enters the 2027 general elections as a united political force capable of inspiring voters or as a party still grappling with avoidable internal divisions.

World.title: Interior Minister’s achievements have projected youths positively
World.content:
Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo

By Saka Ola Ahmed

The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, achievements in his ministry in the last three years have created a positive image for youths in the country and have shown that, when given responsibility , they can excel.

The unprecedented positive performance so far in the Ministry of Interior by the Minister has given everyone hope that the youths can successfully lead and rule the country.

It is the belief of many, therefore , that the Minister is currently the most suitable person to facilitate the development of Ondo State, where he is from.

Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, Minister of Interior, is a Nigerian engineer, entrepreneur, philanthropist, and politician . He was a member of the House of Representatives representing Akoko North East/Akoko North West Federal Constituency of Ondo State from 2019 to 2023.

Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo was appointed minister by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in August 2023. His ministry oversees the Nigeria Immigration Service, Nigerian Correctional Service, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), and Federal Fire Service.

The Minister has been honoured by different organisations for introducing important reforms, which are very beneficial.

These include the digitization of the passport application process, deployment of airport e-Gates, and initiatives to clear extensive passport backlogs.

In correctional service, he has pioneered major decongestion efforts at correctional centres by spearheading. programmes that paid fines to release thousands of inmates held for petty offences, alongside modernizing facilities.

On Border and Asset Security, Hon Tunji-Ojo has focused on integrating intelligence data, enhancing border security, and using the NSCDC to protect critical national infrastructure.

During his first term in the House of Representatives, he was the chairman of the House Committee on Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC). On 26 February 2023, he was re-elected as the federal lawmaker representing Akoko North East and North West Federal Constituency. However, he resigned his membership of the lower chamber of the National Assembly after being appointed by President Bola Tinubu as minister of Interior on 16 August 2023.

Before going into politics, Tunji-Ojo was a business and management executive with a career in ICT, becoming the CEO of a leading indigenous ICT consultant company in Nigeria, Matrix IT Solutions Limited, at the age of 24.

As a professional, he holds a certification in Ethical Hacking and Counter Measures. He is also a certified CompTIA Network Plus Engineer and a Britannia Hardware A+ Management Certificate Holder.

His introduction of contactless passport renewal system for Nigerians living in Europe has endeared him to Nigerians in the diaspora. The system allows eligible Nigerians in Europe to renew their passports online without visiting any physical office, following the successful rollout of the initiative in Canada.

The Minister has helped in fighting insecurity in the country.

To further strengthen border surveillance, 30 new patrol vehicles have been commissioned, while a new Command and Control Centre, housing a 1.4 petabyte-capacity data center, has been constructed at the Nigerian Immigration Service, NIS, headquarters in Abuja.

The Ministry has also activated the role of Document Verification Officers (DVOs) to authenticate passport applicants from their local government areas.

Technological advancement has been a key focus of the Minister, culminating in the commissioning of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu Technology Innovation Complex (BATTIC) on the 11th of December,2024. The facility houses the NIS Command and Control Center, ECOWAS Biometric Card Production Centre, the Interior Data Centre, the Visa Application Centre, and a solar farm.

For his efforts and achievements, Dr Tunji-Ojo was named amongst the 30 most influential young Nigerians by the National Youth Council of Nigeria in 2019.

He was also awarded as Pacesetter in Political Representation by Akoko North West Local Government Council, Okeagbe Akoko, Ondo State , in 2019.

He got the Sir Ahmadu Bello Platinum Leadership Award of Excellence in 2019,

National Assembly Best Legislator of the year in 2020, 2021, and the

Kwame Nkrumah Leadership Award as “Worthy Ambassador of African 2010 Youth” by All African Students Union ,(AASU).

World.title: Chinda most suitable for Rivers Brick House
World.content:
Kingsley Chinda

By Caleb Ekesunnie

Rt. Hon. Kingsley Ogundu Chinda current member of the House of Representatives, representing Obio/ Akpor Federal Constituency, Rivers State has been in the news lately for good reasons. He emerged a few months ago as the Rivers State gubernatorial candidate of All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 general elections . He is the immediate past Minority Leader of the current 10th House of Representatives.

He has used his over a decade and half stints in the National Assembly to demonstrate his preparedness to occupy the Rivers Brick House in a remarkable manner. As minority leader of the House, he showed his leadership dexterities to the admiration of his colleagues by introducing a brand of opposition leadership style that was largely innovative, moderate and strategic.

Accordingly, Chinda provided an alternative legislative governance model that is inherently harmonious as a result boosted the bargaining power of members of the opposition in the House. This creative leadership paradigm distinguished him so exceedingly in the House.

He remains one of the most outspoken members of the House. Chinda always finds his voice on the floor of the House and is one of the notable lawmakers who have contributed immensely in reshaping National Assembly as an institution in a considerable manner.

Besides his exceptional leadership style, since 2011 he has been in the House Chinda has demonstrated unmatched legislative results. These productive legislative years at the National Assembly obviously accounted for his chain of re-elections into the legislative house

His legislative governance abilities and prowess in the areas of parliamentary debates, processes, oversight functions , motions and Bills pursuits are uncommon. This legislative record underlines Chinda as one of the foremost Nigerian parliamentarians

Over the years in NASS, Chinda has chaired the Public Accounts Committee of the House of Representatives and served as leader of the opposition before he decamped to the ruling APC.

The vast experience he has obtained from legislative stewardship would be the gain of his Rivers people when elected and accordingly sworn in as Governor balanced, visionary and forthright, Chinda is known for his collegial, consensual and positive approach to governance. As a team player he would enlist the buy-in of a wide spectrum of Rivers people to fast-pace the state development when elected.

As a leading parliamentarian, Chinda has imbibed legislative principles of collectivity, consensus and compromise. He would obviously bring these democratic virtues to fore when he takes charge at the Brick House when elected and sworn in, Chinda would prove to Rivers people that a robust background in the legislature is indispensable to drive state development. Chinda would certainly break barriers, dismantle bureaucracy and its hurdles and delays to put infrastructures in place in the state Chinda would not spend his first hundred days wrestling with structural gridlock, fighting with the members of the state legislature. He has enough experience to tame the initial challenges

As a legislator, Chinda has for years watched endless brilliant ideas die in legislative committees, unutilized due to institutional wrangling to the detriment of the people; when he becomes Governor such ideas would be brought to fore for utilization for the benefit of Rivers people having groomed on executive/legislative relationship management over time.

In bringing this time-honed legislative experience to bear on state responsibilities and imperatives, he would not just build roads and fund social services, he would ochestrate and build statutory architecture that endures and outlives his administration. This would be achieved through the introduction of state laws that would be best focused on needs assessment and reform development strategy .

When elected, Chinda would treat every major development initiative and goal as permanent piece of policy tightly engineered to anchor and sustain executive strategy in the overall interest of Rivers people.

Honourable Chinda is not new to the dynamics and workings of the executive arm of government; he had been a Commissioner for Environment where he effectively used state-level authority to regulate what was within the legal jurisdiction of the federal government by implementing actionable state environmental laws as it partains to waste generation and management of local and industrial pollution by forcing the bounds of federal actors with regards to continuous gas flaring and emissions, enforcement of strict compliance with environmental impact assessments (EIAs) for state-level infrastructure works through litigation, formal petitions, regulations and above all sustained citizen enlightenment and sensitisation.

He would therefore be symbolic of converging executive and legislative action, a melting-pot of a formidable experience of both the executive and legislative arms of government.

It is worthy to note that he is an astute lawyer, a human and civil rights advocate with a bias in public interest advocacy committed to fighting systemic injustice and underseved communities, giving voice to the voiceless, indigents and individuals living in poverty, marginalised or minority communities, non- profit organizations and charities as well as environmental rights’ groups and a host of others.

With his vast experience in governance, legislative responsibilities and civil society sector, Rt Hon Kingsley Chinda is indeed most fitting to serve and save Rivers State today. He represents Rivers brand and pearl. The votes of Rivers people for him would strengthen his resolve to bring unprecedented and positive change to the oil rich state.

World.title: GLO@23: The Bull still reigns supreme
World.content:
Adenuga Mike

By Bodex Hungbo

In a corporate world where corporate giants regularly swap boardrooms like trading cards and sell off equity at the first sign of volatility, one legendary tycoon continues to prove that absolute control is the ultimate power move. That man is Otunba Mike Adenuga Jr., the visionary billionaire whose dense belief in indigenous enterprise gave birth to Globacom, the telecom powerhouse affectionately known across the continent as Glo.

As Globacom marks a monumental 23-year milestone, the spotlight shines brightly not only on the company’s extraordinary ascent, but on the enduring legacy of its founder. Adenuga stands as the only Nigerian to establish, nurture, and retain 100% sole ownership of a national telecommunications network; one that has evolved into one of Africa’s most recognizable, resilient, and influential brands.

While rival networks scrambled through endless corporate restructuring, foreign buyouts, hostile takeovers, and high-stakes rebrandings, “The Bull” pulled off what many in international finance considered impossible; holding complete control of Nigeria’s proudest homegrown tech giant for over two decades without surrendering a single inch of authority.

From the very beginning, Adenuga refused to follow the standard playbook written by foreign multinationals. When Globacom officially launched in August 2003, the market was heavily dominated by well-funded international operators who insisted that certain consumer-friendly models were economically impossible in Africa. Skeptics openly declared that a wholly indigenous, single-owner startup could never go toe-to-toe with established global giants.

Adenuga didn’t just compete; he single-handedly revolutionized the entire landscape.

At a time when competitors claimed that charging consumers per second rather than per minute was technically unfeasible, Glo introduced per-second billing on day one. By charging 1 kobo per second, Globacom shattered the status quo overnight, forcing the entire telecom industry to follow suit. That single disruptive move democratized mobile access, saved everyday Nigerians billions of Naira, and transformed mobile phones from luxury items for the elite into essential tools for the masses.

Adenuga’s commitment to self-reliance went far beyond marketing strategies; it was backed by monumental capital investments in hard infrastructure. To ensure that Glo would never be beholden to external actors, he funded game-changing projects directly from his own vision and capital.

Chief among these milestones was the construction of Glo-1, a multi-million-dollar, high-capacity submarine fiber-optic cable stretching over 9,800 kilometers directly from the United Kingdom to Nigeria. Single-handedly funded without taking a single dollar in foreign equity, Glo-1 provided West Africa with unprecedented broadband capacity, drastically improving internet speeds, powering corporate enterprises, and anchoring the region’s digital economy.

Alongside this undersea marvel, Globacom built an extensive terrestrial fiber-optic backbone across Nigeria, expanding coverage into underserved rural communities and providing the critical pipeline for modern data services, mobile banking, and digital commerce.

The fierce independence that defines Globacom is a direct reflection of its founder’s personal journey. Adenuga’s rise is the ultimate story of relentless African grit. Long before he was dubbed “The Bull” of African commerce, a young Adenuga drove taxis and worked security jobs in the United States to pay his way through university.

Returning to Nigeria with a sharp mind and an insatiable work ethic, he built his fortune brick by brick. He conquered hard commodities, established a presence in oil and gas with Conoil, mastered corporate banking, and ultimately turned his sight toward telecommunications. Every venture was driven by the same philosophy: absolute dedication, hands-on execution, and a fierce refusal to settle for second best.

Despite commanding a multi-billion-dollar fortune, Adenuga remains famously reclusive. Operating largely away from public cameras and party circuits, he chooses to let his work speak for him. His quiet philanthropy, strategic investments, and relentless job creation have lifted thousands of families and injected vital energy into the broader West African economy.

Beyond cell towers and fiber-optic lines, Globacom transformed itself into an iconic symbol of African pride. Recognizing the power of local culture long before global streaming platforms arrived, Adenuga turned Glo into the largest single corporate promoter of African entertainment and sports.

Glo flooded the creative industry with record-breaking sponsorship deals and endorsements, signing Nollywood legends, musical powerhouses, and sports heroes as brand ambassadors. From sponsoring the prestigious CAF African Footballer of the Year Awards and the Nigerian Premier League to funding cultural festivals, comedy tours, and reality shows, Glo actively elevated African talent to global prominence.

Through these cultural investments, the brand cultivated an emotional connection with millions of subscribers, proving that an African brand could stand tall, celebrate its heritage, and deliver world-class service without losing its soul.

Industry analysts frequently cite Globacom as more than just a corporate success; it is an enduring case study in what happens when visionary local leadership is matched with long-term capital and solid determination. Over 23 years, Glo has weathered fierce market competition, rapid technological transitions from 2G to 5G, and volatile macroeconomic shifts, all while maintaining its position at the top tier of African telecommunications.

As customers, industry leaders, and well-wishers celebrate GLO@23, the milestone serves as a powerful tribute to a titan who dared to build on his own terms.

Today, Globacom isn’t merely a telecom network; it stands as living proof of African capability, self-determination, and industrial excellence. As the green network prepares for its next era of digital expansion, artificial intelligence integration, and next-generation connectivity, one truth remains crystal clear across Africa’s business landscape: The Bull is still on the throne, and his legacy is built to last.

Bodex Hungbo, a media professional, writes from Lagos.

World.title: A black face and a thousand ships, by Bisi Adeleye-Fayemi
World.content:
We read Homer’s ‘The Odyssey’ when we were in school, about King Odysseus of Ithaca who joined other Kings in the Trojan war. It took King Odysseus ten long years to make it back home to Ithaca. We remember the captivating, epic story of love, honour, betrayal, loyalty and redemption. The adventures of King Odysseus began with the narrative of ‘the face that launched a thousand ships’. Helen of Troy was known in Greek mythology as the most beautiful woman in the world. She was the daughter of the God Zeus and Leda. Many Greek Kings wanted her, and she ended up with King Menelaus of Sparta. The myth was not clear if Helen fell in love with the visiting Trojan Prince Paris and eloped with him, or if he kidnapped her.

What is without doubt is the rage of her husband and his determination to get her back. A massive Greek fleet was assembled by King Menelaus and his allies, and they proceeded to lay siege on Troy. Reading Homer’s ‘The lliad’, as a child who was being educated in a post-colonial, commonwealth country, it is no surprise that right from the time I learnt about these characters, the image of Helen of Troy was one of a white woman. Who else would have a face that could launch a thousand ships? When Hollywood produced the Cleopatra epic in 1963, there was no outrage, when Elizabeth Taylor was cast as Cleopatra. Cleopatra existed for real, she was not a mythical character like Helen of Troy, yet the most acceptable face to portray her was a Caucasian actress.

In 2004, Wolfgang Peterson produced Troy, which was an all-star mega production. According to reports, famous actresses such as Nicole Kidman and Uma Thurman were considered for the role of Helen. Wolfgang Peterson, who was also the Director, insisted on throwing it open to a global search that involved thousands of candidates. He settled for the German actress Diane Kruger who met all the boxes he had in mind. Knowing Hollywood standard operating procedures, it was clear that whether famous or unknown, the ‘face that launched a thousand ships’ would be a white one. Till Christopher Nolan came along.

In July 2026, The Odyssey was released to mixed reviews. While many acclaim the story-telling, cinematography and acting, the film is going to be best known for the casting choices of the Director, Christopher Nolan. The casting of Lupita Nyong’O as Helen of Troy has inspired reactions ranging from shock to disbelief and even disgust. Helen of Troy was the daughter of a God, her beauty was incomparable, she was so desirable that Kings fought for her and over her for years. Her face placed a thousand ships on the sea. That face, as literature, history, popular culture and convention has tried to tell us over the years, was definitely one that met global beauty standards. A face with the right skin tone, cheek bones, eyes, nose, neck. A body with all the right proportions. A woman who could be described as a Goddess. The image that Helen Kruger famously embodied when she played the role in 2004. In essence, what the reactions to Lupita Nyong’O’s casting as Helen of Troy tells us is that a black woman can never be beautiful enough to force Kings to go to war.

Christopher Nolan could have chosen to cast any other actress of colour. He had many choices which included Latina, Asian and light skinned black women, with famous names from all those communities. Yet, he chose Lupita Nyong’O, a woman who is ‘unarguably black’. An Oscar and Daytime Emmy award winner. A woman from the African continent, who has distinguished herself as a film and stage actress. A model, producer, philanthropist and social justice advocate.

What was Christopher Nolan trying to say with his casting of Lupita? He has not said why, he does not need to defend his choice. His attitude seems to be ‘Why not?’ We can attempt to read between the lines. Christopher Nolan’s agenda might have been to generate controversy. Controversy means attention and it is all good for ticket sales. However, the meaning I choose to give his choice is, ‘Who defines what beauty is? Who sets the standards? Who makes the rules?’ Too many times, we have been told and shown, what ‘beauty’ looks like. Beauty is tall, fair-skinned, slim, straight nose, long and wavy hair. There was a time when I thought we had overcome this narrative and had started to affirm the wholistic beauty of black women. Sadly, looking at the reactions to Lupita’s role as Helen of Troy, and seeing what is happening with many young women of colour, particularly African women, this battle is far from over. Right from the times of slavery when the shade of your skin determined if you would spend your life working in the fields or in the Master’s house, black women have suffered the consequences of falling within or without the established beauty standards.

In some of our communities, being plump with ‘front and back endowments’ were acceptable beauty norms. Trust patriarchy to capitalize on this. For those born without, the savvy producers of artificial breasts, hips and backsides now do brisk business. What the manufacturers of these contraptions cannot do, medical procedures can take it from there. We now even have artificial pubic hair! So, we see young women struggling to invest resources trying to live up to these questionable standards of beauty. In the process, they not only endanger their health, they internalise all the negative stereotypes about how low black women are on the beauty hierarchy.

The beauty industry has lived off our insecurities for too long. Fixations on skinny bodies, large, firm breasts, small waists, firm behinds, skin bleaching, expensive wigs, make-up that is unsuitable for all skintones, dubious skin-care products, we have had too much of this shoved down our throats. Beauty is universal, and so it makes sense that expressions of beauty are everywhere, regardless of race, ethnicity, body size, hair texture and skin tone. Recently, Naomie Pilula, a Lawyer from Zambia, posted a selfie of herself. It went viral, with astonishing comments about how ugly she was, the level of cyber-bullying was terrible. Naomie, however, proceeded to teach her detractors a powerful lesson. She not only refused to take her photograph down, she stated that she knows she might not fit conventional beauty standards, but she loves herself and embraces her unique appearance. Naomie went from being a laughingstock because of her ‘lack of beauty’ to commanding respect due to her integrity.

In 2026, thanks to Christopher Nolan, when we think about ‘a face that launched a thousand ships’, the image that comes to mind should not automatically be that of a blue-eyed, blond, model-thin Caucasian woman. Who is a beautiful woman? Lupita Nyong’O is a resilient, dignified, well-educated, award-winning, talented woman. A worthy role model, whose beauty is internal as well as external. Let us encourage our daughters to seek self-love like Lupita and Naomie, and support them to make affirming choices. Let them grow to be proud of whatever size or shade they are. They should know that they are worthy and they are enough.

They should have power and control over their image on their own terms, and not because they believe this is what men want. Many men don’t even know what they want. People should stop calling light-skinned women ‘clean’ and dark-skinned women, ‘dirty’. It is appalling and makes us no better than our then slave masters. No woman should be made to feel that she is too ugly or unattractive for the world she lives in. Who determines that? Is itthe men she will come across, many of who will likely look like they got run over by a bus? Not every man is a Denzel Washington, Idris Elba, Jude Bellingham or Maduka Okoye. Black women are beautiful. African women are beautiful. And Lupita Nyong’O? She is a Goddess whose face and body can launch a thousand missiles.

World.title: Put your wife down at your peril!
World.content:
By Bunmi Sofola

LARA had often moaned that someone else had got the life she was supposed to have. We were mates at the secondary school and have remained close decades after we left. A fairly brilliant student, we were all mildly surprised when she opted for matrimony. Within the spate of a decade, she’d not only had four children, she’d become fat and frumpy. It didn’t help that her husband’s clerical job didn’t pay much to keep the family above the breadline. In the end Lara resigned her low-paid job and trained as a caterer.

“It was the best move I’d made so far,” Lara had said. “After running a modest canteen, I was extremely lucky when one of our mates in school helped me get the job of running the canteen in her office. It was a big one too and the responsibilities were challenging. But there were perks too – it meant the difference between paying the school fees and putting decent meals on the table.

“You would think Lere my husband would appreciate the extra money. The business centre he set up when he was retrenched wasn’t bringing in much and that really frustrated him. When we argued, he said lots of things – that I didn’t know when to shut up, that I looked like the back of an elephant. He even complained I came home reeking of kitchen fume.

“Thanks to his criticism, I spruced myself up a bit. I got some new clothes I could afford and tried applying make-up. The staff teased me but I enjoyed the attention. But the day that really changed my life for the better happened some nine months ago. We were already packing up for the day when one of the top officials sent for me. He was going to work late and wondered if I could rustle up something for him to eat. I told him I would try my best. The rest of the canteen staff were all set to leave, so I told them not to bother, I would handle things.

When I later took the tray to the man, we shall call him Leo, he was already on the settee in his office with a lot of files on the coffee table. I cleared a portion of the table and set the food down. I gave him drinks from his fridge and told him I would wait at the reception when he was through. He shook his head and told me to sit with him as he ate. He told me to help myself to a drink and I took a bottle of stout. He raised his brow slightly and giggled. When I sat next to him again, I noticed a photo of three smiling children – all boys and they looked just like him. He chatted as he had his meal and I realised what friendly man he was.

“The setting was so domesticated that I suddenly realised I missed proper sex and felt sexually drawn to Leo. I don’t know where the courage came from but as he raised his glass for more drinks, I leant forward and kissed him. Leo’s eyes widened in surprise. I thought he might recoil, embarrassed, and order me out of his office. Instead, he pulled me closer and frantically kissed me back. As he pushed my top up, I tugged at his trousers. His fingers were all over my boobs. I was wearing an old, grey bra, but he didn’t mind. He pushed it up, wanting skin to skin. Some of the files laid scattered on the floor but we took no notice. I ended up with some of them under my buttocks as we made frantic love. I felt I was that ‘someone else’, that I had finally taken my life back.

When it was over, Leo seemed happy with himself as he gave me a cuddle. ‘You’re one sexy big girl!’ he whispered. In that moment, I knew it would has. Sex with my husband had become something that happened on a Saturday night when he rolled in from his beer parlour to wake me up. I missed proper sex and thank goodness, Leo is providing that.

“I supposed you could say we’re having an affair – except that Leo and I never meet anywhere but at the office. Yet it’s enough for me. Lere and I are still arguing. A few nights ago, I even blurted out in the heat of temper: ‘I’m sleeping with one of my bosses!’ He looked at me as if I’d gone off my senses. ‘Don’t be daft,’ he snorted. ‘Who’d want a fat slob like you?’ Well, Leo does. And that’s why I won’t stop what I’m doing. I can face life and my husband’s callous indifference as long as Leo wants me. He’s a very generous man too. Come to think of it, I must be a lot cheaper than those hoity-toity high-maintenance girls in the office – and I’m no threat.

“Thanks to his generosity, I’m able to afford small luxuries for the family – including my husband! I’ve shed a bit of weight too – not that much as I enjoy my food. If Lere notices anything, he hasn’t said a word. He should really be grateful that another man is helping him shoulder his responsibilities.

Sweet Smell Of Success! (Humour)

Sitting at home one night with his wife, a man is casually tossing peanuts into the air and catching them in his mouth. As the couple take in the latest episode of watchdog, the man loses concentration for a split second and a peanut goes into his ear. He tries to get the nut out, but succeeds only in forcing the thing in awfully deep. After a few hours of fruitless rooting, the couple decide to go to the hospital, but on their way out of the front door they met their daughter coming in with her boyfriend.

The boyfriend takes control of the situation: he tell them he’s studying medicine and that they’re not to worry about a thing. He then sticks two fingers up the man’s nose and asks him to blow – and lo, the nut shoots from the ear and out across the room. As the daughter and her boy friend go through the kitchen to make a pot of tea, the man and his wife sit down to discuss their luck. “So, the wife says,” what do you think he’ll become after he qualifies? A GP or a surgeon?” “Well,” says the man, rubbing his nose, “by the smell of his fingers, our son-in-law.”

In The Heat Of Passion

A man and his wife are driving home in their expensive new car one night when they both got horny, and decided to christen the sparkling motor with a shag. Pulling into a lay-by they get down to business, but soon realise their nice new motor’s actually too small for the amount of erotic manoeuvring they want to do. The guy suggests they limb out and have a go under the car, which he promises his wife will provide ample clearance for his heavy buttocks, so the couple slip under the pristine vehicle and go at it like the clappers. In fact, they’re enjoying themselves so much that they don’t notice when a policeman comes over and taps the man on the back of his exposed legs.

“What do you think you’re doing?” the copper asks the man. “I’m fixing my car,” the chap calmly replies. “No you’re not!” the policeman says through hysterical laughter. “You’re having sex in public, and, I’m going to nick you for indecent exposure.” “How do you know I’m lying?” the indignant man asks. “Well,” the copper replies, “for a start, you’re facing downwards on top of a naked woman. Secondly, I don’t see any tools anywhere. And thirdly, your car was stolen five minutes ago.”

World.title: Osun 2026: Between politics and law, by Tonnie Iredia
World.content:
The matter of the moment in the last couple of days has been the rift between the Osun state government and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission EFCC. While Nigerians have continued to comment on the subject, a major gain of the nation is the people’s realization that if their president is careful and observant, he can easily become personally conscious of public opinion. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu passed that simple exam of the week by intervening in the EFCC-Osun rift. The strategic intervention has not only soaked the political tension in Osun; it has dramatically converted the tension into a debate for all comers sending political jobbers back to the drawing board to find new controversies to create.

Tinubu must take advantage of the gain by staying away from relying on only the version of a story told by allies, aides and supporters. For each controversy, a leader must seek to comprehend all the dimensions of the stories he is told. Before Tinubu, a few presidents relied on the one-sided story at the expense of their image. For example, President Jonathan should not have relied entirely on a supposed technical advice to change his plan to personally visit Chibok. If a president who is armed to the teeth is dissuaded by men of technical and security expertise from visiting a troubled spot, what does he expect the public to feel and into what use is he expected to put his gamut of security convoy? We submit that there is always a difference between technicality, law and politics.

It is against this backdrop that the decision of President Tinubu to put a pause on EFCC’s action in Osun state ought to be interrogated. I have watched many colleagues on national television marshalling several points to disagree with the intervention. Some of their arguments especially the legal options they have raised are no doubt quite persuasive but President Tinubu’s intervention was not designed to deal with a legal topic. The argument that he should have left the matter to his Attorney General establishes clearly that the commentators had made up their minds that it is only through law that matters are resolved which is not true. I want to believe that whereas the commentators were looking at the letters of the law, the president was thinking of the spirit of the law.

Law to my mind is useless if its handling cannot prevent the dismemberment of society. Those of us who think Tinubu’s intervention was not bad are not in any way suggesting that EFCC was pursuing any hidden or illegal agenda. Indeed, we are strong among those who have found cause to commend the current leadership of that reformed anti-corruption agency. So much has changed there; prosecution has improved, convictions have increased while it has embraced an effective inter-agency synergy that is yielding great positive results. We also agree with the argument that the EFCC was acting within its legal mandate in its Osun mission. The point to be made therefore is that it is simplistic to see the president’s intervention as evidence that the EFCC did some wrong.

What appears to have unsettled the president was not EFCC’s work but the public opinion that the agency was being used to destabilize a sitting state government so as to empower the political party of the president to take over the state. Almost every Nigerian believes this which the state concerned has helped to amplify across all digital media organs. Even the EFCC would be shocked to learn that some of its staff do not only feel so but may have confirmed it privately to their friends and family. What this suggests is that most people must have imagined that it was the president who may have directed the EFCC to do the hatchet job on Osun state especially as he was quoted to have said recently that all is fair in politics.

With only a few months away to his own re-election bid, there is no way Tinubu would have adopted the option of ‘silence is golden’ and allow the damaging public opinion to take root. The president actually has many more interventions to make to reduce the unduly high degree of politicisation of Nigeria. In the last decade, the only industry flourishing in our country is politics. It has become so attractive that people are prepared to kill to get into office. Painfully, threats are carried out using the privileges of public office. Members of the ruling party at the national level are usually able to access the instruments of coercion to perpetrate violence. The president must therefore intervene to halt the trend whereby people in government often seek to overwhelm members of the opposition. That is not democracy

It is worse when the opposition in a state such as Osun is seen by the public as strong enough to overpower a state government – a development that is likely to happen only through the help of federal power. If the same overpowering opposition party in a state wins the next election, no one is likely to believe that it was through the ballot. There is therefore no better time than now for President Tinubu to put a halt to the belligerence in Osun or any such state. The idea of a ruling party losing at the polls happens all over the world. But it usually happens when an opposition has better ideas or more charismatic candidates who are able to persuade voters. It is time to stop the victories attained in our clime through the force of law or fraudulent systems. In particular, let’s stop the show of force in the states by Abuja-based politicians.

Perhaps, one way of doing this is to alter our attitude to elections. About a decade ago when the current ruling APC was in the opposition, it went to court to stop the use of the military in our elections. The court ruled in its favour; yet, the involvement of the military in elections in Nigeria is increasing. Who usually approves the release of the military to our election merchants and into what use do they put them? Why do we require soldiers to be part of our elections when we keep saying the worst democratic government is better than the best military dictatorship? Is our election so tense that we need more than the Police? Is it not strange that security agencies are even more active in non-chaotic segments like collation of votes?

Answers to the above posers may help us understand the direction of the Osun governorship election which is just a few days away. For me, as an independent election observer, I will always remember the Osun Governorship election which took place on Saturday, September 22, 2018. The current governor, Ademola Adeleke was also the leading candidate at the time but INEC refused to declare him the winner because of certain issues in about 7 polling units. According to the electoral body, the election was inconclusive – a popular title at the time, so a rerun was fixed for Thursday September 27, 2018. During the rerun which INEC announced was won by the ruling party rather than the leading candidate, both voters and election observers were harassed by security agencies to achieve a predetermined goal. The US, EU and UK observers reported irregularities and interference by inappropriate persons in the election.

As we are set to re-enact the old 19th Century battle of Osogbo 1840, there is need to caution politicians to let the contest be determined by voters rather than by top politicians who would converge on the state to ensure their party wins by whatever method. If that is allowed, it would be a bigger stain to wash than stopping the EFCC that would have evidence to justify its actions. This is why we call on the President today to take the same step he took concerning the EFCC to warn INEC to be diligent in handling the coming Osun election. He should also send a strong appeal to his own party members especially their “inter-state professional players” to allow Osun APC members run the show in line with the rules set for the game. A ruling party is usually a big party with all manner of members – wealthy chieftains, gentlemen, fraudsters etc.

In its days, PDP had specialized riggers, most of whom have since defected to their successor party. Whoever can counsel such riggers to allow us have credible election would have done so much service to the fatherland. This is because it is only from credible elections that we can source visionary leaders who would formulate and implement proactive public policies that can improve the living conditions of our compatriots and push Nigeria into the big league of developed political entities.

World.title: Obasanjo, Osoba, AD, and 2003 old men stale stuff, by Dele Sobowale
World.content:
Dele Sobowale

“The loser at the hazard, when the game breaks up/ Sadder, sorrier lingers on alone

Replays each throw and drinks of wisdom’s cup” – Aligheri Dante, 1265-1321, in Purgatory.

For me, this is one of the most painful articles I have ever had to write in 39 years of writing for VANGUARD. In a fight between older brothers, friends and political associates on the one hand, and, a barely tolerable opponent on the other side, I naturally stand by the former – and damn the consequences. This is the first exception. With all due respects to my senior brothers in the South-West, the recent controversy between former President Obasanjo and former Governor Osoba, can most aptly be regarded as “the same stale old stew, warmed up and served in new plates” (Apologies to ex-President Babangida).

Nothing substantially new was added to what we knew already before the fresh outburst. I know why we are again being treated to another round of recriminations. I will discuss that later. I was never a party card holder; but, my family had been in the progressive camp ever since my eldest brother, the late Chief Sanu Sobowale, joined the Action Group Youth Wing with the late Chief Bola Ige. I had the privilege of knowing Ige when he and my brother attended Ibadan Grammar School. Ige was the Kaduna Boy; my brother was the Zaria Boy in their class. They exchanged visits and that was when I first came across the man later nicknamed Cicero.

I remember, as if it happened yesterday, my encounter with the late Chief Ayo Adebanjo; lifetime stalwart of Afenifere, in his chambers at the Western House, Broad Street, Lagos Island. I was sitting watching the NTA News, for days before the meeting, when it was reported that the leaders of AD/Afenifere had reached an agreement with President Obasanjo not to field a presidential candidate for the 2003 elections. Despite the fact that Nigeria and the world were still several years from when government-controlled media agencies broadcast barefaced lies, the announcement was still incredible to me; principally, because it made no sense for AD.

REQUIEM FOR AD/AFENIFERE

“To know/That which before us lies in daily life/Is the prime wisdom, what is more is fume” – John Milton, 1608-1674, VANGUARD BOOK OF QUOTATIONS p 275

There was only one way to find out. I wrote an article the Sunday after the announcement titled REQUIEM FOR AD. Briefly summarized, my position was this: First, given the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the presidency is the only position any political party should aspire to hold. My political arithmetic convinced me that, unlike the US Constitution, the Nigerian president had more clout than all the 36 governors combined. Any party not vying for the presidency is heading for the graveyard of politics. Second, AD/Afenifere controlling the six states of the South West should aim at expanding its influence nationwide, while still contesting for president; and hope that superior governance in the zone would attract support from other states. Third, and this was perhaps the most important, Obasanjo should not be trusted, the agreement announced sounded to me like the lion asking the leopard to form a hunting partnership; every success to be shared equally. The leopard might soon find itself on the lion’s menu.

Fourth, I ended by asking the leaders of AD/Afenifere to withdraw from the deal. That was the main presentation – which characteristically was full of global precedents as well as one of local examples.

The article appeared on Sunday; I received an urgent message from the late Chief Ayo Adebanjo, highly respected, almost worshipped, who I visited several times before.

It was a most unhappy meeting for both of us. The late Chief Adebanjo, like most great men, sooner or later, invest themselves with infallibility. They can never be wrong; and they don’t tolerate younger people trying to correct them; more so, when it was a group decision made by older, more experienced politicians and wiser than me. He proceeded to lecture me on the details of the agreement. The more he revealed, the more alarmed I became. I couldn’t believe that our most trusted leaders in the progressive alliance could be so easily duped. The meeting turned combative when I asked a question.

“Sir, you said Obasanjo agreed to leave your governors untouched. What if he reneges on that promise? It will be too late to make amends.”

“Obasanjo is a senior military officer; they keep their words.”

“Sir, that is precisely my fear. Deception is fair in war; and politics is like war without shooting.”

“Are you saying that the president of Nigeria can be distrusted?”

“Yes Sir, on a matter like this.”

“Dele, please walk out of my office.”

Unfortunately for the progressives, the leaders had been lured to their own self-destruction. One victim of this catastrophe was of particular interest to me.

SEGUN OSOBA, OLD BOY, METHODIST BOYS HIGH SCHOOL, LAGOS

“God save me from my friends; I can take care of my enemies.”

Senior Segun Osoba and I grew up in Lagos; he was my senior at Methodist Boys High School while I was trailing a few years behind at Igbobi College. Both schools valued high ethical standards and bred them into the students. He was unprepared for politics.

Lagos boys always were instinctive loyal to each other. I was totally devoted to Osoba; I also feared for his safety given the agreement with Obasanjo. Chief Osoba, like all politicians, had enemies; who never hurt him. Instead, he was a victim of his friends in AD/Afenifere as well as his newly found “friend” – President Obasanjo. As soon as the pact was sealed, Osoba could be seen at the Lagos Airport to receive the president each time Obasanjo was in Lagos and Abeokuta. The governor was faithful to the terms of the deal; the president was not. It was painful watching the game playing out; though I naively thought that Osoba would defeat anybody thrown at him; deal or not.

I was at the VANGUARD Editorial meeting the day Gbenga Daniel came to announce his candidacy for the governorship of Ogun State. We listened politely and laughed heartily when he departed. To us, it was a bloody joke for anybody to want to challenge Osoba. Complacency crept in; Osoba hardly campaigned. I cried when the results came in; Osoba and four other AD governors had been sent home. The deception had worked as I predicted.

Chief Adebanjo and I met, at a funeral, months after the AD/Afenifere had lost five states, leaving only Lagos State; where Bola Tinubu had refused to be a party to the agreement. Good upbringing demanded that I should greet first and respectfully. It was not triumph but sadness. The progressive movement in the South-West had been decapitated. Henceforth, the zone will fall into the hands of non-Awoists.

PLEASE STOP THE NEEDLESS CONTROVERSY

“A peaceful mind is often built by avoiding arguments that prove nothing” – Author Unknown

Just as I was struggling with how to end this article, stopping at a petrol station yielded this gem of advice on the back of a T-shirt worn by a bus driver. I quickly wrote it down. The current controversy erupted when someone pointed to references made in Osoba’s book concerning the 2003 elections. Obasanjo was portrayed as a traitor. Ever combative and deeply self-righteous, Baba Iyabo rejected the branding. As far as he was concerned, he played higher level politics and won handsomely. The losers are still licking their wounds. Nothing to apologise for. This is a classic case of a dispute involving parties who cannot even agree on what the disagreement is all about.

Under the circumstances, my modest proposal to both sides is for them to stop this needless controversy. AD/Afenifere committed a monumental blunder; which swept them away as a political force. Obasanjo, military, took advantage of their innocence; and is not magnanimous in victory. Nothing more will be gained by disputes. We are bored.

OBASANJO: HOW NOT TO BE A RESPECTED ELDER STATESMAN

“Character is destiny.”

Obasanjo versus Fayose, Obasanjo versus Osoba, Obasanjo versus Atiku…and the list goes on. Each and every time former President Obasanjo exchanges insults with those less divinely blessed than he, the old man diminishes himself more. A man, who should be above political fray; who should enjoy, indeed command, the respect of all Nigerians, routinely collects insults like a pig in polluted marshland. It is a pity that one of our human national monuments willfully debases the institution of past presidents.

It was disclosed in his altercation with Fayose that N10 million had been sent to him together with invitation – before disagreements occurred and insults were exchanged.

“I clothed and fed you, Atiku fires back at Obasanjo” – VANGUARD, August 2, 2026

Any man with self-respect does not invite people to wash his dirty underwear in public. Why is Obasanjo doing this to himself? The man is his own worst enemy…

•Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola

World.title: CDS Applauds Troops’ Commitment to Defending Nigeria
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Olufemi Oluyede, has commended troops across all theatres of operation for their discipline, resilience and unwavering commitment to the defence of the nation.

Oluyede also praised the sustained collaboration between the Armed Forces, other security agencies, local security groups and relevant stakeholders.

According to a statement by the Director of Defence Media Operations, Major General Michael Onoja, the CDS said the synergy had continued to produce positive results in the ongoing campaign against terrorism, kidnapping and other forms of criminality.

The Defence Chief also commended the media for its professionalism and balanced reportage of military operations, urging members of the public to continue providing useful information to security forces to strengthen the nation’s security architecture.

He assured Nigerians of the Armed Forces’ unwavering resolve to sustain the current operational tempo until peace and stability are fully restored across all theatres of operation.

Major General Onoja revealed that troops of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, had apprehended two suspected terrorist logistics suppliers in Monguno LGA of Borno State, recovering assorted foodstuffs and provisions allegedly destined for terrorists in Kukawa LGA of the state.

“Similarly, another terrorist logistics supplier was arrested at Gwalaram Village in Magumeri LGA on 4 August 2026. In a separate operation conducted on 3 August 2026, troops rescued Miss Blessing Tuggur, an 18-year-old victim who was abducted in November 2025 at the Dogoba Kopre axis in Askira-Uba LGA of Borno State.

“The victim was subsequently reunited with her family after receiving medical attention. On the same day, a suspect was arrested at Kan Lamba Village in Darazo LGA of Bauchi State for allegedly attempting to procure firearms. Similarly, a suspected terrorist informant was arrested at Dzangola Kilba in Hong LGA of Adamawa State on 5 August 2026,” the statement revealed.

The Director also stated that several family members of suspected terrorists had surrendered, while others were intercepted in Gwoza, Konduga and Bama LGAs of Borno State.

“Additionally, a group of 20 persons surrendered to troops at Kwuari in Konduga LGA of Borno State,” Onoja said.

World.title: Transcorp Hotels Launches New Padel Courts at Transcorp Hilton Abuja
World.content:
Transcorp Hotels Plc, the hospitality subsidiary of Transnational Corporation Plc, has launched new padel courts at Transcorp Hilton Abuja, adding one of the world’s fastest-growing sports to its evolving collection of experiences designed for guests, families, professionals and Abuja’s active social community.

The launch is the latest in a series of investments that continue to enhance guest experience at Transcorp Hilton Abuja, reflecting Transcorp Hotels’ commitment to creating vibrant spaces where business, leisure and lifestyle come together.

Speaking at the launch, the MD/CEO of Transcorp Hotels Plc, Uzoamaka Oshogwe, said: “People want more from hospitality today. They want places where they can work, unwind, stay active, and create meaningful memories all in one destination. That is what we are offering at Transcorp Hilton Abuja. Our new padel courts are another way we are bringing people together and creating experiences our guests will love.”

Regarded as one of the world’s fastest-growing sports, padel enhances Transcorp Hilton Abuja’s growing lifestyle and recreational offering, alongside its award-winning accommodation, exceptional dining, wellness facilities, swimming pools, tennis and squash courts.

Complementing these offerings is the Transcorp Centre, one of Africa’s largest purpose-built events and conference venues. With a 5,000-seat capacity and state-of-the-art soundproof partitioning system, the facility adapts seamlessly from intimate functions to large-scale gatherings, positioning Transcorp Hilton Abuja as a preferred venue for high-volume, high-level international conferences, corporate meetings, exhibitions, weddings and cultural events.

Together, these investments strengthen the hotel’s position as a destination where business meets leisure.

World.title: Oath-taking Video: APC’s Desperate Attempt To Smear Adeleke Will Not Save Him From Defeat, Says Imole Campaign Council
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Imole Campaign Council has described as laughable and defeatist the attempt by the Osun State All Progressives Congress (APC) Governorship Campaign Council to link Governor Ademola Adeleke to an alleged oath-taking video currently circulating on social media, stating emphatically that the governor has absolutely no connection whatsoever with any such activity.

In a statement issued yesterday by the Chairman, Media Committee, The Imole Campaign Council, Bamidele Salam, said the council is presently examining the authenticity, source and circumstances surrounding the video in question.

According to him, “It is important to state categorically that Governor Ademola Adeleke has neither authorised, participated in, directed nor endorsed the taking of any oath by anyone in relation to the August 15 governorship election or for any other political purpose.

“Governor Adeleke is a democrat who believes fundamentally in the freedom of citizens to make their political choices according to their conscience. He does not need oaths, threats, intimidation or any form of coercion to secure the support of the people of Osun State.”

He further said, “Indeed, the governor enjoys broad and demonstrable support across the state based on his record of performance and his personal connection with the people. His campaign is therefore anchored on his achievements, his vision for Osun and the confidence of the electorate, not on superstition, coercion or clandestine practices.

“The APC’s attempt to immediately attribute an unverified social media video to Governor Adeleke is therefore nothing but a hard-sell political manoeuvre by an opposition that is increasingly confronted with the reality of its rejection by the Osun electorate.

“The APC’s attempt to convert an unverified video into a campaign issue also exposes the poverty of its campaign strategy. Rather than engage Governor Adeleke’s administration on roads, healthcare, education, workers’ welfare, infrastructure, rural development and other measurable areas of governance, the opposition has resorted to allegations based on videos whose provenance remains unclear.

“But let there be no ambiguity: Governor Ademola Adeleke does not require anybody to swear an oath before supporting him. He does not require anyone to invoke a curse before voting for him. He does not require supernatural intervention to win an election. His strength is the people. His campaign is based on his record. His mandate belongs to the electorate.”

Salam noted that the APC should therefore stop looking for excuses in videos and begin preparing for the verdict of the Osun people on August 15.

“The people of Osun are not being asked to vote for Governor Adeleke because of any oath. They are being asked to vote for him because they have seen the difference between a government that works for the people and an opposition that has offered little beyond fear, propaganda and empty accusations.

“Governor Adeleke will face the people on August 15 with his record. Let the APC face the people with its own record.”

World.title: Benue ADC Guber Candidate Confident Atiku Will Win 2027 Presidential Election
World.content:
George Okoh in Makurdi

The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Benue State, Herman Hembe, has declared that the ADC’s presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, will win the 2027 election.

Hembe disclosed this in Makurdi yesterday while unveiling his deputy, John Abba.

He had constituted a committee to select the party deputy governorship candidate a few days after he emerged as the party’s gubernatorial candidate.

According to Hembe, the selection of deputy governorship candidate which has the endorsement of the national chairman of the party, Senator David Mark, was transparent.

Hembe said, “Let me congratulate Abba on his selection as deputy governorship candidate of the party. We constituted a team to consult and get the deputy governorship candidate and our leader, David Mark ensured the process was transparent.”

Speaking on the permutations, Hembe stated that all things are working in favour of the party presidential candidate.

“Our permutations are that the votes from the Southern part of the country will be shared between Peter Obi and Bola Tinubu and we are very sure that none of Obi and Tinubu will be able to defeat Atiku in the three geo political zones in the North,” Hembe said.

While charging the party members to go all out to work for all the party candidates at the presidential election, Hembe assured that there will be band wagon effects on the second election.

“Our hardest job is to work and ensure that our party wins the presidential and National Assembly elections, then, we will just go and sleep because that victory will have a positive effect on our election.”

Hembe promised that he is only going to spend a term in office to complete the eight years of Jechira Zone and create history to hand over to the Benue South senatorial district, known as Zone C.

World.title: 2027: Kogi East APC Stakeholders Back Tinubu, Ododo, Demand Power Rotation
World.content:
• Say East will no longer be appendage to any political bloc

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 general election, critical stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kogi East Senatorial District have declared their total support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, while demanding a fresh and equitable framework for political power rotation in Kogi State.

The stakeholders, who spoke through a communiqué issued at the end of their Strategic Leadership Conference in Abuja and made available to THISDAY on Saturday, said Kogi East would no longer accept a political arrangement that relegated the senatorial district to the status of an appendage of another political bloc.

They also called for direct negotiations with political stakeholders from Kogi Central and Kogi West on what they described as “distinct, transparent and equitable” terms to establish a predictable framework for power transition and inclusive development in the state.

The stakeholders said their immediate priority was to ensure victory for the APC in the January/February 2027 general election, particularly the re-election of Tinubu and the victory of all APC candidates contesting National and State Assembly seats.

They further pledged to mobilise support for Governor Ododo’s re-election for a second term in the November 2027 governorship election.

According to them, the political objective was not merely to win elections but to reposition Kogi East within the mainstream of state and national politics and secure what they described as the “deserved share of development” for the district.

The communiqué noted that Kogi East had recorded the highest bloc vote for President Tinubu among the three senatorial districts of Kogi State in the 2023 presidential election, stressing that the district was prepared to increase its contribution to the APC in 2027.

He said: “We look forward to increasing our electoral contributions to the APC and to strengthening our collaboration with our fellow compatriots from Kogi Central and Kogi West Senatorial Districts to return power to Kogi East.

“However, we are resolved to mobilise total support for the incumbent governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, and his re-election for his second term come

2027.”

The declaration came against the backdrop of what the stakeholders described as more than a decade of political fractures, disaffection and missed opportunities in Kogi State following the 2015 governorship election and the death of the late former governor, Prince Abubakar Audu.

They said attempts to achieve political realignment in 2019 and 2023 were not sustained, leaving ordinary citizens of Kogi East to bear the consequences of prolonged political disagreements.

The stakeholders insisted that the time had come to heal the wounds, rebuild trust among the three senatorial districts and establish a new political understanding based on equity, inclusion and mutual respect.

They said: “We refuse to allow old wounds to permanently damage the deep historical linkages between the people of the various sections of Kogi State.

“Our only path to reawaken the political strength of Kogi East is to encourage healthy collaboration with the other sections of the state and negotiate truthfully for all that our people deserve.

“We reject any attempt to make Kogi East an appendage of any group in the state.”

The stakeholders invoked the political legacy of Prince Audu, saying his philosophy was anchored on statewide unity, inclusion, dialogue and equitable distribution of development.

They recalled that during Audu’s administration, major projects were conceived and executed across the three senatorial districts, including the establishment of the state university in Anyigba and the Obajana Cement Project, as well as roads and other civic infrastructure.

They argued that the late governor’s political philosophy should be revived as the foundation for a new era of cooperation in Kogi State.

“That is the true political philosophy we must revive today: vision, selflessness, courage, fraternity, equity and shared purpose,” the communiqué stated.

The stakeholders also demanded an immediate shift towards a predictable political transition arrangement, arguing that sustainable development could not be achieved where political succession remained a source of tension.

According to them, “We assemble here today to lay a solid foundation for Kogi East to be part of a realistic, predictable and harmonious political transition in Kogi State.

“We call for an immediate shift towards building consensus, renegotiating power transfer and rotation, and establishing an inclusive, development-driven agenda that guarantees equitable access to the instruments of power.”

The group also sought national recognition for Audu, describing him as a statesman whose contribution to Nigeria’s democratic development should not be confined to his final years in politics.

It urged the Kogi State Government to present Audu’s contributions to the Federal Government for a “highly merited and long-overdue national honour”.

The stakeholders cited the 10th anniversary commemorative events held in Lokoja in October 2025, which brought together national political leaders, traditional rulers and former governors, as evidence of the late governor’s enduring national stature.

They also noted the naming of a major boulevard in Lokoja after Audu by Governor Ododo and the unveiling of the Prince Abubakar Audu Leadership Foundation by the representative of President Tinubu at the anniversary events.

The stakeholders called for the foundation to operate as a nationwide, non-partisan platform for preserving Audu’s memory and promoting his leadership philosophy.

They argued that restricting his legacy to one election cycle or the final period of his political career would amount to historical injustice.

“Prince Audu belonged to multiple eras of Nigeria’s democratic development, from his early public service to his trailblazing leadership as the first and second civilian executive governor.

He must be remembered as a statesman,” they said.

In their resolutions, the stakeholders pledged to unify APC grassroots structures across the nine local government areas of Kogi East behind Tinubu and all APC legislative candidates in the 2027 elections.

They also committed themselves to dialogue with political leaders in Kogi Central and Kogi West, stressing that such engagement must be conducted on mutually acceptable and equitable terms.

The stakeholders further resolved to align with the state government to promote peace, inclusivity and accelerated development across Kogi East.

They called on party leaders, youth leaders, elders and other members of the late Audu’s political family to put past grievances aside and work towards a united political front.

“Our goal is to reintegrate Kogi East into the mainstream of politics in Kogi State and the nation on terms that will assure us of our deserved share of development,” they declared.

World.title: Idris Deserves Second Term, Says Zuru, Urges Voters To Support Gov For Continuity
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent

The Special Adviser to the Kebbi State Governor on Media Strategy and Communication, Abdullahi Zuru, has declared that Governor Nasir Idris has performed credibly well and deserves to be re-elected for a second term in 2027.

Zuru made the declaration yesterday while responding to questions from journalists who paid him a courtesy visit. He said the assessment was based on the governor’s record of delivery across key sectors since assuming office in 2023.

“Since the creation of Kebbi State, we have never had it this good,” Zuru said. “The governor has touched every sector and the impact is visible to the people.”

According to him, the Idris administration has prioritised the economy, infrastructural development, education, health, workers’ welfare, and human capital development. He noted that the interventions were designed to directly improve the lives of ordinary citizens.

On infrastructure, the media aide said the government has embarked on road projects, urban renewal, and rural development programmes aimed at opening up communities and boosting commerce across the 21 local government areas of the state.

“In education and health, we have seen massive investments in schools, primary healthcare centres, and the welfare of teachers and health workers,” he added. “Workers’ salaries are paid as and when due, and their welfare is receiving serious attention.”

Zuru further stated that the governor’s approach to governance has restored public confidence in government. He said the administration runs an open-door policy that allows citizens to feel the presence of government at all levels.

Calling on voters in the state, he urged them to rally behind the governor ahead of the next election. “I encourage the good people of Kebbi State to support Governor Nasir Idris and ensure he returns for a second term so that the good work can continue,” he said.

The Special Adviser also took a swipe at some politicians in the state, saying they lacked the pedigree to challenge the governor’s record.

“Some of them have held positions at state and federal levels before, yet they have no track record to show for it,” Zuru stated. “Leadership is about results, and the results are there for everyone to see.”

He noted that with the current momentum, Kebbi is on the path of sustainable development, and continuity under Governor Idris remains the best option for the people of the state.

World.title: Beyond Interest: The Alternative Bank Charts New Path for Wealth Creation
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Alternative Bank has concluded plans to chart a new course for capital allocation in Nigeria as it hosted investors, policymakers and business leaders in Lagos under the theme, ‘Beyond Interest: Capital, Innovation, and the Future of Wealth’.

The event focused on non-interest finance and the need to deploy patient capital into the country’s productive sectors rather than extractive models that only generate short-term gains.

Opening the forum, Muhtar Bakare, Chairman of The Alternative Bank, said the economy must move away from capital that merely harvests value.

“Extractive capital treats the economy chiefly as a place from which value is harvested. It may reward its owner, but it rarely leaves the economy stronger. Productive capital invests in enterprises, assets and systems that grow over time. It creates income for workers, demand for suppliers, revenue for governments and sustainable returns for investors,” Bakare stated.

Delivering the keynote on behalf of Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, the Commissioner for Finance, Abayomi Oluyomi, said government has a critical role in de-risking investment through infrastructure and credible policy.

He cited the Blue and Red Line rail projects as examples of public investment expanding markets and reducing business costs.

“The future of finance will belong to capital that is more purposeful, innovative and closely connected to productive economic activity.

“The future of development finance will increasingly draw on instruments including green bonds, sukuk and other ethical and non-interest structures that connect capital to real assets, productive activity and measurable outcomes. Investors do not invest in government promises. They invest in credible systems,” he said.

Also speaking, former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Raji Fashola, urged financial institutions to prioritise investments tied to tangible assets and community well-being over those chasing immediate profits, noting that such investments deliver more lasting social and economic returns.
