NEW DELHI: The government said on Saturday that the proposed merchant discount rate (MDR) for UPI transactions will be nominal and apply only to a limited set of merchants for transactions above a threshold, while seeking to assure users that all person-to-person transactions will remain free and consumers who make the payment will not face any fees."A vast majority of the transactions will remain free of charge for merchants on UPI. MDR, if introduced, will only be threshold-based and not levied on a blanket basis to all," the statement said, adding that the UPI and Services Steering Committee, headed by NPCI, will decide on the MDR, if any.It also dismissed reports of the charges being imposed under pressure from the US, which was seen to be pushing the case of Visa and Mastercard that levy MDR on credit card and debit card transactions, which are up to 2%, and usually not passed on to consumers unless the merchant is keen on a cash transaction. "If external pressure had been a factor, the government would not have introduced UPI in 2016 or made it free of charge for both merchants as well as citizens since Jan 2020 and ensured that it became the world's largest real-time interoperable payment system.The amendment should be viewed in the context of the government's broader objective of ensuring that India's digital payment infrastructure remains sustainable, competitive, and capable of serving the country's rapidly expanding digital economy."The finance ministry argued the move was necessary to expand the infrastructure into rural and semi-urban areas. Officials have indicated an MDR of 0.25% to 0.4% may be allowed for UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, provided they are not person-to-person, with a ceiling on the charge.

World.title: Government spending on education below Unesco's 15% standard
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India remains just above Unesco's minimum GDP benchmark for education, but the sector's share in government spending has slipped below the prescribed threshold. Education accounts for 4.1% of GDP but 14.2% of total public expenditure, down from 15.7% in 2015 and below the 15% benchmark, Unesco's 2026 SDG 4 scorecard has shown.

The funding picture assumes significance because India continues to lag on secondary school completion. Its latest lower secondary (Classes VI-VIII) completion rate is 86% as against its 99% national benchmark for 2025, while upper secondary (Classes IX-XII) completion rate is 51% as against 84%. Unesco classifies progress at both levels as slow.

Under the Education 2030 framework, countries committed to spending 4-6% of GDP and/or 15-20% of public expenditure on education.

The scorecard uses the lower thresholds as minimum benchmarks. India meets one. Its spending on education has remained at 4.1% of GDP since 2015, but its share of public expenditure has declined 1.5 percentage points to 14.2%.

Among major emerging economies, China too meets one benchmark, at 4% of GDP (11.9% of public spending), while figures for Brazil are 5.6% and 12.9%. South Africa meets both, at 6% and 19.1%, while Indonesia, Bangladesh and Pakistan meet neither.





The pattern is common among developed economies too: the US, UK, Germany and France meet the GDP threshold but not the public expenditure benchmark, while Sweden and Switzerland meet both.

Unesco noted that richer countries tend to meet the GDP benchmark but not the public expenditure threshold because they raise more revenue, while education often accounts for a larger share of budgets in poorer countries.

Latest data show 39 of 205 countries, or 19%, meeting both benchmarks, while 72, or 35%, meet neither.

Another 64 countries, including India, spend above 4% of GDP but below 15% of public expenditure. Among high-income countries, 11% meet both benchmarks and 50% follow India's pattern.

India, however, has larger unmet schooling needs. Lower secondary completion has risen from 81% in 2015 to 86% but remains 13 percentage points below its 99% benchmark. Even Unesco's "feasible" 2025 benchmark of 90% is four points above the latest rate.

This is despite programmes operating at scale. Unesco's India profile says Samagra Shiksha supports about 15.6 crore learners, while PM-Poshan covers around 11.8 crore children in 11.2 lakh government and aided schools. The trend is part of a broader global concern. The scorecard concludes that, on average, countries are "moving away" from the public education expenditure benchmarks of at least 4% of GDP or 15% of total public expenditure.

World.title: 6 years after NDA exit, Punjab's SAD backs delimitation push
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A day after his meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi,

president

on Saturday reversed his party's earlier opposition to the rollout of the women's reservation law from 2029 with an increase in the Lok Sabha's strength by 50% and supported any fresh move to implement the two together, signalling the possibility of the govt reviving the Constitution amendment bill soon.

Akali Dal had walked out of the BJP-led NDA government in September 2020, ending a 23-year-old alliance, due to the Centre's passage of the three farm bills. DMK, another opponent being eyed by the government as a potential supporter of its renewed bid, snubbed governing TVK's all-party meeting on delimitation. NDA is also banking on NCP(SP) to support the measure.

Government likely to bring back delimitation bill , but timing not clear yet

While Sukhbir Singh Badalâs party has only one MP â his wife Harsimrat is a Lok Sabha member â his announcement conveyed the governmentâs efforts to realign the numbers in its favour this time round, after a similar exercise was defeated in the last session by a joint opposition, which has since been considerably weakened.

While DMK called it a diversionary tactic and wondered why CM Vijay did not summon the meeting on a pressing issue like the Mekedatu dam row, the party clearly did not want to be part of an exercise to frame delimitation as damaging to the interests of the state, with TVK ally Congress up in arms against it.

Developments in governing BJP-led NDA and opposition camps are a clear indication that the government is bringing back the bill, which will need two-thirds support in Parliament.





Its timing, however, remains uncertain, with a section of lawmakers being of the view that Parliament can be summoned after Independence Day to debate it.

The ongoing monsoon session is scheduled to end on Aug 13, leaving the government with not much time to pursue its ambitious agenda that seeks to raise Lok Sabhaâs maximum strength from the existing 550 to 850.

Sukhbir demanded implementation of one-third reservation for women in Lok Sabha and state assemblies.

He said, âSAD also demanded a fair and equitable delimitation.â Incidentally, his wife had made a fiery speech against a similar bill last time, flaying the government for linking reservation for women to delimitation.

The changed political environment and the fact that the government may write into the new bill all the assurances it has made verbally may have persuaded his party and DMK to consider a rethink.

NCP MP Supriya Sule had earlier suggested that if the bill proposes a rise in Lok Sabha seats of every state by an equal proportion, it would not create any problem, though she had added that they will be part of opposition consultations before making a final decision.

World.title: Two memorials of 1962 war heroes figure in 27 places formally named in Arunachal
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Sher-e-Thapa Memorial, set up in memory of 1962 China war hero Havildar Shere Thapa, is one of the 27 places in Arunachal that the Union government on Friday formally named by their standard names on the official Indian map.

Havildar Shere Thapa of the 2nd Battalion, Jammu & Kashmir Rifles, was credited with saving the Subansiri Valley during the 1962 Chinese aggression. He was part of a team to delay the advance of the enemy. On Nov 18, 1962, undaunted by the advance of the Chinese troops, he continued to engage the enemy from his position despite his buddy succumbing to enemy action. The Chinese suffered heavy losses, and their advance was delayed by 72 hours.

The Indian Army installed a memorial in his name.

Another name, Jaswant Garh, which houses the memorial of Indian martyr Rifleman

on Tawang Road, also figured in the list. Located at 10,000 feet on the highway to Tawang, it marks the site where he single-handedly fought Chinese forces for 72 hours during the 1962 war. The memorial has been built in honour of his extraordinary bravery at the Battle of Nuranang.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Jairampur, an important logistics hub in Changlang district which is known as the gateway to the eastern border region supporting movements of security forces towards eastern Arunachal and the Myanmar frontier, also figures in the list.





One of the most strategically important high-altitude passes, Thag La, where one of the opening battles between Indian and Chinese forces took place in 1962, has also been formally identified.

The list also includes Bisa village and strategically important high-altitude mountain passes in the region: Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La.

By formally naming some of the places, famous for the memorials of the Army war heroes, the government is paying homage to bravehearts who laid down their lives fighting for India in the northeastern state.

SRINAGAR: The Forum for Human Rights in J&K has called for full restoration of statehood and repeal of 2019 Reorganisation Act, cautioning that linking statehood to the security situation and terrorist attacks could erode democratic rights in the Union territory.It presented its annual report âSeven Years Under Union Rule â With a Special Section on Ladakh & Pakistan-held Territories of J&K (Aug 2025âJuly 2026)â to National Conference president Farooq Abdullah, PDP president and former J&K CM Mehbooba Mufti, CPMâs MY Tarigami and Congressâs J&K president Tariq Hamid Karra.The forum said arguments that restoration of statehood is ânot appropriateâ because of security concerns and terrorist attacks are dangerous and could be used to undermine peopleâs democratic rights.It also backed statehood for Ladakh and its inclusion in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution.It praised J&K HC for a series of orders quashing detentions under Public Safety Act and granting bail under UAPA and PSA ââ¦but we are constrained to note that its repeated strictures do not appear to have led to course correction by police,â the report said.The forum, an informal group of concerned citizens, is co-chaired by former Union home secretary Gopal Pillai and Radha Kumar, a former member of the group of interlocutors for J&K. World.title: Activists say Tamil Nadu Budget made no mention of child protection schemes
World.content:
The Revised Budget Estimates for 2026-27, unveiled on Wednesday by Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, had no mention of child protection schemes, child rights activists in the State pointed out.

While education and nutrition related schemes involving children saw many announcements from Super Clean Super Campus to anti-drug clubs, modern bicycles, gold ring for babies and special school for children with intellectual disability, child rights activists noted that no announcement regarding child protection were made which involves the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR), Juvenile Justice Boards or the Juvenile Homes.

“The TVK government which was voted into power because of children continues to look at children as beneficiaries and not as stakeholders,” said a child rights activist.

Kalpana Sathish, development consultant and researcher noted that in the past five years of the government almost 53% of the allocation for children welfare was done in education and 23% in nutrition while child protection expenditure is skewed. “There was no systemic reform announcement or concerns addressed in this Budget,” she said.

Child rights activist Andrew Sesuraj said, “There was no announcement regarding children-friendly infrastructure in Juvenile Justice Boards or separate funds for SCPCR. The child protection mechanism has now been forgotten,” said

The Tamil Nadu Child Rights Watch in a statement said that while children are increasingly recognised as future innovators and workers, less attention is devoted to their rights to protection, participation and holistic development.

The next phase of budget reform should therefore move from human capital budgeting towards child rights budgeting, where every investment is assessed by its contribution to children’s survival, development, protection and participation, they added.

Kalpana also said that child protection is emerging as a major issue in Tamil Nadu. “There are rising child sexual abuse cases, child marriage, children eloping, migration and others. These need to be addressed. Right now the State is depending on centralised funds and these are not enough for trickle down efforts to take place. There needs to be radical change seen in investing in children,” she said.

World.title: Four militants arrested in Manipur
World.content:
Four militants of two banned outfits have been arrested in two Imphal Valley districts of Manipur, police said in a statement on Saturday (August 8, 2026).

Also read | NSCN(K) militant arrested in Manipur’s Tamenglong

All the insurgents were arrested on Friday (August 7) for their alleged involvement in extortion.

Two cadres of the banned outfit SOREPA were arrested from the locality of their residence in Kakching Khunou Umathel Awang Leikai in Waikhong police station area in Kakching district, the statement said.

They were identified as 25-year-old Mayanglambam Nimaichand and 27-year-old Mayanglambam Khoiraba.

Another cadre of SOREPA was apprehended from the Checkon area in Imphal East district. He has been identified as Md. Majahar Ali (52).

A 25-year-old cadre of the militant outfit People's Liberation Army (PLA) was apprehended from Seijang Awang in Imphal East district. He has been identified as Pheiroijam Karanjoy Singh.

A hand grenade, an empty INSAS rifle magazine and three empty rifle cartridge cases were seized from his residence.

World.title: Political parties urge govt. to convene all-party meeting on Mekedatu project
World.content:
Leaders of several political parties in Tamil Nadu on Friday urged the State government to convene an all-party meeting on the proposed Mekedatu dam project in Karnataka, saying a united political and legal response was essential to protect the State’s share of Cauvery water.

Speaking at a demonstration organised by Puthiya Tamilagam in Chennai, the leaders accused successive governments in Karnataka of failing to release Tamil Nadu’s due share of Cauvery water in accordance with tribunal and Supreme Court orders.

They contended that the State had often received only surplus water released during periods of heavy rainfall rather than its allocated share.

Naam Tamilar Katchi chief co-ordinator Seeman alleged that Karnataka had repeatedly failed to comply with Cauvery water-sharing orders. He said the State should insist on receiving its legally allocated 177.25 tmcft of water. He alleged that successive governments at the Centre had failed to safeguard Tamil Nadu’s interests and urged the State government to pursue all available political and legal measures to secure the State’s rightful share of Cauvery water.

Puthiya Tamilagam founder K. Krishnasamy said the proposed Mekedatu dam would further reduce flows to Tamil Nadu if constructed. He claimed Karnataka had failed to release the quantity of water due to Tamil Nadu, affecting kuruvai cultivation this season in the Delta districts.

Mr. Krishnasamy also criticised the State government for not initiating stronger legal action to secure the release of water.

Tamilaga Vaazhvurimai Katchi president T. Velmurugan called on political parties in Tamil Nadu to unite on the Mekedatu issue, including during the upcoming byelection.

Representatives of the Pattali Makkal Katchi, Indiya Jananayaga Katchi, and other parties, also participated.

World.title: In Bihar, four new minority residential schools will start academic activities from August
World.content:
The Bihar government on Friday (August 7, 2026) announced that four new minority residential schools will start academic activities from August, taking the total number of such schools to six in the State.

While addressing the press in Patna, Minority Welfare Department Minister Mohammad Zama Khan said the department has given the nod to build new minority residential schools in 24 districts.

“The construction of four new schools at Jamui, Nalanda, Kaimur and Muzaffarpur has been completed, and the academic session is likely to start from August 17,” Mr. Khan said. He added that this will be in addition to the existing two such schools which are already operational at Darbhanga and Kishanganj.

The department has implemented “Bihar State Minority Residential School Scheme” in the State since 2018-19, he said, adding that at least one minority residential school will be opened in each district under the scheme.

A minority residential school provides high-quality residential education from Class 9 to Class 12 for meritorious minority students, besides offering free boarding, lodging, and books, the Minister said.

With a view to improve educational standards of madrasas, especially located in bordering districts of the State, the department is carrying out “online/smart classes” in association with Maulana Mazharul Haque Arabic and Persian University, Patna and Bihar State Madrasa Education Board, Patna, the Minister said.

“We have made arrangements for providing ‘skill development’ to the students of madrasas so that they can get jobs in different fields,” Mr. Khan said, adding that the skill development programme in madrasas will be run in association with National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), a public enterprise under India’s Ministry of MSME.

The madrasa students are being taught subjects like Hindi, English, Social Science, Science and Mathematics to make them competitive in today’s world, he added.

The department has sent the requisition to Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) to fill the 288 posts of teachers to be appointed through TRE 4.0 in ‘residential minority schools’ of the State, Mr. Khan said. He added that the government has approved 481 posts of teaching and non-teaching staffers to operate 13 minority residential schools.

In order to promote entrepreneurship and self-employment among the youth of the minority community in the State, Mukhya Mantri Udyami Yojana (Chief Minister Minority Entrepreneur Scheme) was launched in 2023, Mr. Khan said. Loans amounting to ₹100 crore were disbursed among 1,247 beneficiaries under the scheme in 2025-26. So far, a total of 3,741 beneficiaries have received loans worth Rs 270 crore.

He also said that the Bihar State Haj Committee has been constituted to facilitate and assist Haj pilgrims, and a total of 2,526 pilgrims undertook the Haj pilgrimage through the committee during 2025-26 while the registration process has been completed for a total of 3,637 applicants for the Haj pilgrimage for 2026-27.

World.title: New Colombia President pledges robust fight against crime, fiscal austerity in maiden speech
World.content:
Colombia’s new right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella was sworn in on Friday (August 7, 2026), ‌using his inaugural speech to pledge a vigorous fight against drug trafficking, as well as austerity measures to restore confidence in the economy. Mr. De ​La Espriella, 48, won June’s runoff on promises to crack down on armed groups, shrink the state by as much as 40% ⁠and revive the oil and gas sector. An ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, he represented people with ties to right-wing paramilitaries during his time as a lawyer. Mr. De La Espriella has never before held elected office.

“I have come to close a long chapter of national resignation and, together with the people, embark on the most profound transformation of our destiny,” Mr. De La Espriella ‌said at the Pichincha Battalion military base in Cali, after being sworn in at a nearby university auditorium with dignitaries and officials. “I send a firm message to the Colombian people: the time has come to restore order, authority, and freedom.”

Election part of righward shift of Latin America

“Members of ‌criminal gangs and narco-terrorist groups have two choices: submit to the rule of law or face the determined response of the Colombian state and its ‌security ⁠forces,” the new President told assembled troops at the base during a 75-minute speech, adding the option of peace talks with armed groups had ⁠been “completely exhausted.”

Mr. De La Espriella’s election was part of a rightward shift rippling across Latin America. In Peru, Argentina, Chile, Ecuador, Bolivia and Panama, weak economies and rising crime have reshaped voter priorities, allowing once-fringe hard-right candidates to gain traction by promising crackdowns amid a global rise of right-wing nationalism.

Mr. De La Espriella could push through some of his policies via decree, but analysts say many of his proposals will require backing ​from a divided congress and could be watered down in negotiations. The new ‌President vowed to “definitively eradicate the scourge of illicit crops,” saying he would use aerial herbicides that do not harm human health or the environment to destroy coca, the plant used to make cocaine.

In one of his first acts as President, Colombia will join the Shield of the Americas program founded by Mr. Trump, he said. He pledged to freeze public spending and pursue tax reform to simplify the country’s payment regime and boost investment and employment, while preserving popular social ‌programs, some put in place by his predecessor, leftist Gustavo Petro. “I want to tell Colombia’s business leaders — large, medium-sized and small — that this government ​will be your partner in investing in Colombia. Once again, it will be a safe and profitable decision for you,” Mr. De La Espriella said. He pledged to expand oil and gas exploration, including through “the development of responsible and sustainable fracking”.

“We cannot resign ourselves to having ⁠proven oil reserves that will last only a few more years, nor can we accept the decline of our gas reserves,” he said, adding his government will work to strengthen state-run oil company Ecopetrol. Mr. De La Espriella was the first Colombian president in modern history to be sworn in at a location other than the country’s congressional building in ‌the capital Bogota.

Market-friendly, fiscally constraned

Before the ceremony, he held bilateral meetings with the king of Spain and the Presidents of Argentina, Ecuador, Chile, Paraguay and Panama. Also attending was Gianni Infantino, the embattled head of soccer’s world governing body FIFA, while the U.S. sent a delegation headed by acting Attorney General Todd Blanche. Mr. De La Espriella has blamed Mr. Petro, who has not recognized the new President’s victory, for an expansion of armed groups, and narrowly defeated Petro ally, leftist Senator Ivan Cepeda, in the runoff. Mr. Cepeda led a morning march in Barranquilla on Friday, where he told demonstrators that the country’s opposition will work to defend democracy and called for peaceful civil disobedience.

Investors have welcomed Mr. De La Espriella’s market-friendly agenda, but expectations for rapid change are tempered by fiscal constraints and high public debt. The head of the stock exchange has called for simpler participation ‌by foreign and retail investors, lower transaction costs, eliminating dividend taxes and increasing Ecopetrol’s publicly traded shares to 20%. Oil and mining guilds are optimistic but say changes must come quickly if Colombia ​is to ramp up gas production and meet other pressing needs.

The new administration is likely to focus its first 100 days on steps that Mr. De La Espriella can take directly, consulting firm Colombia Risk Analysis said in a report on Thursday.

“Security and anti-corruption efforts will ⁠likely serve as the most visible pillars of early momentum, though largely through workarounds and partial measures rather than full-scale execution,” the report said. “Markets are likely to respond favorably in the ⁠short term [reflected in peso appreciation], but tax simplification and wealth tax elimination will likely reduce state revenue just as new spending needs emerge, especially if Colombians believe there’s a rollback of benefits from the Petro administration.”

Mr. De La Espriella has leaned heavily on Vice President-elect Jose Manuel Restrepo, a former Finance Minister ‌who traveled to Washington to meet with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Other cabinet picks include Omar Bula, a former World Food Program official turned United Nations critic, as Foreign Minister; retired Major General Jorge Eduardo Mora as Defense Minister; electrical engineer Maria Arboleda as Energy Minister; and Miguel Gomez as finance minister. Mr. Gomez has ​said the fiscal deficit stands at 7% to 8% of GDP, above outgoing government figures, and that the new administration will present a growth-focused tax reform.

World.title: Biren Singh’s audio clip altered, says Centre; SC allows Manipur civil society group to access report
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (August 7, 2026) directed the Union government to share the latest report by the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) with the petitioner-NGO Kuki Organisation for Human Rights in a case seeking probe into the alleged involvement of former Manipur Chief Minister N. Biren Singh in the ethnic violence in the northeastern State.

According to the report, the leaked audio clips alluding to Mr. Singh have been “clearly manipulated”.

Appearing before a Bench headed by Justice Sanjay Kumar, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, representing both the Centre and the State of Manipur, said even the first-generation copy of the audio clippings outed by a whistleblower showed alterations.

Ms. Bhati asked the top court to dismiss the petition.

Advocate Prashant Bhushan, representing the NGO-petitioner, strongly objected to the report, saying tests of the audio clippings done at Truth Labs had shown a 93% match with Mr. Singh’s voice. Agreeing to keep the report confidential, Mr. Bhushan said he would nevertheless counter its findings in court on the next date of hearing.

Select clippings

The court, in an earlier hearing, had asked the petitioner-NGO to hand over to the national forensics lab a ‘first generation copy’ of the full audio tapes.

On December 15 last year, the court had questioned why the entire available leaked audio clips were not sent for forensic examination. The court had conveyed its unease at the affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioners on November 20, 2025, that stated that “only select clippings were sent” for forensics.

The petitioner has sought an independent SIT probe into the matter.

More than 260 people were killed and thousands displaced since the ethnic violence broke out between the Imphal valley-based Meitei and neighbouring hills-based Kuki communities in May 2023.

The court listed the case next for hearing on October 5.

World.title: Cannons in Adoor Mahalingeswara temple stand guard over centuries of history
World.content:
At the ancient Adoor Mahalingeswara temple in Kasaragod district, every visit offers a journey into history. Alongside its deity, centuries-old inscriptions, and unique architecture, two old cannons preserved in the temple courtyard stand as a silent reminder of a turbulent past, adding another layer to the temple’s rich historical legacy.

The temple, located in Delampady Gram Panchayat, is already renowned for its 10th-century origins, its three-tiered Gajaprishta (elephant-back) style architecture, the famous Adoor inscription, an intricately carved Balikkal (sacrificial stone), and the Sathyakallu (oath stone). The presence of the historically significant cannons has further enhanced the site’s archaeological importance.

The cannons drew scholarly attention when Nandakumar Koroth, Head of the Department of History at Nehru Arts and Science College, Kanhangad, visited the temple to study the Adoor inscription.

According Dr. Koroth, both are made of an alloy that may date to the 18th century or even earlier. One cannon measures 96 centimetre in length, including its handle for directional movement, while the second is 90 centimetre long. Each has side trunnions designed for mounting on wheeled carriages, while a small opening on the top was used for loading gunpowder.

“The comparatively small size of the cannons suggests that they were probably mounted on wheels and used as mobile field artillery during military campaigns,” Dr. Koroth said.

He noted that the cannons bear no visible foreign insignia, manufacturer’s mark, or date of production. The absence of European markings indicates they may have been locally manufactured and probably predate British rule in South Canara, which was established around 1800, he said.

The origin of the cannons, however, remain a mystery. No inscription or historical record directly links them to any ruler or military campaign.

Temple renovation committee volunteer Balakrishnan Adoor said local tradition associates the cannons with the military expedition of Tipu Sultan in the late 18th century.

“According to oral tradition, Tipu Sultan reached the temple during one of his campaigns against local rulers. He is believed to have intended to plunder the temple after defeating a regional chieftain and expanding his kingdom,” Mr. Balakrishnan said.

There are no written records to authenticate the legend or establish that the cannons belonged to Tipu Sultan. They are believed to have been abandoned here during that period, but there is no evidence to prove it, he said.

Mr. Balakrishnan said the heavy cannons were originally found elsewhere within the temple compound and were later shifted to their present location for protection. Local residents also recall that large iron balls, believed to be cannonballs, were unearthed during excavation works around the nearby temple and school premises several years ago.

Kannada scholar and historian N. Radhakrishna, who has studied the temple’s inscriptions, said the temple’s epigraphs document donations made by rulers of the Kumbla dynasty, including Kattillamma and King Gunyappa Rasa, particularly to the temple’s sacrificial stones.

“The inscriptions are well documented, but there is no inscription or historical record explaining how the cannons reached the temple. We only know that they are old,” he said.

Mr. Radhakrishna said the temple itself dates back to the 10th century, while some inscriptions belong to the 17th or 18th century, probably marking later renovations.

“There is no documentary evidence linking these cannons to Tipu Sultan or any particular battle. Similar traditions exist in other temples, but historical proof is absent,” he said.

World.title: Kabini dam: Fresh flood alert issued as rains intensify in Kerala
World.content:
Inflow into the Kabini dam in Mysuru district has gone up yet again as incessant rains lashed its catchment areas in Kerala. The dam authorities have once again issued a flood warning urging people living in the downstream stretches of the Kapila to remain alert following increase in the discharge of water from the dam.

The outflow from the dam was 7,000 cusecs on Friday morning while the inflow was 11,217 cusecs. As the inflow into the dam went up, owing to a fresh spell of rains in Wayanad and nearby areas in the neighbouring State, about 10,000 to 15,000 cusecs of water were being discharged into the river, prompting the issue of a renewed flood warning.

Executive Engineer of the Kabini Reservoir Division, H.D. Kote, in a flood warning note on Friday, said there is a possibility of further increase in the outflow from the dam considering the dam’s safety, following significant increase in the inflow into the dam. Therefore, people on the banks of the Kapila have been cautioned to shift to safer places and safeguard their properties and livestock as the river levels will rise.

D.B. Kuppe in H.D. Kote taluk recorded the day’s highest rain of 11.5 mm in Mysuru district.

Meanwhile, fresh spell of rain in Kodagu increased inflow into the Harangi dam near Kushalnagar. The inflow was 8,940 cusecs while the outflow to the Cauvery was 8,000 cusecs. The reservoir level stood at 2,858.14 ft. as against the maximum of 2,859 ft. on Friday.

After a brief lull, rainfall activity in Kodagu has picked up, with the district recording 24.36 mm rain in the last 24 hours ending at 8.30 a.m. on Friday. On this day last year, Kodagu recorded just 1.46 mm rain. Bhagamandala recorded 43.20 mm rain, while the highest rain was recorded at Sampaje which was 72.50 mm.

As rainfall had earlier receded in Kodagu, the inflow into the Krishnaraja Sagar had dropped. The inflow on Friday was 7,477 cusecs and the reservoir level stood at 106.37 ft. on Friday.

World.title: Initial findings of second post-mortem show multiple injuries on Mir Raza Ali, police surgeon says
World.content:
The initial findings of the second post-mortem examination of 25-year-old business owner Mir Raza Ali revealed multiple injuries and a congealed black substance in his mouth and throat, Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed said on Saturday.

Raza, owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

His body was exhumed earlier today after the Sindh government restored the original medical board.

Dr Summaiya told Dawn that Raza had multiple injuries to his head and face, including fractures to his nasal bone and skull. She said there were also injuries to his right flank and feet.

The police surgeon added that a congealed black substance was found in Raza’s mouth and throat.

Regarding the bullet wound, she said there was a fractured rib in the back, which was the entry point of the gunshot, while the bullet exited through the front.

She further said that DNA samples had been collected and sent to a laboratory, along with samples for chemical analysis and gunshot residue testing.

The cause of death, she added, would remain reserved until the laboratory reports were received.

‘Tortured and murdered’

Advocate Jibran Nasir, representing the family of the 25-year-old, alleged on Saturday evening that Raza had been tortured before being murdered, hours after his second post-mortem was conducted, and demanded that the entire investigation team be replaced.

Speaking to the media in the evening, Nasir said the initial report of the second post-mortem answered “14 questions” and detailed some of the alleged injuries Raza had sustained before his death.

“This was murder following torture — the murder of a happy, ambitious and educated young man from Karachi,” he alleged.

“He had an injury on his chin,” the advocate said, adding that Raza’s eye sockets were compressed and that traces of a foreign substance were found.

“Samples were taken and sent to a lab to see if there are any chemical traces,” he told reporters.

The lawyer also claimed that Raza had wounds to his forehead and a fractured nose, as well as swelling and congealed blood around his lower jaw, consistent with having been punched.

“There is a fracture to his temple above his ear, indicating he was struck,” he alleged.

“In the tongue area, a congealed black substance was discovered, which is not naturally found in the body. This substance has been taken and sent to a lab to see what he was forced to ingest.”

Continuing the description, he also claimed that internal muscles in Raza’s throat were covered in the same black substance, and that a broken hyoid bone and muscle damage suggested that he also was strangled.

“Now we come to the firearm injury, where it was earlier said that he was shot in the chest and the bullet exited through his back,” Nasir said.

“We have now proven 110 per cent that the bullet entered his back and exited after breaking and fracturing his ribs.”

The family’s lawyer also criticised senior police officials, alleging that they “do not want to investigate, but rather humiliate, harass and exhaust the family”.

“They are finding months-old recordings and frustrating, emotionally exhausting and humiliating Mir Hussain and Maryam Hussain. Are you investigating or harassing them? They sat them in their offices and told them repeatedly, ‘It’s a suicide, accept it’. Our city’s AIG was saying this,” the advocate claimed further.

Nasir added that he and the family had “no faith” in the AIG or the SSP’s investigation team and that they wanted the entire team changed, including senior officers.

“If they appoint the same kind of officers, such as those doctors from Jamshoro and Hyderabad, then we will approach the court,” he added.

“But have no doubts about it: senior officers spent 10 days with the parents and misguided them into believing it was a suicide,” Nasir alleged.

Raza’s father, Mir Hussain, told reporters that he had maintained since July 30 that his son’s death was a brutal murder.

“We saw the body and told them [that it was murder], but they kept saying, ‘Suicide, suicide, suicide,’” he said. “Sometimes the SSP would talk to us; the IG would say that the matter had been resolved but there was a problem in the report.

“If your entire police station investigates based on post-mortem reports, then how can someone in such a position of responsibility say something like this?”

Mir Hussain said it “brought us peace” to learn that their claims that Raza had been attacked before his death were true.

“We have said it was murder from the start,” he added. “Why are they hiding the killers?”

Speaking to the media earlier today, Nasir said the investigation officer was present when the body was exhumed and examined, while all eight members of the medical team were also present. The deceased’s parents were nearby and, “most importantly”, a judicial magistrate was present as well.

The lawyer also contended that “incomplete CCTV footage and out-of-context messages” had been used to fuel rumours and draw hasty conclusions since Raza’s death.

While his family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, investigators probing the incident continue to build their case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

Commenting on the medical board controversy, Nasir expressed concern that the government did not provide any reason for changing the medical board overnight on Friday.

The lawyer said the victim’s family did not need “character certificates” for the doctors on the medical board.

He expressed hope that the medical board’s report would be received by Saturday evening, which would help clarify the circumstances of the young businessman’s death.

The report would clearly indicate if the incident was a murder or suicide, Nasir said, adding that the “police will be under even more pressure” once that question was cleared up.

He reiterated that the report would answer the question of whether it was “self-inflicted or a murder”.

Nasir further said he was surprised to know that the police had shared audio evidence with the media before revealing it to the parents of the victim, who found out about it from TV reports.

Nasir expressed gratitude to the judiciary for intervening in the case, adding that “the work that police could not do in eight to nine days was done in two days after judicial intervention”.

Separately, a PPP delegation comprising MPAs Asif Moosa and Saima Agha visited Raza’s family to convey their condolences.

Moosa assured the bereaved family that Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar and Sindh Inspector General Javed Alam Odho were monitoring the case.

He affirmed that efforts were being made for a transparent inquiry so that justice can be served.

Saima said the probe will be taken forward once the post-mortem report is compiled, asserting that the culprits will be punished. She further said the PPP stood with the victim’s family.

Medical board controversy

The exhumation, which was scheduled for Friday morning, was postponed after the deceased’s family objected to the abrupt reconstitution of the medical board and inclusion of members from outside Karachi division.

On Thursday, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Raza’s father, Mir Hussain Ali, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation.

The court ruling came after a controversy emerged between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding the post-mortem examination.

Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself, said some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. Prof Dr Naseem Ahmed of Dow University of Health Sciences, Dr Farah Waseem of Jinnah Sindh Medical University, Amir Hassan Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza of Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, and Dr Mohammed Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon office, were the other members of the board.

However, in the early hours of Friday, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan.

On Friday morning, Raza’s family was present at the Tariq Road graveyard for the exhumation, which was then deferred.

Standing alongside Raza’s father, Nasir had accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts and held the police, health department and the Sindh government responsible for the delay.

World.title: Voting on remaining AJK Poonch division seats may be held by Aug 20-21, says CEC
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal said on Saturday that the Election Commission had decided, for security reasons, to first complete the electoral process in four constituencies of Bagh and Haveli districts and hinted that polls in the remaining seven constituencies of Poonch division could be held by Aug 20 or 21.

Talking to a group of journalists at his office, he said the commission would be in a position to announce the election date for Poonch and Sudhnoti within the next seven days, adding that voters in the two districts would have to be given time to campaign.

Poonch division, comprising 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti districts — has a total of 1,154,626 registered voters.

Monday’s polling, however, will be held in four constituencies in Bagh and Haveli, where 460,371 voters — 238,664 men and 221,707 women — are eligible to cast their ballots at 803 polling stations with 1,254 polling booths.

A total of 82 candidates are in the fray, with the highest number of 30 contesting LA-14 (Central Bagh) and the lowest, nine, in LA-17 (Haveli). The contestants include one sitting prime minister, two former prime ministers, one sitting minister, three former ministers and one sitting member of the AJK Council.

“I appeal to the people of Bagh and Haveli to complete the process of change through their votes,” Justice Mughal said, adding that voting was “not only their democratic right but also a religious obligation, as it is their responsibility to ensure that the trust reaches its rightful recipient”.

He said security personnel had already reached Bagh and Haveli, while transportation of polling material was under way under the supervision of the army.

Asked about the oath-taking of successful candidates, the chief election commissioner said there was no constitutional impediment to them taking the oath.

“However, there are moral grounds for withholding the oath until the House becomes complete following the completion of the electoral process in Poonch and Sudhnoti districts.”

“Once the House is complete, elections will be held for the reserved seats, followed by elections for the speaker, deputy speaker and leader of the House,” he added.

Justice Mughal said eight security personnel would be deployed at each polling station identified as highly sensitive from a security perspective.

“The security personnel who had been deployed in Muzaffarabad have now been moved to Bagh and Haveli,” he said.

He added that the Election Commission would try to have internet services restored in Bagh and Haveli on Aug 9 and 10 to facilitate the compilation and transmission of election results.

On allegations of rigging levelled by political leaders, the CEC said the Election Commission had limitations in responding to such claims.

“The Election Commission has its own limitations. Political leaders’ allegations cannot be answered through statements or political rhetoric,” he said.

“Once the elections are completed, we will bring the facts before the public — whether rigging took place and, if so, who was responsible for it,” he added.

Explaining the procedure for compiling results, Justice Mughal said: “The Returning Officer compiles the result, while counting is conducted beforehand in the presence of the polling agents of the candidates.”

Earlier today, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said that the PML-N would form the government in AJK with a two-thirds majority.

World.title: JI announces Aug 16 sit-ins in provincial capitals to protest petroleum levy
World.content:
LAHORE: Jamaat-i-Islami Pakistan (JI) has decided to intensify its campaign against the petroleum levy and inflation, announcing simultaneous sit-ins in all four provincial capitals on August 16 to press the government to withdraw the levy.

The decision was taken after extensive deliberations at a special meeting of JI’s central and provincial office-bearers, chaired by party chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman at Mansoora on Saturday.

Rehman said the sit-ins would be staged outside the Punjab chief minister’s house in Lahore and the governor houses in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh and Balochistan.

Under the plan, the JI and its youth and women’s wings will participate in Independence Day activities on August 14, using the occasion to mobilise people around the party’s vision of a just system.

The JI chief added that the previous day’s nationwide protest had given the party’s campaign against the petroleum levy and inflation a new direction and fresh momentum; and that over 510 organised and peaceful protests were held across the country, with people from across Pakistan participating.

He said the protests had demonstrated that the JI was “becoming a symbol of national unity”, as people from Chitral, Malakand, Hazara and central Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, among others, had raised their voices against the petroleum levy.

The JI chief added that the public had rejected the levy and wanted petrol prices reduced to Rs225 per litre. Rehman accused the ruling elite of pushing ordinary citizens into an unbearable inflationary crisis while refusing to cut their own privileges and expenditures.

The party chief also claimed the rulers were “unwilling to give up official aircraft, reduce government vehicle expenses or end perks such as free fuel and electricity”, while students, motorcyclists, workers and farmers were being burdened with indirect taxes on petroleum products.

“Even people whose incomes were below the taxable threshold were effectively being taxed through fuel prices,” he added.

Rehman said the JI had previously taken to the streets to force the government to negotiate with independent power producers (IPP), after initially refusing to engage with them.

He added that negotiations had been held with 17 to 18 IPPs, resulting in some reduction in electricity prices, but the process was subsequently halted.

“The unresolved energy crisis and rising prices have fuelled an inflationary storm that is affecting every segment of society, particularly salaried people, the middle class and poor families,” Rehman said.

He warned that the public could no longer be left to suffer the consequences of government policies and said the rulers would have to deliver their rights.

Rehman also welcomed the recently signed defence agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, describing it as “a positive development for the Muslim world”.

He said closer cooperation among Islamic countries could lead to a strong bloc and reduce Pakistan’s and the wider Muslim world’s dependence on external powers.

Additionally, he proposed expanding the defence cooperation to include Iran, Qatar, Bangladesh, Malaysia and Indonesia, saying efforts should gradually be made to bring all Muslim countries into such a framework.

“Muslim countries should overcome their differences, strengthen mutual cooperation and build collective capacity to face regional and global challenges,” Rehman emphasised.

A day prior, several major thoroughfares in Karachi were blocked or affected by traffic disruptions as the JI held sit-ins as part of the nationwide demonstration against the petroleum levy.

Responding to the protest, Sindh government spokesperson Sadia Javed said the petroleum levy was a federal matter and questioned why Karachi’s citizens were being “punished” through road closures.

“Jamaat-i-Islami is using the protest to score political points instead of serving the public,” she alleged, adding that the party should focus on the performance of its local government representatives to improve conditions for Karachi’s residents.

World.title: Pakistan, New Zealand seek to boost cooperation in agri, education sectors
World.content:
Pakistan and New Zealand discussed boosting cooperation in various fields, with a special focus on agriculture and education, as the two sides held a Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meeting in Wellington, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday.

The third Pakistan-New Zealand JTC meeting and the fifth round of Pakistan-New Zealand Political Consultations were held in Wellington on Thursday, “marking a significant step in deepening bilateral engagement between the two countries”, the FO said.

A key outcome of the meetings was the signing of the Education Cooperation Arrangement between Pakistan and New Zealand, which is “expected to significantly deepen collaboration in the education sector”.

At the JTC meeting, both sides “deliberated on improving market access and enhancing cooperation in sustainable agriculture, including exploring technical collaboration in wool production and plant protection”, the FO said.

The discussions focused on bolstering bilateral trade and investment, with particular emphasis on technology, education and services.

Institutional mechanisms to further economic cooperation were also discussed, the statement added.

Commerce Secretary Jawad Paul Khawaja represented Pakistan during the JTC meeting, while Grahame Morton, deputy secretary of the Americas and Asia Group at New Zealand’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, headed the other delegation.

Meanwhile, during the political consultations, both sides conducted a comprehensive review of bilateral relations. They also exchanged views on regional and international developments, and agreed to enhance coordination within multilateral forums.

Additional Foreign Secretary (Asia Pacific) Ambassador Dr Syed Ali Asad Gillani co-chaired the Pakistani side at the political consultations, while Morton headed the New Zealand delegation.

Islamabad and Wellington “explored avenues to strengthen cooperation across a wide spectrum of areas of mutual interest, including high-level exchanges, economic development, science and technology, education, counterterrorism, transnational crime, and people-to-people ties”, the FO said.

Ambassador Gillani briefed the New Zealand side on Pakistan’s efforts to de-escalate tensions in the Middle East, as Islamabad remains actively engaged in efforts to defuse the Strait of Hormuz stand-off.

Morton “acknowledged Pakistan’s constructive role in the Middle East peace process”, the FO statement said.

Gillani also discussed the situation in South Asia, including in India-occupied Kashmir (IoK) and India’s “continued violations” of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT).

India had unilaterally decided to put the IWT in abeyance in late April 2025 after hostilities flared up between the two neighbours last year. The issue of water has remained a bitter point of contention between the nuclear-armed nations since then, with Islamabad repeatedly raising the issue on international platforms.

The overall discussions between Pakistan and New Zealand “provided an opportunity to assess progress in bilateral ties, identify new areas for partnership, and reaffirm the shared commitment to a forward-looking and mutually beneficial relationship”, the FO noted.

Pakistan and New Zealand enjoy cordial and friendly relations, with both countries being members of the Commonwealth.

Bilateral trade stands at $12 million, with Pakistan’s major exports being textile products, apparel, rice, leather articles and sports goods, according to the FO’s website.

Main imports from New Zealand include dairy products, wood pulp, paper, edible oil, wood, iron steel and electrical machinery.

Agriculture and education were also among areas of cooperation discussed between the two sides when former military dictator Gen Pervez Musharraf visited Auckland in June 2005.

Last month, India and New Zealand signed a free trade deal as they sought to boost exports amid global economic uncertainty made worse by the war in the Middle East.

World.title: Rana Sanaullah says PML-N will form govt in AJK with two-thirds majority
World.content:
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Saturday that the PML-N would form the government in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) with a two-thirds majority.

He made the remarks while addressing a rally in Bagh ahead of the third phase of elections in the region. The third phase was originally slated to be held in the 11 constituencies of Poonch division, but will now only be held in its Bagh and Haveli districts due to law and order concerns.

Addressing the rally, Sanaullah said that in the first two phases, the PML-N had secured 24 seats. He said that six more seats were required for a two-thirds majority government.

Expressing confidence that the public will vote for his PML-N, the minister asserted that four more seats would be added following the August 10 polls, while five more would be added when polls would be held in the rest of Poonch Division.

“The PML-N will form a government with a two-thirds majority. The people of Kashmir have trusted PML-N. They have trusted Mian Nawaz Sharif. They have trusted the development in Punjab,” he said.

He urged supporters to show up and cast their votes on Monday to help PML-N secure a victory, promising that a PML-N government would prioritise development projects.

He also said that once in power, the PML-N government would meet with members of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

“When this government will be set up, with a two-thirds majority, they will sit with [JAAC] representatives. Their first task will be to resolve this issue.”

He said that 99 per cent of JAAC protesters were “our brothers”, adding that they were patriotic Kashmiris and Pakistanis.

He added that the remainder were focused on creating divisions within the nation.

Sanaullah said India was trying to create misunderstandings between Pakistan and Kashmiris after failing to achieve its objectives through direct confrontation, adding that such attempts would never succeed.

He urged cooperation between a future PML-N government and the people of AJK in “exposing and defeating” those divisive elements.

“We will defeat them and we will make Kashmir prosperous,” Sanaullah said.

He further added that in the past, all large-scale development projects in AJK were only completed when the PML-N was in power in the Centre and in the region.

He urged the people of Bagh to go out and vote on Monday, stressing that “all of Bagh should be involved in the government”.

He added that PML-N founder Nawaz Sharif would fulfil his promises to the people of AJK by nominating one of the three PML-N candidates in Bagh as the future prime minister of AJK.

Sanaullah added that Nawaz has already mentioned that he would sit down with the future AJK prime minister to discuss development projects in the region.

Highlighting federal support, Sanaullah said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s government had approved a Rs23 billion special package for AJK in 2024 and provided wheat subsidy to facilitate the people.

He said the prime minister had also approved five Daanish Schools for AJK, while PML-N intended to take forward the public welfare and development model being pursued in Punjab.

World.title: Hamas says still ready to go ahead with Gaza plan
World.content:
Hamas said on Saturday it remained ready to proceed with a US-backed Gaza peace plan and urged pressure on Israel, which insists it did not agree to the latest part of the deal.

Hamas informed US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace that it stood by the latest stage of the plan, under which the group would hand over weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing committee in the war-battered territory.

“Hamas and other factions have confirmed to mediators their readiness to begin implementing the agreement and move to the second phase, provided it receives Israeli approval and that Israel begins implementing the agreement,” a Hamas official told AFP.

“Hamas is urging the US administration to exert pressure on Israel to compel it to abide by the agreement and move to the second phase,” the official said on condition of anonymity.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces a tough reelection fight in October and wide opposition from his right-wing base to the Gaza deal, said on Tuesday that Israel had not agreed to the “draft” presented by the Board of Peace.

Trump last week hailed as a breakthrough that Hamas had agreed to disarmament under the plan, with the Board of Peace saying Israel would in tandem carry out a phased withdrawal from much of Gaza.

Netanyahu met Monday with the Board of Peace’s high representative for Gaza, Nickolay Mladenov, who backtracked and said Israel would withdraw only after a full disarmament by Hamas.

Israel’s military also vowed to keep hitting the Palestinian group.

But Israeli attacks in Gaza, while ongoing, appear to have decreased in intensity in recent days. On Saturday, the Nasser hospital in Khan Yunis reported three people injured by Israeli army gunfire.

Israel has killed 1,257 Palestinians since October last year, when the two sides agreed to a ceasefire backed by Trump, according to the Palestinian health ministry.

The Israeli army has reported five deaths in its ranks during the same period.

World.title: Heavy rain disrupts traffic, daily life in Lahore’s low-lying areas
World.content:
LAHORE: Heavy rain lashed Lahore on Saturday, inundating low-lying areas, major roads and several underpasses, making movement difficult for pedestrians and motorists in different parts of the city.

The downpour disrupted normal traffic as rainwater accumulated on roads and in low-lying localities, leaving motorists struggling to navigate waterlogged stretches.

Pedestrians also struggled to move through streets and roads where water had accumulated.

According to rainfall data from the Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa), the city received an average of 24.6mm of rain.

The highest rainfall of 104mm was recorded at the airport, followed by 75.6mm at Kahna, 62.6mm at Hadiara Defence Road and 58.6mm at Manawan.

Tajpura sub-divisional officer’s (SDO) office recorded 40.2mm of rain, while 32.8mm was recorded at the Mughalpura SDO office.

Shadipura received 28.4mm, Nishter Town 28mm, Chowk Nakhuda 11mm, Johar Town SDO Office 11mm, while 10.8mm was recorded at the Wasa head office in Gulberg.

Upper Mall received 9mm, Samanabad SDO Office 4.4mm, Iqbal Town SDO Office 3.8mm, Saggian 3.8mm, Lakshmi Chowk 3.2mm, Jail Road 2mm, Gulshan-e-Ravi 1.8mm and Farrukhabad 1.4mm, while only trace rainfall was recorded at Pani Wala Talab.

Rain was also reported in Farrukhabad, Tajpura, Defence Phase-VI, Shadipura, Saggian, Lakshmi Chowk, Chowk Nakhuda and surrounding areas. Harbanspura and several other localities received heavy showers.

The rain brought relief from the heat and made the weather pleasant, but waterlogging in several areas caused inconvenience to residents and exposed the vulnerability of low-lying localities to heavy rainfall.

Meanwhile, Wasa Lahore said it had deployed field staff and machinery at various locations to drain accumulated rainwater.

Wasa Managing Director Ghufran Ahmed inspected drainage operations at Mubeen Shaheed Underpass, Noor Jehan Road, MM Alam Road, Main Boulevard Gulberg, Qaddafi Stadium and Liberty Chowk.

He also visited Kalma Chowk Underpass, Garden Town Water Tank, Usman Block Emergency Relief Camp and Usman Block Disposal Station.

Officials said drainage operations were continuing at waterlogged locations, with heavy machinery deployed in low-lying areas. Disposal stations in areas experiencing power outages were being operated on generators.

Wasa Vice Chairman Chaudhry Shehbaz Ahmed also inspected drainage operations at Shalimar Link Road, Bhagwanpura, Baghichi Sethan, UET, Ek Moriya, Do Moriya and Chowk Na Khuda.

Earlier, Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Abdul Rahim Shirazi directed supervisory officers to remain in the field and monitor low-lying points and traffic conditions during the rainfall.

Traffic officials were directed to coordinate with Wasa for the timely drainage of rainwater from waterlogged locations.

Traffic police advised motorists to drive at moderate speeds, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles and avoid sudden braking on slippery roads. Motorcyclists were advised to wear helmets and avoid unnecessary overtaking.

Citizens were also advised to assess the depth of accumulated water before entering flooded roads and avoid crossing stretches where water levels were unsafe.

The traffic police warned citizens against standing near electric poles, transformers, fallen power lines, trees, weak walls and under-construction structures during rainfall.

World.title: Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan's Okinawa, China shuts ports ahead of landfall
World.content:
Typhoon Dolphin lashed Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture on Saturday, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings, while China shut ports and halted ferries ahead of the storm’s expected arrival on its east coast.

Five elderly people, three of whom fell due to strong winds, suffered non-life-threatening injuries in Okinawa while another person was injured in Kagoshima prefecture, authorities said.

Nearly 39,000 buildings were without power in Kagoshima while just over 12,000 were affected in Okinawa. Domestic airlines, ANA and Japan Airlines, cancelled flights to and from Okinawa.

The typhoon had maximum sustained winds of 162 kilometres per hour with gusts reaching 216 kph. Okinawa and Amami Island in Kagoshima prefecture are the main areas expected to be affected in Japan.

Typhoon expected to make landfall in China

In China, where the typhoon is expected to make landfall between late on Sunday and early on Monday, authorities have designated Dolphin as an orange-category typhoon, the second-highest level.

Worried about the risk of flooding and landslides, authorities also raised the emergency response level for Dolphin by one notch to level III, the second-lowest level.

The typhoon is most likely to make landfall between Zhoushan city in Zhejiang province and Fuding city in Fujian province and is expected to have winds of 38-45 metres per second near its centre, according to China’s National Meteorological Centre.

Cars drive along a street during heavy rain in Beijing, China on August 7, 2026. — Reuters

China’s National Marine Forecasting Centre on Saturday maintained its highest, red-level warning for waves, forecasting 5-to-8-metre (16-to-26-foot) waves in coastal waters off Zhejiang through Sunday afternoon.

Under an orange-level warning, waves in coastal waters off Shanghai and northern Fujian could be 3 to 5.5 metres.

On Saturday evening, Chinese authorities issued five weather and disaster warnings, including orange alerts for typhoon, heavy rain, and geological-disaster risks, along with a red alert for mountain torrents.

Ports and airports halt operations

Rain and strong winds are expected to affect eastern China through August 12, including parts of Shanghai and neighbouring provinces. Some areas could see short bursts of rainfall exceeding 80mm an hour, accompanied by thunderstorms and strong winds.

Zhejiang, one of China’s biggest provincial economies and a manufacturing and export hub, raised its coastal typhoon alert to its highest level and halted port operations. Authorities in eastern and southern China also suspended ferries, halted some construction work and ordered fishing boats back to port.

Ningbo Lishe International Airport in Zhejiang said it will suspend all flights on Sunday. Shanghai’s Yangshan port had been cleared of vessels by late on Friday, while some rail services in the Yangtze River Delta will be suspended from Sunday.

Beijing authorities have said they are monitoring the typhoon’s path and are preparing flood-control and evacuation plans for the capital.

In Taiwan, 78 flights, mostly international, were cancelled because of the typhoon, the government said. Heavy rain was expected in northern parts of the island over the weekend, though authorities had not ordered evacuations as of Saturday.

China has ordered that, due to the typhoon, ships passing through the Taiwan Strait must heed its traffic control instruction measures that Taipei denounced as “ridiculous”, saying that Beijing has no right to restrict access to international waters.

China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory and claims the strategic strait. Both Taipei and Washington reject that claim.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.
